item.description: John Baloy is a Johannesburg-based photographer and visual artist, born and raised in the township of Evaton West, South of Johannesburg. From a young age, Baloy had a deep passion for the arts, particularly in drawing and sketching. His interest was further ignited in high school when he studied visual arts, solidifying his desire to pursue a career centered around creativity. Though he didn't have the opportunity to study art formally after high school, he begun working as a graphic designer before transitioning into the mining industry as an Automotive Electrician, a role he held for four years.In 2013, inspired by Instagram accounts like Iseeadifferentyou, Rog Walker, Street Etiquette, and Andile Buka, Baloy's interest in photography grew. His exposure to their work led him to buy his first camera, and photography quickly became a consuming passion. Realizing that weekend shooting wasn't enough, he decided to pursue photography full-time, quitting his job in 2017 to become a freelance photographer.Since then, Baloy's career has flourished. He has collaborated with notable brands such as Bombay Sapphire, Adobe, Adidas, Markham, Mr Price, and Bisquit Cognac. His work has been featured in prestigious publications, including DESTINY magazine, and he has exhibited his photography internationally at the AKAA Art Fair in France and the Abantu Exhibition with Dyman Gallery in 2019.Baloy’s photography documents the unique experiences of Black people through a surreal, Afrocentric lens. His work seeks to portray people of color as living works of art, challenging conventional narratives and encouraging subjects to view themselves with pride and reverence. His themes evoke alternative perspectives, aiming to educate and inspire self-reflection and empowerment.

item.title: John Kramer
item.description: John Kramer is a South African artist whose oil paintings capture the essence of the small town in the Western Cape, Karoo and beyond. Born in Worcester, Cape Province, in 1946, Kramer developed a deep appreciation for the region's unassuming houses, quirky shop-fronts, and nostalgic corner cafes. His artistic journey began in the early 1970s when he started photographing these structures, fearing their eventual disappearance. These images became the foundation for his realistic oil and acrylic paintings, which have since become highly regarded and collected world wide.Kramer received formal art education at the Hugo Naude Art Centre in Worcester and later pursued a Diploma in Fine Art at the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town, majoring in painting. He is a winner of the Michaelis prize. In 1969 he joined the Van Zijl and Robinson advertising agency, as a junior finished artist, learning a new set of skills. In 1970 he joined the South African Museum as a designer, working on a diverse number of exhibitions ranging from Wonders of Nature to the Whale Well, ultimately rising to the position of Head of Exhibitions. In April 2002 he took early retirement from the Iziko Museums to pursue a full time painting career.Currently residing in the Gardens suburb, Cape Town, he continues to captivate audiences with his solo exhibitions, showcasing his realistic paintings that capture the essence of the South African small town. A theme that he has pursued for over fifty years. Throughout his career, Kramer has participated in numerous group exhibitions, leaving an indelible mark on the South African art scene. His work has been featured in prestigious events such as the Cape Town Biennial, Cape Town Triennial, and various exhibitions at renowned galleries like the South African National Gallery. He has had work shown in the Netherlands and Belgium. His work is in a number of private and public collections.John Kramer's realistic paintings transport viewers to a bygone era, preserving the essence of small-town life in South Africa. With his meticulous attention to detail and unwavering passion for his craft, Kramer continues to make a significant contribution to the South African art landscape.

item.title: John Moore
item.description: John Mark Moore (b. 1972, Johannesburg) is an acclaimed South African master printmaker, wildlife illustrator, and educator whose deeply evocative practice operates at the intersection of surrealism, conservation, and spiritual archaeology. Operating from Studio Moore in Fourways, Johannesburg—home to one of the largest private fine-art printing presses in South Africa—Moore handles a vast array of challenging manual techniques, including etching, woodblock printing, linocut, lithography, and mezzotint. Rather than delivering traditional, passive wildlife studies, his technically complex, large-scale works blend high-fidelity execution with a surreal, mystical worldview, inviting audiences to reconsider humanity's spiritual connection to the natural world.Exposed to animal behavior from a very young age due to his father working as a veterinarian, Moore spent his childhood observing wildlife at waterholes in the Kruger National Park, Namibia, and KwaZulu-Natal. He later formalized his draftsmanship at the Technikon Witwatersrand, graduating with a Higher National Diploma in Fine Arts in 1995 before completing further training in art education. In his studio, Moore approaches animal subjects by inviting what he describes as an open, mystical dialogue with nature. His complex compositions draw heavily from ancient Southern African oral traditions, San rock art, and Zulu mythology, framing native species—such as baboons, rhinos, or whales drifting through cloudscapes—as sacred ancestral guardians and carriers of regional memory.

item.title: John Newdigate
item.description: John Newdigate (b. 1968) is one of South Africa’s most celebrated ceramicists and artists. Living in the mountainous Overberg region of the Western Cape, Newdigate records contemporary issues alongside the physical landscapes, plants, and animals he encounters. An exuberant colorist, Newdigate specializes in painting hand-built, porcelain vessels using a unique technique inspired by precise and spontaneous mark-making.Newdigate's signature process involves hand-painting multiple layers of underglaze pigment, reserving certain areas with a wax resist, and then removing surrounding pigments. This process is repeated multiple times, resulting in complex, translucent, and radiant imagery with a mix of sharp and blurred lines that provide depth and perspective.Recurring themes in his work include plants and animals used to make wry commentary on human emotions and interactions. Recently, Newdigate has ventured into creating three-dimensional renditions of his painted imagery, using fiber-reinforced polymer cement layered over a wooden and PU framework, then adorned with oil paints. This exploration, free from the constraints of ceramics, has sparked a wave of fresh creativity and concepts.Newdigate’s work is part of several public collections, including the Iziko South African National Gallery, the William Humphreys Public Art Gallery, and the South African Cultural History Museum.

item.title: John Newdigate and Ian Garrett
item.description: John Newdigate (b. 1968) and Ian Garrett (b. 1971) are two of South Africa's most prominent contemporary ceramic artists whose collaborative partnership redefines the intersection of classical form and expressive surface design. Represented by the premier gallery EBONY/CURATED, the duo combines Garrett’s architectural mastery of hand-built clay with Newdigate’s vibrant, fluid painterly sensibilities. For both master artists, this ongoing collaboration is far more than a simple division of creative labor; it functions as a highly active, intuitive material conversation. Working in tandem and constantly responding to each other’s evolving visions, materials, and techniques, their iterative studio process ensures that every co-creation is imbued with the collective innovation of their combined perspectives.

item.title: Johnny Allison
item.description: Johnny Allison is a contemporary South African multidisciplinary visual artist, illustrator, and public designer whose progressive studio practice increasingly focuses on the activation of public and commercial muralism. Operating at the modern intersection of fine arts and graphic design, Allison brings a unique, powerful perspective to the contemporary street art landscape. Specializing in large-scale wall interventions, his practice intentionally subverts the flat, ordinary boundaries of urban architecture. He transforms everyday brick and concrete surfaces into highly immersive alternative realities, delivering impactful, socially conscious messages to diverse audiences.Allison’s distinct visual vocabulary is heavily defined by a brilliant style of "magical realism" that unfolds in meticulously structured layers of complexity and meaning. His public works rely on exceptionally bold, high-contrast color palettes and captivating, dreamlike subjects that seamlessly weave folklore, local identity, and contemporary design trends together. Rather than delivering simple decorative graphics, he uses layered visual storytelling to challenge or comfort viewers, sparking active community dialogue right on the street. Through these large-scale murals and community projects, Allison firmly establishes himself as an important, driving voice pushing the boundaries of public art, proving that fine-art sensibilities can beautifully thrive in accessible, everyday shared spaces.

item.title: Jonathan van der Walt
item.description: Jonathan van der Walt (b. 1991) is a Gqeberha-based visual artist, curator, and academic whose expressive paintings and mixed media works delve deeply into complex themes of memory, identity, and the natural landscape. His art intentionally combines vivid colour and heavily textured layers to build compelling visual stories that resonate with viewers on both a visceral and intellectual level. A highly interdisciplinary practitioner, Van der Walt holds a Master’s degree in Fine Art from Nelson Mandela University, where he also serves as a visual arts lecturer and manages the university’s active Bird Street Gallery.His expanding portfolio serves as a profound psychological bridge between historical inheritance and contemporary displacement. Through a complex layering process that merges tactile mediums with fluid, vibrant palettes, Van der Walt captures the sensory friction of navigating the postcolonial South African landscape. His canvases explore personal heritage alongside wider collective histories, turning abstract elements of the earth and sky into spaces for deep existential reflection.Regularly exhibiting at prominent national institutions—including a notable solo showcase at the William Humphreys Art Gallery (WHAG)—his work challenges the boundaries of traditional representation while creating a poignant space for dialogue about home, heritage, and identity construction.

item.title: Joseph Ntensibe
item.description: Joseph Ntensibe (b. 1953, Uganda) has dedicated his life to addressing the diminishing forests of his youth. The Uganda of his childhood has changed dramatically due to rampant deforestation caused by mining, war, drought, urbanization, and a lack of awareness about the value of forests. In the past twenty years, Uganda has lost over 1 million hectares of virgin forest cover—almost 30% of the country’s total land.Although Ntensibe is a highly collectible artist, his large-scale canvases are rare in the contemporary art market. The opportunity to collaborate with and showcase his extraordinary piece from the celebrated 'Disappearing Forest' series is a great privilege. Ntsensibe's dreamlike forest scenes shimmer with hidden sources of light, creating multicoloured sensory feasts. His work has been likened to that of Cezanne and Klimt for its luminosity, but many believe this artist-activist's work stands in a league of its own. The ever-changing landscapes in the series serve as a profound and poignant timeline of Uganda’s loss. In recent years, critics have noted how glimpses of sky and shafts of light, previously unheard of in true equatorial rain-forests, have appeared in Ntensibe’s forestscapes. While undeniably beautiful, these depictions evoke a sense of witnessing a living tragedy.

item.title: Joshua Miles
item.description: Joshua Miles (b. 1967) is a landscape artist who grew up in the Western Cape in South Africa. He studied fine arts at the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town where he received the Michaelis Prize for best student in his final year.Joshua is one of those rare artists who has managed to make a living solely from his art. He spent many years painting oils on canvas but his passion has always been with reduction block printmaking. Joshua’s influences in printmaking started at a young age seeing his aunt Elsa Miles’s woodcuts and later studying under Cecil Skotnes at UCT. He is inspired by the play of light on the landscape which leads him to explore his local areas. He is always hunting qualities of light that evoke emotion. This is often the softer light that brings out the in-between tones and greys most would miss. This love of capturing the play of light is found mostly in reflections on water or objects. He is also inspired by the impressionist style of loose mark making and the Japanese tradition of printmaking.After finishing at UCT Joshua moved to Hermanus where he met his Scottish wife, Angela. They have been married more than 20 years and they have over the years lived and worked between South Africa and Scotland. They work together in the business of selling Joshua’s art and have a home with studio in both countries.

item.title: JOY ADEBOYE
item.description: Joy Adeboye (b.1998, Nigeria) is a contemporary artist who lives and works in Lagos, Nigeria. She received her BA (2019) in literature from the Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile Ife.Joy Adeboye’s use of watercolor as her primary medium has been described as both bold and deeply inspiring. She is carving her own path within the contemporary revival of this technique; a medium with a history that stretches back to the origins of art itself and that only a few contemporary artists have reinterpreted as a means of navigating the ambiguous space between reality, the fantastic, and political utopia.Adeboye’s practice extends this lineage while shaping a language of her own. In her previous works; she explored a more mystical interplay of color and form, for her solo project in Tommorows Today she has produced a new body of work that delves into the intimate realm of desire, religion and sexuality.Sometimes appearing as collages of different papers or as a single piece, these watercolor paintings evoke both the delicacy of petals and the softness of flesh, while avoiding explicit representation. They seem to wander through the inner self.. both physically and mentally, through a language of form and color that remains open, shifting and poetic. Following a very well received solo presentation at FNBartjoburg 2024 adeboye was invited to feature in the Tommorrows Today section at Investec cape town art fair this year.Recent Projects: "Chaos the 8th year" FNBartJoburg 2024. "The vanguard" AMG Projects, March 2024, Lagos, Nigeria. Social media: @joyadejolaadeboye

item.title: JP Meyer
item.description: The initiation processes we experience throughout life are normally etched in our memory as milestones: sometimes pleasant, sometimes painful. Like pieces in a puzzle, Meyer highlights specific initiation processes and rituals in the lives of young boys and men which find expression later on in life: life on the playground, military service or simple acceptance within a new circle of friends. It is a process that is both welcoming and unsettling in its departure from comfort zones.In contrast to the notion of transitional processes as a necessary part of life, Meyer’s body of work highlights the tension between youthful innocence – individuality even – and the brutal transition towards a uniform group identity. One cannot help but lament the loss of innocence that is suffered during each ritual; like youthful feet being forced into rigid wooden clogs to impose uniformity. Meyer’s work is however not entirely a tale of social suppression.He sits comfortably with the fact that individuals form part of groups, and that transitional phases such as “religious christening and catechism, the shaping of a toddler to become a scholar, the initiation of a child into adulthood, first sexual encounters, marriage, even student initiations all signify processes towards membership of a new subculture, gang, group or organization”.

item.title: Judith Mason
item.description: Judith Mason (1938 - 2016) was a painter and graphic artist of symbolic and mythological landscapes, figures and portraits. Mason worked primarily in oils and pencil but also incorporated various graphic media and found objects into her work as well as having made a number of artists' books.Judith Mason drew and painted in reaction to her world: political events, books that she read, snippets of history or poetry which caught her eye, or the experience of particular people or animals.She taught art at the Scuola Lorenzo de Medici in Florence (Italy), the Michaelis School of Fine Art (UCT), at the University of the Witwatersrand and privately. Her work is represented in South African national art collections and museums and internationally in private and public collections including the Museum of Modern Art, New York; Yale University, The Bodleian Library at the University of Oxford and the Smithsonian National Museum of African Art, Washington DC.Mason's most well known public commission is The Man Who Sang and the Woman Who Kept Silent aka The Blue Dress (1998) at The Constitutional Court in Johannesburg, South Africa. Justice Albie Sachs considers the piece to be "one of the great pieces of art in the world of the late 20th century."

item.title: Judy Woodborne
item.description: Judy Woodborne is an acclaimed artist and printmaker with a distinguished career marked by innovation and international recognition. She earned her Master of Fine Arts Degree with Distinction from the University of Cape Town (UCT) in 1993. The body of work from her MFA received critical acclaim and is held in significant collections, including the Smithsonian Collection of African Art (USA) and the Sanlam Corporate Collection (SA).Woodborne's artistic prowess was highlighted when she was selected as the ABSA Klein Karoo Nasionale Kunstefees Festival Artist in 2007, for which she produced "The Garden of Eden," a unique series of paintings on gold leaf. Her curatorial talents are evident in "The Exquisite Corpse," a portfolio of 16 etchings she curated and published, which was selected for the Klein Karoo Nasionale Kunstefees 2009 and later exhibited by the Norval Foundation. She also served as a guest curator for the Woordfees in 2018 and 2019.Internationally recognized, Woodborne has participated in numerous International Print Biennales, and her work is represented in various international public collections and museums. Her experimental approach to printmaking was showcased at the Salzburg Summer Festival, Austria, in 2015, and further explored in her series of experimental print constructions, "The Anatomy of the World," exhibited at Lizamore Gallery in 2018.Her excellence in printmaking was affirmed in 2019 when she was awarded the S.C. Bes Romania S.R.L. prize at the International Contemporary Engraving Biennial, Romania, for her engraving "The Weaver." Most recently, her work was selected for the "Summer 2020" exhibition curated by the International Print Centre in New York, USA.

item.title: Justice Mathonsi
item.description: Justice Mathonsi (b. 1987, Soweto), raised in Ribugwani, Limpopo from 1990, is a Johannesburg-based South African artist and printmaker. After completing high school and briefly studying Architecture at Intec College in 2011, he found his calling in printmaking, enrolling at the prestigious Artist Proof Studio in 2012. There, he specialized in the intricate technique of lino reduction.Currently working as a full-time artist, Mathonsi focuses on creating compelling, large-scale portraits, primarily of the significant women within his life and community. His detailed works serve to emphasize their importance and acknowledge their often-overlooked roles in society, particularly in raising children. The lines and textures in his portraits capture elements of time, age, history, and accumulated knowledge. Through his distinct mark-making and the incorporation of patterns referencing his Tsonga roots, Mathonsi elevates these humble women, creating a powerful visual record of his family tree and heritage while prompting viewers to recognize their profound contributions.

item.title: Justin Dingwall
item.description: Justin Dingwall born in 1983, South Africa is a successful Johannesburg-based artistic photographer. He achieved a Baccalaureus Technologies in Photography Cum Laude from the Tshwane University of Technology in Pretoria in 2004. Dingwall has exhibited extensively both locally in South Africa and Internationally. He has been selected for various awards including, SA Taxi Foundation Art Award 2015, Sasol New Signatures 2014, and IPA – int’l photography awards 2013. .Justin Dingwall creates images that resonate with emotion and challenges traditional notions of beauty. His works leans towards the unusual, and avenues less traveled with cultural undertones.

item.title: KADARA ENYEASI
item.description: Kadara Enyeasi is a multidisciplinary artist based in Lagos, Nigeria. A graduate of architecture from the University of Lagos, Kadara’s conceptual work combines his interest in history, design and literature. Best known for his work in photography and digital college, his practice has expanded to take on painting, moving images, tactile processes and abstraction. His work which is often paradoxical, based off local themes and challenges the status quo through the reimagination of myths and legends.Recent projects include: Zeitz MOCAA exhibition, 'Still Here Tomorrow To High Five You Yesterday' (2019). solo exhibition, Is it not enough for the sea to be beautiful? (2020).

item.title: Kagiso Reuben
item.description: Kagiso Reuben (b. 1999, South Africa. Lives and works in Vereeniging)Kagiso Reuben portrays a strong sense of storytelling in his work, exploring his past and environment with a sense of child-like communication, as seen in his vivid use of colour blocking and scenery. His practice considers both his personal context and the backdrop of an environment shaped by political and social dynamics, with particular emphasis on portraiture infused with elements of caricature.Reuben's visual language draws on memory and lived experience, translating everyday moments into bold, expressive compositions. Rather than presenting a purely documentary account of his surroundings, he filters observation through imagination, allowing colour, form, and gesture to carry emotional weight. This blending of the personal and the political situates his work within a broader dialogue on identity, place, and belonging in contemporary South Africa. Through his distinctive approach, Reuben continues to develop a visual vocabulary that is both intimate and socially engaged, inviting viewers to reflect on the layered realities of everyday South African life.

item.title: Kagiso Gundane
item.description: Kagiso Gundane is a multidisciplinary visual artist, born and raised in the North West Province, South Africa.Born into a family of three, he is the oldest and only male among his siblings. Gundane has been fascinated and enthusiastic about art from a young age, and as a result pursued a visual arts degree at the University of Johannesburg.He works in a variety of art mediums, including; printmaking, drawing, sculpture and installations. Growing up among African traditional healers in his community, his subject matter is centered around African spirituality and cultural sensitivity in a post-colonial space. As a person with a spiritual gift, Gundane is more involved in his work to express his ideas and interpretations at a close and intimate level.

item.title: Kagiso Patrick Mautloa
item.description: Kagiso Patrick Mautloa studied art at the Rorke’s Drift Art Centre in KwaZulu-Natal and at the Mofolo Art Centre in Soweto. He has participated in Thupelo and Triangle workshops, held numerous solo and group exhibitions, and has work in a number of important public collections across South Africa.His work explores the street life around him and his studio at the Bag Factory (Fordsburg Artists’ Studios) in downtown Johannesburg. He observes the women roasting mielies (corn) over coal-fired tin braziers on street corners; wholesalers and hawkers selling cheap imports from the Far East; and street traders who eke out a living with a few items displayed on small boards near busy intersections.Working with figurative elements, abstract textures and multiple colour overlays, Mautloa explores the possibilities of lithography. He has made innovative use of drawing materials in his prints, using found objects as stencils through which he sprays tusche and toner. Textures are an important part of Mautloa’s work. As he works, he notices the mundane surfaces around him and sometimes incorporates them into his artwork.Unexpected things, such as the rough surface of a well-used cutting board or a worn-out cotton rag, hold a new fascination and beauty for him. Delicate drawing and seemingly random splatters entice the viewer and challenge us to look at the world in a new way.Kagiso Patrick Mautloa is an artist whose work eludes a neat definition. He is as comfortable working in abstraction as he is with more figurative imagery. Most of his work is created in oils and acrylics, but he has also incorporated found objects and collage into his two-dimensional work. He has produced a number of installations and has also worked with photography.

item.title: Kaleab Abate
item.description: Kaleab Abate was born in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia in 1998, where he also currently lives and works. In 2021, he graduated from the renowned Ale School of Fine Arts and Design, Addis Ababa, with a focus on printmaking. He has shown at Art on Paper Brussels, 1-54 London, INVESTEC Cape Town Art Fair and African Galleries Now x Artsy, and has completed a 3-month residency at Silhouette Projects in Kampala. He was part of the group exhibition Eastern Voices: Contemporary Art from East Africa at Addis Fine Art, London (2023) and Form and Fantasy at Afriart Gallery, Kampala (2024).Employing various printmaking techniques, different materials, charcoal drawing, among others, allows Ethiopian artist Kaleab Abate (*1998) to experiment with different layers in his works on paper and canvas. Beginning with a portrait in which he focuses on emotions and expression rather than the likeness of his subject, he then allows the material and printmaking patterns to guide his compositions intuitively. He allows bodily shapes to fragment and deform into layers, some rich, others delicate, half-transparent, or patterned, adding his distinct surreal twist. Abate’s layering technique becomes a process to imagine and visualize the complex depths of the stories that may live within the bodies he depicts.Abate’s composition is loaded with unexpected forms and textures, the majority of which are unrealistic. Figures are distorted, shapes are erratic, and color options are limited. The vast majority of events are unreal. This daring fantasy piques the artist’s interest. His creations, however, have a considerable amount of realism. This is why he regards his works as “fantasized realities”.

item.title: Kamyar Bineshtarigh
item.description: Kamyar Bineshtarigh was born in 1996 in Semnan, Iran. He lives and works in Cape Town, South Africa. He is currently in his final year, completing a BA Fine Art degree at the Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town (UCT). He received a Diploma in Fine Art at Ruth Prowse School of Art in 2019 where he also won the Ruth Prowse Award for his body of work An Exhaustive Catalogue of Texts Dealing with the Orient which explored Edward Said’s concept of Orientalism using Said’s eponymous book (1978) as the source material.In 2021 Bineshtarigh was awarded a Creative Knowledge Resources (CKR) Fellowship: CKR is an interdisciplinary project by the National Research Foundation & UCT studying socially engaged artistic practices in Africa and its diaspora. Bineshtarigh works in a variety of media, most notably painting and video. His conceptual concerns range from language, (mis)communication as well as the practice of writing and transliteration.In 2021 Bineshtarigh was awarded a Creative Knowledge Resources (CKR) Fellowship: CKR is an interdisciplinary project by the National Research Foundation UCT studying socially engaged artistic practices in Africa and its diaspora. Bineshtarigh works in a variety of media, most notably painting and video. His conceptual concerns range from language, (mis)communication as well as the practice of writing and transliteration.

item.title: Kamohelo Blessing Rooi
item.description: Kamohelo Blessing Rooi is a South African artist born in the province of Gauteng in 2001. Rooi's work centres around the artist's personal connection to the township and interrogates the emotional landscape of Soweto, where he currently lives and works.Rooi's interest in the arts was first initiated through 'arts and crafts', classes where he was introduced to Nelson Makamo, Wonder Buhle Mbambo and Jean Michel Basquiat, who became significant influences. Working primarily in Acrylic on Canvas, Rooi has established his style through a series titled; 'Kasiflavour' which translates to 'Location Flavour', highlighting his deep affection for the township. Rooi paints stills, culled from both his own photobook collection and personal experiences to capture Soweto's nocturnal allure through his use of bright colours and flat brush strokes.The moments captured in Rooi's paintings are the result of a delicate balance between recollection and interpretation. Whether it's an intimate moment between friends or figures staged against the Sowetan landscape - Rooi's reverence for his richly diverse home and its inhabitants is paramount.

item.title: Karabo Maine
item.description: Karabo Maine (b. 1986, Gaborone, Botswana) is a visual artist currently residing and practicing in his hometown. He holds a BA Fine Art (Photography) from the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town. He has exhibited his artwork in several exhibitions in Gaborone, as well as at the FNB Art Joburg Art Fair in 2022.Karabo Maine's artistic practice not only celebrates the aesthetic richness of his subjects but also invites contemplation on societal narratives and personal introspection through his own lens. Importantly, Maine's artistic practice is deeply personal, informed by his own experiences as a recovering individual. This perspective adds a layer of authenticity and empathy to his work.

item.title: Kate Otten
item.description: Kate Otten is a South African architect, who has won numerous awards for her South African traditional work. After working for a number of other practices, Otten established her own firm in 1989 in Johannesburg.She has designed community libraries, the waterfront development at Tzaneen, an art therapy centre in Soweto and the museum exhibition space at the former Women's Jail at Constitution Hill which received a commendation from the South African Institute of Architects (SAIA).Kate has won many awards including the SAIA Award of Merit House Staude in 1998 to the Mbokodo Awards Architecture and Creative Design in 2013.

item.title: Katherine Bull
item.description: Katherine Bull is currently a practicing artist with two decades of experience lecturing in the visual arts at Stellenbosch University and the University of Cape Town. She is currently a part-time lecturer in Visual Art at the Cape Town Creative Academy and offers private mentorship for artists at Fourfold.In 1998 she was awarded a Master of Fine Art degree from the University of Cape Town with distinction. Since then Bull has produced five solo exhibitions, taken part in numerous group exhibitions and performed at international conferences in Poland, USA & Estonia. In 2004 a public sculpture project titled Come to Pass was unveiled, produced in collaboration with artist Fritha Langerman as winners of the 3rd Cape Town Public Sculpture Competition (2002). She was selected for the Ampersand Fellowship in New York (2007), Dwayer International Residency in Alexandria, Egypt (2008) and most recently she participated in a residency in Bologna Italy (2015) as an AIR Laureate (2014).

item.title: Katlego C.L Twala
item.description: Katlego C.L. Twala (b. 2000, Gaborone, Botswana) is a contemporary painter whose practice centres on figurative portraiture, combining the technical discipline of classical realism with a distinctly contemporary perspective. She received formal training at the Swedish Academy of Realist Art and the Barcelona Academy of Art, where she developed a strong foundation in traditional painting techniques, including careful observation, anatomy, and the nuanced use of light and colour. Through her work, Twala explores themes of identity, representation, and the human experience, using portraiture as a means of engaging with broader social and cultural narratives. Her paintings often invite viewers to reflect on questions of belonging, memory, and the complexities of contemporary life. By merging time-honoured artistic methods with modern social commentary, Twala creates compelling works that bridge the past and present, contributing to ongoing conversations about portraiture and the role of realism in contemporary African art.

item.title: Katlego Phetlhe
item.description: Katlego Phetlhe is a photographer whose work is currently inspired by the imaginative and restorative practice of studio photography across the African continent. They are primarily concerned with rest, pleasure, and the erotic, viewing these states not as luxuries, but as immediate entrances into personal and communal liberation. By engaging with studio traditions, Phetlhe creates visual spaces where intimacy and self-expression can flourish without boundary. Their latest body of work traces the roots of these central concerns deep into their own family history, using personal archives and memory to explore the complexities of multiple self-hood. Through this nuanced approach, Phetlhe's images offer a tactile and reflective space that honors lineage while actively pursuing new forms of autonomy. Ultimately, their practice serves as an ongoing process of physical and social grounding, inviting audiences to reconsider how rest, joy, and ancestral connections can function as vital tools for collective healing and liberation.

item.title: Katlego Tlabela
item.description: Multidisciplinary artist Katlego Tlabela creates work that examines social and political crises in post-apartheid South Africa. He employs painting, sound, photography, and sculptural installations to spark important dialogues surrounding race and representation.After graduating from the University of Cape Town’s Michaelis School of Fine Art, where he majored in printmaking, Tlabela began showing work in group exhibitions throughout South Africa. Though at first reluctant to call himself a painter due to his formal training as a printmaker, Tlabela has received attention for his paintings depicting Black subjects in positions of leisure and luxurious domestic settings. These works—often composed of acrylic, ink, and collage on canvas—feature sprawling interiors, high-end furniture, and walls adorned with colorful artwork.

item.title: Kay Gasei
item.description: Kay Gasei is a British-born, Zambian artist whose work fuses mythology, history, and personal narratives into richly detailed, symbolic compositions. Working primarily in painting and drawing, Gasei weaves stories that traverse cultures and time, creating surreal yet deeply human worlds. His art often explores themes of identity, memory, and the interplay between tradition and modernity. Known for his refined line work and layered symbolism, Gasei invites viewers into a universe where folklore and contemporary life meet in a harmonious, thought-provoking dialogue. Through intricate mark-making and balanced figurative forms, his practice examines how ancient allegories and historical narratives shape contemporary consciousness. By seamlessly blending mythical motifs with intimate personal reflections, Gasei creates multi-layered compositions that challenge viewers to look beyond surface aesthetics. Ultimately, his work serves as both a vital cultural bridge and a meditative exploration of belonging, encouraging deeper reflection on how ancestral heritage continually informs our shared human experience.

item.title: Kato BC
item.description: Kato BC, born in 1997 in Masaka, Uganda, is a painter whose work explores the delicate balance between constraints and freedoms experienced by religious leaders in Africa. He sheds light on the complex challenges and opportunities these leaders face as they navigate societal expectations, internal religious hierarchies, and political landscapes within diverse cultural and social contexts. His artistic vision is deeply influenced by the shadows of his childhood, especially the impact of his twin sister’s blindness. These personal experiences have heightened his sensitivity to light, shape, and form. His artworks reflect both his introspective journey and keen observations of the world around him. He offers a nuanced perspective on the intersections of faith, culture, and power, capturing the subtle tensions and harmonies that define the lives of religious leaders. He explores the human condition, inviting viewers to engage with the intricate dynamics of belief and authority. Through his evocative use of color, patterns, and texture, Kato BC’s paintings provide a window into the multifaceted experiences of those who lead and serve within religious communities.

item.title: Kedirile Kemaketse
item.description: Kedirile Kemaketse is a self-taught artist born and raised in the vibrant village of Kanye in southern Botswana. Deeply attuned to the rich atmosphere of his home village, he draws continuous inspiration from its everyday sights, sounds, and the intricate narratives, both seen and unseen, that weave through daily life. Beyond his local surroundings, Kemaketse derives profound creative energy from nature and the expansive universe at large. Working fluidly across diverse mediums, including pencil, crayon, charcoal, pen, graphite, and acrylic, he crafts tactile, highly evocative visual works. He holds a strong fascination with ancient ruins, historical artifacts, and weather-worn structures. This enduring interest directly shapes his artistic expression, giving rise to pieces rich in heavy texture, intricate cracked lines, and expressive abstract compositions. Through these weathered surfaces and deliberate marks, Kemaketse thoughtfully explores themes of memory, passage of time, and the subtle dialogue between human existence and the natural world.

item.title: Keith Hennin
item.description: Keith Henning (b.1982, South Africa), currently lives and works in Cape Town. In 2024 Henning completed his postgraduate diploma in Fine Art at the Michaelis School of Fine Art, at the University of Cape Town. Originally developing a practice in design, founding the well-known AKJP design store and clothing label, Henning has expanded his material interests into sculpture, working primarily in steel and ceramic.Most recently, the artist presented WATERSPORTS — Not for public consumption, at RESERVOIR in Cape Town. This marked Henning’s third solo exhibition, expanding on the body of work which was exhibited at the Michaelis Gallery upon conclusion of his studies in 2024. In 2023 the artist presented PUMPED at The Fourth Gallery in Cape Town, South Africa. In 2023 his work was included in the group exhibition, Hello Stranger at Bhalla Munro, New York, USA. In 2019 Bad Paper Editions presented Henning’s work at AKAA Art and Design fair, Paris, France, and the Investec Cape Town Art Fair, Cape Town, South Africa.Keith Henning’s contribution to material and design discourse has been recognised by TWYG, who in 2021 awarded him the Sustainability Prize in 2021, and Cape Wools as the Designer Competition Winner in 2018. In 2021 Zeitz MOCAA exhibited his work in 21 Years of South African Fashion. His work is included in the Zeitz MOCAA Permanent Collection.

item.title: Kelebogile Marope
item.description: Kelebogile Tshegofatso Marope was born in Ramotswa, Botswana in 1985. After a Bachelor of Fine Art degree in 2009, in which she majored in sculpture, Marope went on to complete a Master of Fine Art in 2013 at Rhodes University, Grahamstown, South Africa. She works predominantly in the medium of sculpture, using the found object, and more recently two- dimensional drawings and prints. Her work engages with issues of nostalgia, familiarity, everyday life, and the implications of cleansing rituals in the domestic space.She explores familiar household objects and reveals in practice how these ordinary objects are bound up with one’s own history, experiences, and ideals. What interests her with the domestic object is what is usually hidden behind over familiarity and mundanity. She has been part of group shows held in Grahamstown, South Africa and Gaborone, Botswana. She lives in Gaborone, Botswana.

item.title: Kelvin Trautman
item.description: Kelvin Trautman is a self-taught photographer and filmmaker based in Cape Town and London, specializing in narrative-driven content that explores the intersection of human experience and environmental conditions. Known for his creative direction, unique perspectives, and athletic ability behind the camera, Kelvin has made a significant mark in the outdoor industry.His work spans all seven continents, with high-profile clients such as Patagonia, the United Nations, Reuters, and Red Bull. His images have been featured in prominent publications like The New York Times, National Geographic, Red Bulletin, and Outside Magazine.Kelvin is passionate about using photography and film-making to connect, educate, and inspire, believing that all you need to tell a good story is a camera, courage, and empathy. He strives to challenge perceptions and push creative boundaries, seeking to go beyond the stereotypical perfect moment to capture authentic, immersive experiences.

item.title: Kerri Liebovitz
item.description: Kerri Liebovitz, born in 2002, is an emerging contemporary South African fine artist whose work is marked by a deep exploration of themes surrounding the self, the representation of the nude in art, vulnerability, sexual violence, and having a room of one’s own.Drawing inspiration from her own experiences, Liebovitz utilises the image of her own body as her subject for her portrait paintings to explore these complex concepts. Based in Johannesburg, Liebovitz has just completed her studies at The University of the Witwatersrand, with a Bachelor's in Fine Arts. Her more recent works comprise of a series of nude, self-portrait, oil paintings, serving as a form of empowerment and reclamation of her body and the representation of the female form.In her artistic methodology, she references her exploration and research into the portrayal of women and the nude and challenges historical representations shaped by the male gaze. This holds great personal importance for her as she advocates for women to assert their presence in the art world and to reclaim agency over their own bodies and narratives, transcending the constraints of patriarchal historical frameworks.

item.title: Ketumile Malesa
item.description: Ketumile Meso (28) is a South African Artist whose interdisciplinary practice explores – Identity, Faith and Belonging in a South African context. Originally hailing from a small village in the North West Province – Meso seeks to understand his heritage, and his surroundings through the mediums of: Collage, Sound, Video & mobile.Meso has been exploring Johannesburg's visual, sonic and cultural identity for the past eight years – with the site being his foundational point of inspiration. In an effort to further understand himself and his place within the metropolis, Meso explores the black lived experience and visual language of the inner city. Currently, Meso is interested in the themes of: Remembering, Music As Time Travel, & The African Influence on Western Spirituality.

item.title: Kgotlelelo Sekiti
item.description: Kgotlelelo Bradley Sekiti is a 21-year-old performance artist from Alex. Sekiti explains that his work is inextricably linked to his experience of being a black queer body – one that is, undeniably, not been the easiest. His work speaks to that fact that the journey of being a black, queer body seems to be designed with the challenge of navigating “safe” spaces of existence which - along the way - prove that the notion of a safe space is one that is almost non-existent. This work looks into what he has deemed as a “safer” space. “As recently discovered by NASA —the possibility of an alternate/parallel universe — m practice forms into the exploration of parallel universes that queer bodies create in order to enable the co-existence of split realities that they identify with into a single frame".

item.title: Khanyisa Agnes Brancon
item.description: KHANYISA AGNES BRANCON| b. 2002 Tzaneen, Limpopo is a Johannesburg-based multidisciplinary artist hailing from Polokwane. Brancon explores mediums of expression namely Printmaking, Photography, and Installation through an interdisciplinary approach that consists of the use of textiles, thus prioritising materiality throughout her work. The manifestation of labour and leisure, maternal lineage, and the black experience are grand themes addressed throughout her work.Her work explores the contemporary feminist approach that calls to attention the intersection of representation needed for the kind of black women who reflect on personal and family-related histories. The existence of Spirituality as an additional layer of which life is experienced and explored in the work. Brancon plans to actively participate within the art ecosystem by creating platforms of representation for black bodies envisioning her story as a reflection to theirs.She is currently pursuing a degree in Fine Arts with the University of the Witwatersrand. In addition to her ventures, Brancon forms part of a collective bonded by the practice of printmaking with three black women artists from Limpopo. The printmaking collective called Boteng, explores themes of materiality and the black experience within its art practice. Due to their meticulous organisation and continuous dedication to the practice of art; their direction leans towards curation and establishing a presence within the art ecosystem.Khanyisa is the recipient of the 2025 Blessing Ngobeni Art Prize.

item.title: Khanyisile Mahlangu
item.description: Born in 1999, Khanyisile Mahlangu is a self-trained Visual Artist. Having studied Interior design and Project Management, garnering a degree from the University of Johannesburg where the skills and knowledge gained have seamlessly integrated into her artistic journey. Allowing her to explore new mediums and techniques and leaving a lasting impact. Khanyisile is interested in creating modern abstract harmonious form compositions and environments that immerse the viewer in her realm of being. Imagination is at the heart of her artistic journey.The constant flow of ideas that once only found life in her interior design projects now have a canvas of their own. Her work reflects a continuous dialogue between the imagined and the real, the conceptual and the tangible. This interplay allows Khanyisile to explore new dimensions of abstract art, pushing boundaries and redefining spaces through her creative lens. Her work is characterised by its modern abstract style, heavily influenced by themes of contemplation and confusion influenced by young South African Artists. It is a visual exploration of the human psyche, delving into the complexities of identity, emotion, perception and transforming spaces through their presence. Colour choices always aim to reflect the duality of calm and chaos inherent in her introspective and subconscious abstract thoughts.

item.title: Khaya Sineyile
item.description: Khaya Sineyile’s subject matter ranges from township scenes to more introspective themes –referencing childhood games and observations on religious hypocrisy, faction-fighting and witchcraft. Most recently he turned his attention to the effects of social inequality, specifically relating to the South African family structure. His confident brush marks and considered palette convey a rawness which he contrasts with cartoon-like outlines - a device which removes the figures from their ground and introduces elements of playfulness, wit and humour to the often-loaded subject matter.Sineyile is a mostly self-taught artist from Nyanga, Cape Town. From an early age, he has had a love for drawing and painting and trained at the Arts and Media Access Centre (AMAC) in 2005. In 2009, he was selected as a resident artist at Greatmore Studios and later that year at the Souq Waqif Art Center in Doha, Qatar. Sineyile has participated in several solo exhibitions and more than 30 group exhibitions, locally and abroad. Artworks of his are included in private collections overseas and the corporate collections of Spier, Nando’s UK, Truworths, Groote Schuur Hospital and Hollard.

item.title: Kholofelo Simon Moshapo jnr
item.description: Simon Moshapo Junior (b. 1991) is a South African multi-disciplinary artist. His artistic practice is deeply personal and serves as a form of healing and self-expression, reflecting his journey with epilepsy and the exploration of identity. Living with this condition has shaped his worldview, inspiring a body of work that speaks to the sense of "otherness" he experiences, and confronting the realities of mortality and resilience.Moshapo's art is characterized by its layered exploration of human existence, often drawing on themes of self-preservation, identity, and cultural heritage. His sculptural work, paintings, and drawings serve not only as expressions of his personal journey but also as reflections on broader societal issues. Through intricate compositions, Moshapo tackles political and social challenges, using his art to provoke thought and foster dialogue about life’s complexities.Moshapo’s art is characterized by its layered exploration of human existence, often drawing on themes of self-preservation, identity, and cultural heritage. His sculptural work, paintings, and drawings serve not only as expressions of his personal journey but also as reflections on broader societal issues. Through intricate compositions, Moshapo tackles political and social challenges, using his art to provoke thought and foster dialogue about life’s complexities.His practice integrates a strong connection to the material world, with wood sculptures and tactile mediums playing a significant role in his exploration of form and texture. Each piece is a testament to his belief in the transformative power of art—his work seeks to communicate not just emotion but also a deeper understanding of the human condition.Informed by his lived experience, Simon Moshapo Junior’s artistic vision is one of resilience and reclamation, rooted in a profound sense of identity and a drive to create art that transcends personal and political boundaries.

item.title: Khotso Motsoeneng
item.description: Khotso Motsoeneng (b. 1993) is an emerging artist who works primarily in photography and painting. His recent body of work is inspired by the wood’s natural grain which he incorporates into compositions of flattened forms of decorative patterned work. He describes this process of stylistic liberation and freedom as a step towards listening to his inner voice and his artwork mimics his emotion. Motsoeneng was born in the Free State province, but now works from his studio at Constitution Hill in Johannesburg. He obtained a National Diploma in Photography from the Tshwane University of Technology in 2017. In the same year he was a Top 100 finalist in the Thami Mnyele Culture and Resistance Fine Art Awards. In 2019 Motsoeneng was one of the four finalists for the Cassirer Welz Award. Motsoeneng has taken part in a number of group exhibitions in Johannesburg and Pretoria.

item.title: Khulekani Mayisa
item.description: Khule Mayisa is an independent filmmaker and photographer. She obtained a BA degree in Film& Television Studies from The University of Johannesburg, and, since graduating in 2018, has created several experimental short films, with a style that has been described in the Mail & Guardian as, “blending polemicism with a unique, sensuous visual sensibility”.Her last film, “Okumhlophe” (2021) won two international awards: Best Short Film at the B3 Biennale of the Moving Image in Frankfurt, Germany; and Best Cinematography at the Mom Film Fest in New York, USA. She was one of 25 participants invited to attend Frankfurt’s B3 Hessenlab in 2022 for a new screenplay in development.Her work has been showcased in local film festivals such as the Africa Rising International Film Festival, as well as film festivals in Nigeria, The United Kingdom, and Poland. Mayisa’s lens, which extends itself to portrait and fashion photography, is focused on amplifying the black woman’s experience as a reclamation from centuries of racial and patriarchal oppression. This work earned her a spot as a finalist for the 2021 Africa Photo Awards, which doubled as an exhibition at The Gallery in Keyes Art Mile. So far, her photography has been featured on Adidas ZA, Photo Vogue, and Morning Live.She has freelanced in the industry as a film director, editor, videographer, photographer, and stylist. Her visual language is empowering, poetic, and understated.

item.title: Khulekani Magudulela
item.description: Khulekani Magudulela is a multidisciplinary artist based in Johannesburg, South Africa. He holds an Honours Bachelor's degree in Fine Arts from the University of the Witwatersrand. Magudulela's artistic practice deeply engages with the thoughtful exploration of meaning and the creation of new possibilities, frequently incorporating organic and tactile materials to investigate core themes of memory, identity, and environmental connection. His versatile approach to contemporary art spans a wide range of creative mediums, including installation, painting, performance, sculpture, and ceramics. Through these varied modes of expression, Magudulela seamlessly bridges physical material qualities with conceptual depth, inviting viewers to reflect on the delicate relationships between natural forms, spatial dynamics, and shared human experience. By continuously experimenting with texture, process, and physical form, he constructs nuanced visual narratives that thoughtfully challenge conventional boundaries, successfully establishing himself as a vital, highly inventive, and compelling artistic voice within South Africa’s dynamic contemporary art landscape.

item.title: Khumo Ramaila
item.description: Khumo Ramaila (b. 2001) is a multidisciplinary artist based in Johannesburg, South Africa. He began his formal training in visual arts at the National School of the Arts, where he graduated in 2019. Ramaila furthered his education in fine arts with a specialization in printmaking at Artist Proof Studio, where he is currently completing his senior year.Under the mentorship of various experienced printmakers, he is dedicated to honing his craft and achieving excellence in printmaking. In the early stages of his career, Ramaila has participated in several notable exhibitions, including the Fine Arts Print Fair (2019), TAF Paper (2023), Umsizi Nopende (2023), Impressions on Paper (2023), Where You Are (2024), Latitudes Art Fair (2024), Faces and Figures (2024), And Why Not A Print? (2025). Additionally, he was part of the RMB Talent Unlocked mentorship program (2024), which focuses on building a cohesive body of work and equipping artists with the necessary skills to establish successful careers.As Khumo Ramaila continues to evolve as an artist, we can anticipate significant contributions from him to the world of contemporary art. His future endeavours promise to further establish his presence in the art community, ensuring that his work remains both relevant and impactful.

item.title: Kidane Getaw
item.description: Kidane Getaw, born in Addis Ababa in 1994, began his artistic journey as a child, spending hours recreating diverse images from posters. This early engagement with visual art laid the foundation for his future career. In 2021, he graduated with a Bachelor of Arts in Painting from Ale School of Fine Arts and Design in Addis Ababa.Getaw’s artistic practice is a profound exploration of the human psyche and the subconscious mind. His work delves into the enigmatic realm of dreams and nightmares, reflecting on how these inner experiences mirror and transcend the mundane aspects of waking life. Through his art, Getaw seeks to unravel the intricate interplay between reality and illusion, revealing how our innermost musings, desires, and fears shape our perceptions and actions.Getaw captures the complex web of human emotions and subconscious influences. His art invites viewers to navigate the blurred boundaries between lived experience and dreamlike reverie, offering a space where the dualities of reality and illusion coexist and interact. By exploring these themes, Getaw encourages deeper reflection on the ways in which our dreams and waking lives are intertwined. Kidane Getaw’s work is characterized by its introspective approach and ability to evoke the delicate dance between reality and fantasy, inviting audiences to explore the hidden depths of human experience.

item.title: Kilmany-Jo Liversage
item.description: Kilmany-Jo Liversage (b. 1973) lives and works in Cape Town, South Africa. Adopting the graffiti or urban art language allows her to update, renew and challenge the conventions of painting, though her rendering of female subjects are inspired by Renaissance era portraiture. It also references digitised mass production and a futuristic post-human world, populated by perfect-looking female cyborgs. The masculine gaze, to which all feminine is subject within a patriarchal framework, is plain to see. However, revealed as self-portraits, the feminine, cast in the roles given to her by The Gaze, stares knowingly, ferociously, straight back. The result is a series of brightly coloured large-scale paintings, evoking the street, art history and the future.

item.title: Kim Karabo Makin
item.description: Kim Karabo Makin (b. 1994, Gaborone, Botswana) is a multidisciplinary artist whose practice weaves together sculpture, sound, and site-responsive installation, grounded in rigorous research and a keen spatial awareness. Informed by lived experiences of displacement, migration, and multiculturalism, Makin’s work examines how geographic, historical, and cultural contexts shape individual and collective identity. Through nuanced material exploration, she invites viewers to reconsider their relationship to physical space, memory, and environment.Holding a Master of Fine Arts (MFA) from the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town, Makin thoughtfully bridges personal narrative with broader social commentary. Her research-driven installations frequently combine tactile mediums and auditory components to construct immersive, reflective spaces. By probing the subtleties of heritage and spatial politics, her practice cultivates meaningful dialogue around home, regional boundaries, and the fluid dynamics of contemporary belonging.

item.title: Kirsten Beets
item.description: South Africa, 1983Kirsten Beets paints our contemporary Eden. Her paintings inhabit a place somewhere between the real and imagined, a painted mythology that explores ethical realities. She is continually looking at the shifting relationship between people at leisure and the natural world. She isolates the moments of these interactions; sometimes as immersive images, and at other times as curious objects suspended in the picture plane where a landscape is reduced to flat colour or soft ombres. Snapshots of our curious human interactions with natural environments are all rendered in delicate detail.Beets revisits certain subject matters which have captured her imagination; and often familiar figures make cameo appearances throughout her work. These characters seem to inhabit a narrative realm within the confines of a canvas where their paths are intertwined and yet, perhaps, they remain strangers to each other. The repetition of these figures embodies the strange familiarity inherent in public spaces, such as the beachfront, where many of the things we use to identify ourselves are stripped away.Her exhibitions are complex collections of observations and imaginary musings made manifest in oil paint on paper, board, and linen. Her carefully considered compositions tell a subtle story of the strange and the familiar, leisure and decay, stasis and transience.

item.title: Kirsten Sims
item.description: Through her painting Kirsten seeks connection; to communicate the way she sees and experiences the world and her place in it. The scenes Kirsten paints are often a self-aware and gentle parody of the lives people portray on social media. Taking a break from the hyper-connectedness of modern living, within a body of work Kirsten will swop the sartorial crowd for big open skies punctuated with an evening star or rolling clouds. She seamlessly replaces the theatre of human interaction with the drama of a natural landscape.

item.title: Kobus la Grange
item.description: Kobus la Grange is a contemporary sculptor whose practice centres on the human figure, positioning body language as the primary locus in his ongoing investigation of what it means to be human. Working with form and spatial relationships, La Grange examines how subtle shifts in posture, alignment, and physical presence articulate complex psychological states. He uses pose as an essential key to mediate internal emotional landscapes into formally and technically rigorous sculptures, bridging conceptual depth with meticulous craftsmanship.A central element of his practice involves creating groups of interrelating figures, establishing dynamic spatial dialogues between individual forms. By arranging these figures in proximity, La Grange explores themes of human connection, interpersonal dynamics, and shared vulnerability. These figurative compositions invite viewers into a nuanced narrative space, ultimately bringing across a deeply resonant atmosphere and contemplative mood.

item.title: Kristen McClarty
item.description: THE PRINTING GIRLS (TPG) is an all-female collective of South African-based artists who work in print. Here's the background story to our #PRINTLIKEAGIRL gang: in 2009, the six founders of TPG graduated in the Arts from Rhodes University, which has always had a strong history of printmaking. The main focus has never changed, to create a platform exclusively for our country's women printmakers to share ideas, network, and exhibit together.Since its founding, TPG has grown into a vital creative community, offering members the opportunity to collaborate across styles, techniques, and generations while championing the specific challenges and opportunities faced by women working in the medium. The collective values printmaking not only as a technical discipline but as a powerful tool for storytelling, activism, and connection. Through group exhibitions, workshops, and ongoing dialogue, TPG continues to build visibility for South African women printmakers, both locally and internationally, while nurturing a supportive space where new voices can develop alongside established practitioners.

item.title: Kutlo Mabua
item.description: Kutlo Mabua (b. 1992) is a self-taught visual artist from Mahalapye, Botswana. His work reflects an ongoing journey of self-discovery and personal evolution, exploring identity in a state of renewal as he settles into the person he is becoming. Through his creative process, Mabua delves into the nuanced layers of growth, introspection, and the balance between vulnerability and strength. His art captures moments of transformation, where past experiences meet present realities, offering a deeper understanding of self. Using mediums like ink pointillism, acrylics, and hand embroidery, Mabua explores themes such as human relationships, belonging, and identity.His portraiture, defined by meticulous pointillism, infuses each dot with emotion and memory, making every piece personal and intuitive. Mabua has exhibited in Botswana, Nigeria, South Africa, Israel, and France, and held prestigious residencies, including at the Bag Factory in Johannesburg (2021) and the Art Residency Center (A.R.C) in Botswana (2023). His open studio event, “Within, Without,” provided insights into his evolving artistic process.

item.title: Kwandiwa Diwati
item.description: Kwandiwa Dlwati, 30, lives and practises fine arts in Johannesburg, specialising in drawing, painting and collage. He studied art and design at Motheo TVET College in Bloemfontein and was a finalist in the New Breed Art Competition in 2022, winning a merit award. Thereafter he completed a one-year programme at the Artist Proof Studio, which selected him as a William Kentridge student funding bursary recipient.In 2023 he was selected as one of the artists to participate in the Open Studios Joburg event. In 2024, Dlwati won the bronze prize awarded at the Umsizi noPende exhibition held at Springs Art Gallery and was part of the RMB Talent Unlocked 2024 exhibition at the Art & About gallery.

item.title: Kyle Kheswa
item.description: Johannesburg-based professional skateboarder and artist Kyle Kheswa, born in 1996, stands as a dynamic force within South Africa’s contemporary urban landscape. Renowned for his effortless style on the board, Kheswa has built a strong reputation across both local and international skateboarding communities, serving as an influential figure for a new generation of street skaters.Beyond his athletic talent, Kheswa is an accomplished creative whose artistic practice seamlessly bridges fine art and skate culture. Drawing inspiration from the energy, architecture, and daily rhythms of Johannesburg, his work captures the vibrant subcultures that define modern South African youth identity. Through collaborations, visual art, and community initiatives, Kheswa continuously merges physical expression with artistic vision. By highlighting the intersection of street sport, design, and cultural commentary, he remains a key catalyst in expanding the footprint of South African skateboard culture on the global stage.

item.title: Kyra Papé Holz
item.description: BiographyKyra Papé Holz (b.1993) a South African artist, raised in Benoni, Johannesburg, focuses her practice on drawing, sculpture and printmaking. She is an abstract artist with a particular interest in materiality. She has a Master of Art in Fine Arts by Research (2018) as well as a Bachelor of Art in Fine Arts Degree from the University of Witwatersrand (2015).As the Robert Hodgins award winner (2014) she went on to jointly achieve the Top Achievers award in the Fourth-Year Fine Arts Department at the University of Witwatersrand (2015). She was a sculpture finalist in the PPC Imaginarium awards (2016) and was nominated by Artist Press for the Queen Sonja Print Award (2017) in Norway. Her sculpture was selected for the top 100 in the Absa Atelier, Give Art Light Exhibition (2018).In 2019 her work, Average (11.9 | 6), was purchased for the Modern Arts Projects collection. Later in 2019 she went on a six-week residency through the Southern African Foundation for Contemporary Art to Entabeni Farm in Knysna with artist Fatima Tayob Moosa. In 2020, she was a selected artist commissioned to make a work for Art Bank South Africa. Most recently Papé Holz was a selected artist for Sasol New Signatures – Expressions Unbound (2023).Throughout her studies and practice as an artist, she has participated in numerous group exhibitions and art fairs. She has had a Solo Exhibition, Transude, in completion of her Master of Art, Fine Art degree at The Point of Order, Johannesburg (March, 2018). Her work is included in a few collections: Modern Arts Projects in South Africa (Harrie Siertsema); Nedbank (Sandton); Investec (London); Art Bank of South Africa; Artist Press Collection (Donated a work during residency); Wits Art Museum (Donated work from two print making exchanges); as well as of several private collections.Artist StatementKyra Papé Holz is an abstract artist working with fluid mediums. She explores form and its disruption through drawing, painting, printmaking and sculpture. Her interests are in the boundaries or non-boundaries that are being pushed, destabilised, or contained. Her practice is a response to her personal, emotional, and physical material experiences.Her work shifted after experiencing traumatic losses and moved towards an exploration of peaceful chaos. While maintaining her exploration of disrupted boundaries, she also explores the ebb and flow of the human experience in an abstract way. Her practice is deeply rooted in the dichotomies of existence, in the fragility of change, and in the reality of impermanence.“If you tear the paper, the ship will sink” - alludes to the ideas of disruption, balance and fragility. It is human nature to crave a sense of understanding, whether the answers are accessible or not. In her capacity, Papé Holz tries to make sense of the chaos of life through her abstract artworks. In her process, she visualises control and repetition co-existing with fluid and free mark-making. Her work does not intend to display difference, rather she explores the blurring of the boundary.

item.title: Lady Skollie
item.description: Lady Skollie (AKA Laura Windvogel) is a feminist artist and activist based in Johannesburg, South Africa. She graduated with a degree in History of Art and Dutch Literature from the University of Cape Town in 2009. Filled with bold colour, god-like figures and suggestive fruits, Lady Skollie’s ink, watercolour and crayon paintings revolve around themes of gender, sex and the politics of lust, consumption, as well as her musings on identity.The artist’s work has been exhibited widely across South Africa, and at a number of international solo and group exhibitions and fairs. In 2017, along with Tschabalala Self and Abe Odedina, the artist contributed artwork for the stage design of a gala performance of The Children’s Monologues, a benefit held by the charitable organisation Dramatic Need, directed by Danny Boyle and held at Carnegie Hall in New York, NY, USA. She has been featured on BBC Africa and CNN International on African Voices, as well as on the BBC World Service’s online and radio series In the Studio. She was also included in the 2018 edition of OkayAfrica’s 100 Women, an annual list which honours women across 10 different fields for their achievements and influence.She was recognised with the 2019 Mbokodo Award for Art and Design, which honours the pioneering spirit of South African women advancing the arts.In 2019, Windvogel was commissioned to design the new R5 coin to commemorate 25 years of constitutional democracy in South Africa.SOLO EXHIBITIONS 2020 Bound, Everard Read, Cape Town, South Africa 2019 Good & Evil, Everard Read, Johannesburg, South Africa Weakest Link, Eastside Projects, Birmingham, UK 2017 Lust Politics, Tyburn Gallery, London, UK Fire with Fire, solo stand at FNB Joburg Art Fair, Johannesburg, South Africa Mating Dance, solo stand at AKAA Art Fair, Paris, France Hottentot $kollie, Tomorrows/Today, Investec Cape Town Art Fair, Cape Town, South Africa 2015 One-Night, WorldArt Gallery, Cape Town, South Africa 2015 Vroeg Ryp, Vroeg Vrot, RAMP Project, Stevenson Gallery, Johannesburg, South Africa 2014 Skattie Celebrates Series, Association for Visual Arts Gallery, Cape Town, South Africa SELECTED GROUP EXHIBITIONS 2020 Against Interpretation, Everard Read, London, UK Staring Straight to the Future, online exhibition, Everard Read, South Africa & UK Masterpiece online, with Everard Read, London, UK 2019 CONTEXT Art Miami, with Everard Read, Miami, USA 2018 Old Masters / New Realities: Gerard Sekoto x Lady Skollie, TMRW Gallery, Johannesburg, South Africa This Is the Gallery and the Gallery Is Many Things X at Eastside Projects, Birmingham, UK Close: Proximity, Intimacy, Tension, Johannesburg Art Gallery, Johannesburg, South Africa Right at the Equator, Depart Foundation, Malibu, CA, USA Investec Cape Town Art Fair, with Tyburn Gallery, Cape Town, South Africa 2016 1:54 Fair, with Tyburn Gallery, London, UK SEX, Stevenson Gallery, Johannesburg, South Africa

item.title: Larry Otoo
item.description: Ghanaian artist Larry Otoo presents a new series of paintings in this exhibition that are proof of his ever-ascending curve. Holder of a Master's Degree in African Art and Comparative Literature from the prestigious "Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology" in Kumasi, Ghana, Otoo has participated in exhibitions and residencies around the world and today is considered one of the most famous painters from his country. Otoo's works have been presented in Ghana, Spain, and in prestigious institutions in the United States, Denmark, The Netherlands, Ivory Coast, Italy, Canada and Germany, and some can be found in public collections as far away as Japan.This does not disturb the life or the creativity of the artist, who traces his path with constants, revealing an infinity of variables. As Otoo himself explains, “All paintings have three things in common. First, they are dedicated to the human being; second, I only use tones derived from a limited number of primary colours that sometimes break down into secondary colours. This is my specialty as a painter. Third, they are all paintings of an unusual style.” From the market scenes he is famous for, to the most unusual portraits of women, Otoo’s work comes from an alchemy that only its author understands.One of the characteristics of Larry Otoo is that he has chosen to only work with the three primary colors: red, yellow and blue, which he uses most often in their pure state, without nuances or mixtures. This gives an obvious visual power to Otoo's works that easily identifies him as the author. We could expect some form of fatigue, from the systematic impact of pure colour, but the artist's talent makes it possible to ensure that this is not the case and that he does not tire of discovering the different forms and combinations that his works take in a multitude of variants.

item.title: Laura de Harde
item.description: Dr Laura de Harde is a Postdoctoral Fellow at the University of Pretoria. In 2019 De Harde completed her PhD in the discipline of History of Art at the University of the Witwatersrand which marked the culmination of five years of cross-continental research in archives and museums in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Germany. Laura’s research required trekking through the southern African landscape in search of rock art shelters and other remote locales and, since completing her PhD, Laura is extending the predominantly text-based research of her thesis and combining it with her own artistic practice. Over the course of her Postdoctoral Fellowship, Laura will be exploring archival materials, including but not limited to, the University of Pretoria archives, with a specific interest in the role women occupy/occupied in research. Her two-year Fellowship will culminate in a solo exhibition.During my Doctoral studies, I immersed myself in an archive of hand-painted copies of rock paintings produced, by the artist-researcher Elizabeth Goodall, from the 1930s until her death in 1971. The archive, housed in Zimbabwe, presented a largely untapped resource of visual information pertaining to Southern African rock art. While conducting my research I used the insights, gathered as a practicing artist, to examine and illuminate the often-illusive processes involved in creating rock art reproductions. Over this time, I also developed a keen interest in the relationship between creative/ artistic practice and scientific research. Since completing my PhD in 2019 I have been using my artistic practice to further develop and explore themes unearthed over the course of my studies. Through a visual engagement with archival materials and ‘women’s work’, I consider the presence of women in archives and historical documents and employ thread to further probe and disrupt the art/craft divide.

item.title: Lawrence Meju
item.description: Lawrence Meju is an artist based in Lagos, Nigeria. His work is consistently experimental with technique, creating unimagined worlds and people by portraying his subjects in intimate, meditative, and surreal spaces. His works have recently been featured in the London Adidas flagship Store in 2022

item.title: Layo Bright
item.description: Layo Bright (b. 1991 in Lagos, NG) received her LL.B from Babcock University, Ogun State, NG and MFA in Fine Art from the Parsons School of Design, New York, NY, US. The artist's first solo museum exhibition Dawn and Dusk will be on view at The Aldrich Contemporary Art Museum, Ridgefield, CT, US since April 2024.Brights works have been also featured in solo and duo exhibitions at Monique Meloche Gallery, Chicago, IL, US; Flux Factory, Long Island City, NY, US, and AWCA, Lagos, NG. The artist participated at numerous group exhibitions, including at Bemis Center for Contemporary Arts, Omaha, NE, US; Halsey McKay Gallery, New York, NY, US; Museum of Glass, Tacoma, WA, US; PM/AM Gallery, London, UK; Johnson Lowe Gallery, Atlanta, GA, US; Lubeznik Center for the Arts, IN, US; Sean Kelly Gallery, New York, NY, US; Bode, Berlin, DE; Welancora Gallery, Brooklyn, NY, US; Anthony Gallery, IL, US, among others. Bright completed an art residency at Museum of Glas, Tacoma, WA, US; UrbanGlass, Brooklyn, NY, US; Tyler Glass Program, Philadelphia, PA, US; and has been selected for Ron Desmett Award Residency 2024, Pittsburgh Glass Center, Pittsburgh, PA, US.The artist is the recipient of numerous honors and awards including the Ron Desmett Award (2023), UrbanGlass Winter Scholarship Award (2021, 2020); and the Beyoncé Formation Finalist Scholarship (2017). Layo Bright lives and works in New York, NY, US.

item.title: Lawrence Lemaoana
item.description: Lawrence Lemaoana is an artist with a Bachelor of Fine Art from the University of Johannesburg. He currently lives and works in Johannesburg, South Africa. He is currently reading for a masters degree at the University of South Africas Art History, Visual Arts & Musicology Department, where he is also a junior lecturer in Visual Art. His body of work has, as its departure, a fascination with the role of the mass media in present-day South Africa.
