item.description: Jacob van Schalkwyk (b. 1979, Cape Town) holds a BFA in Drawing from the Pratt Institute in Brooklyn, New York and a MAVA in Sculpture from the University of Stellenbosch, South Africa.His career incorporating painting, drawing, performance, installation and writing has taken his work to the REDCAT Theater in Los Angeles, The Detroit Institute of the Arts, MassMoCA, the BAM Next Wave Festival, Central Park Summerstage, Irving Plaza, The Standard Bank National Arts Festival, The Centre for the Less Good Idea in Johannesburg, De Singel Arts Centre in Antwerp, The Briggait Gallery in Glasgow, The Edinburgh International Fashion Festival and the Salle Jacques Brell in Paris. His visual art has been included in the Neuberg Museum Collection, NY, the König Buro in Zurich, the South African Reserve Bank collection and the Nando’s/Hollard/Spier collections. The Alibi Club, his 2014 debut novel, was published in both Afrikaans and English versions by Umuzi/Random House to critical acclaim.He taught Drawing and Painting at Stellenbosch University between 2016 and 2024, briefly serving as Head of the Fine Arts Department. Van Schalkwyk is a PhD candidate at the University of Pretoria, where he is the recipient of the UP Postgraduate Research Grant. His practice-led research engages with new knowledge obtained from archive detailing significant African contributions to the conceptual basis of gestural abstraction in 1940’s New York City. Van Schalkwyk has been represented by GALLERY AOP and David Krut Projects in Johannesburg and Suburbia Contemporary gallery in Barcelona.

item.title: Jasirah Sayed
item.description: Jasirah Sayed is a fine artist working in printmaking and photography, exploring themes of space, home, and identity. Rooted in personal experience, her practice reflects on how physical and emotional environments shape belonging, particularly through the lens of a young woman growing up in the Western world.Her series Thresholds of Being: Between Home and Horizon examines “home” as both a physical and emotional landscape shaped by memory, transformation, and renewal. Inspired by the geometry of the Charbagh, the traditional Persian garden, the prints layer collaged photographs and geometric forms to mirror life’s cyclical rhythms. Through this work, Sayed reimagines home as a shifting archive of experience – an evolving threshold between self, place, and possibility.

item.title: Jayshal Gajjar
item.description: Jayshal Gajjar (b. 1999) is an emerging Cape Town-born contemporary artist and Visual Arts educator whose practice explores the intersection of everyday life and imagination. Moving fluidly across painting, drawing, sculpture, and textile work, Gajjar treats the studio as a playful yet deeply evocative space to reflect on routine, emotion, and visual wonder. She earned her Bachelor in Contemporary Art at The Creative Academy in 2020 and subsequently obtained a Postgraduate Certificate in Education (PGCE) in Senior Phase Creative Arts and FET Visual Arts in 2022.Her dual role as an artist and educator fuels her commitment to leveraging the transformative power of creativity to foster self-expression, inclusive learning, and spaces of shared belonging. Gajjar’s quirky, whimsical visual language leans toward a romanticism of the mundane. Her multi-layered mixed-media series celebrate ordinary tasks, daily domestic rituals, and quiet moments of intimacy—be it romantic or platonic—while effortlessly venturing into fantasy and speculative possibility. A keen observer of the human experience, she draws thematic inspiration from childhood nostalgia, imaginary worlds, and iconic Bollywood woman characters and their complex representations of love. Combining humor, a striking sense of color, and a distinct love of animals, Gajjar pairs spontaneous storytelling with an individual, highly recognizable aesthetic that often borders on the playful or the intentionally kitsch.Her innovative visual voice has rapidly built a strong presence within both local and international contemporary art circuits. In South Africa, her distinct narrative works were selected for the curated GIRLS GIRLS GIRLS exhibition at DAOR Contemporary Art Gallery in honor of Women’s Month.

item.title: Jeannette Unite
item.description: Jeannette Unite is a visual artist who is immersed in the materiality of the art making process whether it is using her own large hand-made chalk-based pastels with mineral oxides or using similar metal oxides in glass artworks, paintings or prints. She uses images, information and metaphors from mining as a point of departure for her reflections on her own personal journeys.She travels to mining and industrial sites for samples, to research and photographically record evidence of the residual remains of power, industrialisation and neo-colonialism on the African landscape. She studied towards a BA Fine Art at the Michaelis School of Art, University of Cape Town from 1981 until 1986, and studied further at UNISA while teaching at Frank Joubert Art Centre until demand for her artwork propelled her into full time art practice in 1997. She continues to live and work in, and travel from her studio in Cape Town.

item.title: Joao Ladeira
item.description: João Ladeira is a contemporary artist whose practice explores themes of migration, displacement, and identity within the context of Africa’s socio-political and economic realities. Through expressive compositions that blend drawing, painting, and collage, Ladeira humanizes the experiences of migrants and refugees, reflecting on the tragedies and resilience of those crossing the Mediterranean in search of safety.His use of African batiks within postcolonial narratives reclaims symbols of trade and colonialism as emblems of cultural pride and renewal. Engaging with the complexities of globalization, history, and representation, Ladeira’s work serves as both a memorial and a call for empathy—giving face to the faceless and voice to the voiceless.

item.title: Kelly Fortuin
item.description: Kelly Fortuin is a South African artist and designer from Tafelsig, Mitchells Plain. Working across photography, collage, and digital manipulation, her practice explores memory, place, and belonging, transforming familiar landscapes into layered, vibrant, and unsettled reflections of home.Fortuin’s work reinterprets ordinary suburban scenes, layering colour and texture to evoke the shifting nature of memory, identity, and community. Trained at Cedar Secondary High School of Arts, Spier Arts Academy (mosaic apprenticeship, Cum Laude, 2019), and the School of Explorative Architecture, she combines artistic and architectural approaches to explore urban landscapes, techno-pastoralism, and hybrid methodologies blending hand drawing with digital rendering.

item.title: Kieron Jina
item.description: Kieron Jina is a multidisciplinary artist, performance maker, and cultural provocateur whose creative practice spans live performance, visual collage, body art, and sound design. Rooted deeply in performance and ritual, Jina critically examines concepts of belonging, identity, and social power through ongoing inquiries into place, deliberately shifting focus from "Where are you from?" to "Where do you belong?" Their multidisciplinary practice weaves Afrofuturism, queer identity, global migration, and Indigenous knowledge systems into immersive, sensory experiences that challenge traditional artistic boundaries while exploring the fluid connection between the physical body and the surrounding environment.Holding master’s degrees from Wits University in Johannesburg and the Academy of Fine Arts Nuremberg in Germany, Jina has showcased work globally across international festivals, artist residencies, and gallery spaces. Their practice continually resonates with ancestral memory and radical imagination, actively cultivating transformative, inclusive spaces dedicated to profound human connection, creative empowerment, critical dialogue, and collective liberation.

item.title: Kimberly Bednall
item.description: Kimberley Bednall, born in Cape Town, studied Interior Design at CPUT before pursuing Set Design at RADA in London. Returning home, she continues to draw inspiration from the vibrancy of South Africa and the beauty of Cape Town’s landscapes.While earlier works explored the shifting hues of the coastline, her current series turns inland, capturing the rocky hills and delicate resilience of fynbos. Working with charcoal and chalk pastel on 300gsm paper, each piece is mounted over neutral linen with a shadow gap and framed in a white bevelled box, emphasising texture, movement, and a profound sense of place.

item.title: Kimshay Philander
item.description: Kimshay Philander is an early-career visual artist whose creative practice centres on storytelling through layered symbolic meanings, emotional depth, and subtle narrative resonance. While working across traditional and mixed media, photography serves as her primary medium, enabling her to capture intangible nuances of human existence and transform them into evocative visual narratives. Her deliberate approach pays meticulous attention to light, atmosphere, and spatial composition, turning fleeting moments into enduring reflections on lived reality.Philander’s work deeply explores how geographical places become rich repositories of human experience, examining the concept of home as both a quiet witness to personal memory and a dynamic site of shared social histories. Through sensitive imagery of parks, alleyways, and ordinary urban environments, she reflects on the profound ways surrounding landscapes shape personal identity, collective memory, and spatial belonging, inviting viewers to discover emotional resonance within everyday surroundings.

item.title: Kpingni Maureen Douabou
item.description: Kpingni Maureen (1990, Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire) is a visual artist, writer and curator found between the city center of Abidjan, the outskirts of Paris and other territories that fuel her practice. She draws on her Ivorian heritage and the legacy of black feminist thinkers and artists from Africa and its diaspora to shed light on the past, give birth to alternative narratives, question culture and weave new dialogues.Through figurative representations block women’s bodies -often her own- Kpingni Maureen seeks to highlight the multiple layers of black femininity across geographies and realities. She understands eroticism and sensuality as spiritual power and a tool for healing, and she explores depiction of the body as a powerful site of resistance, remembrance, pleasure, and transformation. Kpingni-Maureen is a multi-faceted, self-taught cultural practitioner.She expands her visual narratives into interdisciplinary realms, weaving together stories of collective memory, recovery, and the importance of community. Her practice of storytelling also takes the form of a monthly newsletter and a multilingual collaborative pan-African magazine on arts and culture.She has exhibited her work and participated in culural mediation programmes in the United States, France, Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana. She is a recipient of the 2025 Prince Claus Seed award.

item.title: Kyle Glendinning
item.description: Cape Town-based artist Kyle Glendinning examines the intersection of engineering, architecture, and human ambition. Centered on the concept of “engineered vulnerability,” his practice transforms iconic infrastructure into intricate paper and mixed-media sculptures, revealing how monumental feats of engineering simultaneously bridge communities and embody inherent fragility.Through meticulous paper engineering integrated with wood, thread, and steel, Glendinning reinterprets massive physical structures as delicate frameworks. In works like “The Expanse” a 1,640mm paper model of France’s Millau Viaduct, he translates grand architectural scales into intimate, precarious forms.By scaling down these monuments, Glendinning challenges the illusion of permanent stability that often surrounds human progress. His detailed constructions probe how physical structures shape collective memory, define a sense of place, and frame our ongoing understanding of human achievement. The resulting works invite viewers to reflect on both the grand ambitions driving civil engineering and the underlying vulnerability of our constructed world.

item.title: Lamont Khoza
item.description: Lamont Khoza is a self-taught documentary photographer whose practice explores Black working-class life through intimate portraiture. Working primarily with 35mm and 120mm film, he handprints his photographs and experiments with co-creation, inviting subjects to press the shutter themselves. This approach challenges conventional ideas of authorship, agency, and representation. Influenced by Dawoud Bey, Cherono Ng’ok, and Roy DeCarava, Khoza seeks to capture dignity, empathy, and authenticity within his community. Since relocating to Cape Town in 2022, his work has been featured in PhotoVogue’s Best Selection of the Month. He continues to refine his darkroom practice, exploring photography as a collaborative process rooted in human connection.

item.title: Lona Ndzimande
item.description: Lona Ndzimande's artistic practice deeply explores the multi-faceted realities of Black womanhood through the specific lens of her Zulu upbringing. Using a diverse array of mixed media—including acrylic, Zulu glass beads, rich fabric, pearls, papier-mâché, and paper collage—she creates deeply layered portraits that celebrate Blackness, femininity, and individual self-expression. Simultaneously, her work actively interrogates rigid societal expectations and the constraints of purity culture.Ndzimande’s striking art beautifully balances intimacy, defiance, and joy. She incorporates rich textures, draped beads, and dimensional sculptural elements to highlight personal resilience, sensuality, and the true complexity of identity. Through this bold visual language, she builds vital archives of Black femininity that deeply honour historical tradition while critically engaging with contemporary life.

item.title: Lungiswa Gqunta
item.description: Lungiswa Gqunta (b. 1990, Gqeberha, South Africa) is an acclaimed contemporary multidisciplinary visual artist and educator whose powerful practice spans site-specific installation, sculpture, printmaking, and performance. Gqunta holds a Bachelor of Fine Arts from Nelson Mandela University (2012) and a Master of Fine Arts from the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town (2017). Her deeply researched studio practice intensely interrogates the complex dynamics of spatial exclusion, historical land dispossession, and the violent, lingering legacies of colonialism and patriarchy in post-apartheid South Africa.Gqunta is celebrated for her deliberate use of ordinary, domestic everyday materials that are heavily charged with political, economic, and psychological meaning. By transforming objects like wooden bed frames, broken beer bottles, paraffin lamps, rusted nails, and razor wire into immersive installations, she exposes the invisible architectural barriers that dictate displacement and segregation. Her work reimagines these common items as weapons of resistance, reclaiming sacred space and actively challenging systemic inequalities rooted in race, class, labour, and gender.As a co-founder of the historic Cape Town-based iQhiya Collective—a network dedicated to elevating Black female voices—Gqunta has achieved massive international visibility. She has held solo exhibitions at prominent global institutions, including the Henry Moore Institute in Leeds and the Zwirner Gallery in London. Her striking installations have also been featured in major international biennales, such as the Istanbul Biennial and Manifesta 12 in Palermo, cementing her reputation as an essential voice exploring structural trauma and spiritual healing.

item.title: Mahilet Afework
item.description: Mahilet Afework is a painter whose artistic practice explores the intricate landscapes of memory, childhood, and emotional recall. Her compelling series, Frozen Moments, draws from old family photographs and imagined recollections to construct intimate portraits. These works reflect both profound safety and a subtle distance, capturing memories felt far more than remembered.Through the thoughtful use of symbolism, familiar everyday items, and rich tactile texture, Mahilet creates visual spaces that speak to the emotional labor of remembering. Her practice continually questions how the past lives within us—not merely through sequential narrative, but in atmosphere, quiet gesture, and poignant absence.In her project The Weight of Soft Things, her work reclaims the personal archive as a vital and valid visual language for emotional life. Ultimately, Mahilet's canvases invite viewers to reflect on their own relationship with time, longing, and personal heritage.

item.title: Maitemogelo Diphetogo Mphela
item.description: Maitemogelo Diphetogo Mphela is a South African artist working primarily in abstraction and mixed media. Her evocative paintings deeply explore themes of belonging, displacement, and memory through rich earthy tones, multi-layered textures, and intimate fragments of text. By embedding personal affirmations and organic traces of handwriting directly onto her canvases, she transforms private, interior reflections into tangible visual forms.Mphela’s dynamic practice continuously investigates the shifting sense of home—framing it as a space that is simultaneously deeply personal and transient. She brings these ideas to life using a versatile combination of acrylic, oil pastels, and mixed materials on both canvas and MDF board.Through her recent exhibitions and active studio collaborations, Mphela has established herself as one of South Africa’s most promising emerging artistic voices, making vital contributions to contemporary conversations surrounding identity and modern abstract art.

item.title: Marco Benz
item.description: Marco Mbenza (b. 1997, South Africa) is a South African-born, Congolese photographer and visual artist based in Johannesburg. After studying at the University of Johannesburg, he began his career in film and media production, developing a strong visual language through directing and editing.His passion for storytelling soon pivoted to music videos, where he began collaborating with friends and quickly carved out a niche that blends bold visuals with authentic African culture. As Marco Benz, he has since built a distinctive brand across music videos, short documentaries, and experimental film, earning acclaim for vibrant, culturally resonant work that bridges continents. His practice into photography, Mbenza continues to explore identity, culture, and belonging through a cinematic lens, capturing the energy and emotion of contemporary African life.

item.title: MBadger
item.description: MBadger (b.1992) is a Ghanaian artist whose practice revolves around mythology, surrealism, and bold visual language as a means of communicating personal narrative. Drawing on a background in fashion and illustration, their work transforms intimate experiences into dreamscapes that explore identity, trauma, and transformation.Their education and professional experience span a BFA in Fashion Design from Savannah College of Art and Design (SCAD Atlanta) and collaborations with Vivienne Westwood, Studio 189, and Pat McGrath. MBadger’s debut solo exhibition In Relation to Light (2023) explored themes of limitation and self-discovery through the interplay of light and shadow, followed by participation in Echoes of Ghana (2023) and Take Your Place, Beloved (2024). Working across both traditional and digital media, MBadger crafts spaces where the bounds of reality are broken and reimagined, inviting vulnerability, healing, and renewal.

item.title: Mbulelo Terrence Lokoto
item.description: Mbulelo Terrence Lokoto (b. 2000) is a highly compelling Cape Town-based contemporary South African visual artist born in East London, Eastern Cape. Lokoto formalised his visual vocabulary at the Ruth Prowse School of Art, where he graduated with a Diploma in Fine Art specialising in painting. Though his passion for the arts sparked in early childhood, limited regional resources initially forced him to abandon the craft. Nearly two decades later, he returned to drawing and painting as a crucial therapeutic coping mechanism to navigate severe depression—an intimate act of healing that continues to infuse his canvases with raw psychological depth.

item.title: Melissa Knoesen
item.description: Here is an expanded 150-word version of the biography: Melissa Knoesen is a multidisciplinary artist working primarily with watercolour, ink, and ceramics. Guided by each medium’s inherent qualities, fluidity, texture, and organic unpredictability, she creates work that prioritises raw emotion over explicit narrative. Rather than prescribing a fixed story, Knoesen distils human expression to its absolute essence, crafting contemplative pieces that invite quiet reflection, stillness, and personal interpretation. Her practice is deeply rooted in a delicate balance between spontaneity and intention. Whether coaxing pigment across paper or shaping clay by hand, she allows the natural tensions of her materials to inform the final compositions. Through visual simplicity, subtle tonal shifts, and emotional sensitivity, her art communicates beyond language. Each piece acts as a quiet dialogue, encouraging moments of profound connection and introspection between the viewer and the artwork, offering an immersive space where stillness speaks volumes and subtle forms resonate deeply.

item.title: Milani Mtshotshisa
item.description: Milani Mtshotshisa is a South African visual storyteller whose practice spans photography, fashion, and community-focused work. Born and raised in the Eastern Cape, Mtshotshisa approaches the camera as both an artistic tool and a means of service, preserving memory, dignity, and the everyday realities that shape her community.Her work captures moments of quiet power – steaming pots, children at play, and landscapes framed through intimate perspectives – highlighting culture, survival, and belonging. Trained at the Durban University of Technology (National Diploma in Photography) and AFDA (Higher Certificate in Film, Entertainment, and Television), Mtshotshisa uses photography as a form of healing and dialogue, affirming resilience and giving voice to the often unseen.

item.title: Mozafar Ramadan
item.description: Mozafar Ramadan (b. Sudan) is a distinguished visual artist and writer whose multidisciplinary practice masterfully bridges fine art painting and the literary dimensions of narrative form. A 2007 graduate of the Painting Department at the College of Fine and Applied Arts, University of Sudan, Ramadan has cultivated an expansive practice centred on the semiotics of space, critically investigating how cultural and emotional meanings emerge from and shape diverse environments.Through this analytical lens, Ramadan examines the intricate relationship between the real and the imagined. He seamlessly weaves together visual elements and written texts to uncover the distinctive, evocative character of place. His compelling compositions invite viewers into a thoughtful contemplation of memory, geographic identity, and spatial perception. By synthesizing narrative storytelling with rich painterly techniques, Ramadan constructs immersive artwork that continuously probes how physical landscapes intersect with personal and collective human experience.

item.title: Mwamba Chikwemba
item.description: Mwamba Chikwemba born in Kitwe, Zambia in 1992 lives in Lusaka, Zambia. Coming from a Public Administration and IT background, Mwamba is a trained artists from the Schooling of the Council of Visual Artists in Zambia. She describes herself as a painter, street artist and print maker drawing inspiration from a combination of art movements like portrait and figurative art. Mwamba is influenced by artists like Geoffrey Phiri, Daut Makala, Agness Buya Yombwe, Frida Kahlo, Jenny Saville and Wycliffe Mundopa.In June 2016 she was selected as the artist of the year under German Embassy Lusaka, taking part in a number of local workshops on printmaking and painting. She has done several public murals in Lusaka, Livingstone, Kampala, Antananarivo to Johannesburg. Mwamba has also gone through schools of learning and residency at Modzi Arts (Zambia), Nafasi Art Space (Tanzania), Is’art Galerie (Madagascar) and Great More Studio (South Africa). She has been awarded the Push Women Award, winner of the Cynthia Zukas young artist award and been granted the Summer academy of fine arts in Austria, Salzburg on relief Printing and Pronto Plate Lithography.

item.title: Myra Brown
item.description: Myra Brown is a Cape Town–based photographic artist whose compelling work explores intimacy, identity, and sense of place through traditional darkroom techniques and analogue practices. Her celebrated series, Opaque Clarity, reflects deeply on queer relationships and the subtle emotional charge of everyday spaces, captured in a signature deadpan yet tender aesthetic style.Rooted in keen observation and visual curiosity since childhood, Brown’s images reveal profound vulnerability, authentic joy, and quiet resilience as a trans woman navigating life’s constantly shifting personal and social landscapes. Her photographs invite viewers into an intimate dialogue with memory, space, and belonging.A 2022 graduate of the Cape Town School of Photography, she continues to refine a nuanced visual language that seamlessly transforms deeply personal experience into universal reflection. Through her meticulous approach to darkroom printing and deliberate composition, Brown establishes herself as a distinctive voice in contemporary South African photography.

item.title: Narique Sangster
item.description: Narique Sangster is an emerging contemporary South African ceramic artist and visual researcher whose tactile, intuitive studio practice redefines the boundaries of modern clay work. Operating as a completely self-taught practitioner, Sangster works exclusively with handbuilding techniques, deliberately bypassing the mechanical uniformity of the potter’s wheel. Her freestyle approach to clay intentionally embraces imperfection, tactile asymmetry, and raw spontaneity. She allows each vessel to unfold naturally during the making process—a rhythm she describes as being directly akin to the improvisational energy, flow, and high-stakes vulnerability of a hip-hop cipher.Sangster’s multi-layered ceramic work serves as a deep meditation on freedom, radical honesty, and spatial belonging. Through the malleable DNA of raw earth, she actively reflects on her own Cape Coloured identity and the intricate, often fragmented complexities of cultural inheritance in post-apartheid South Africa. Her conceptual frameworks are heavily influenced by the core hip-hop philosophy of “knowledge of self”, as well as the boundless, speculative horizons of Black sci-fi and Afrofuturism. By merging these contemporary urban subcultures with ancient, raw coil and pinch-pot methods, she treats her hand-carved vessels as three-dimensional monuments to liberation, self-discovery, and ancestral resilience.

item.title: Natasha Carstens
item.description: Natasha Carstens is a contemporary South African visual artist, textile crafter, and visual researcher whose tactile studio practice explores humanity's intricate relationship with the natural world. Based in South Africa and represented on premier continental art platforms. Carstens has developed a highly distinctive, interdisciplinary visual language. Her work fluidly combines traditional weaving, detailed indigenous beadwork, and deeply textured surfaces to challenge the boundaries between fine art, handcraft, and ecological advocacy. By manipulating raw, organic elements alongside local textiles, her multi-layered surfaces act as living archives that celebrate the deep beauty of material texture while prompting critical reflections on human presence within fragile ecosystems.A central anchor in Carstens’ creative framework is a deep focus on water as both a physical form and a powerful spiritual metaphor. Through her flowing tapestries and intricate glass bead configurations, she masterfully translates the transient qualities of aquatic environments, invoking universal ideas of fluidity, reflection, vulnerability, and transformation. Her works reject passive domestic decoration; instead, they serve as visceral narratives documenting stories of regional ecology, environmental responsibility, and the urgent need to preserve our natural water systems in an era of climate precarity. Through this unique balance of ancient craft techniques and progressive contemporary thought, Carstens establishes herself as a vital, driving voice in modern South African textile art, inviting audiences to slow down and listen to the profound stories held within the materials of the earth.

item.title: Nerissa Brobbey
item.description: Nerissa Brobbey was born in Accra, Ghana to Ghanaian and Romanian parents. Nerissa started painting at the age of three years old when her father noticed her drawing constantly with the paper from his typewriter. She was the youngest art student enrolled at the Children's Club in Bucharest, Romania and, under the mentorship of Romanian artist Mariana Palea, she began painting in oil on canvas at the age of five.She has had exhibitions in Romania, Ghana and USA as a child and as a marketing student. Most recently she has exhibited at Nubuke Gallery (Accra, Ghana) and The World Bank Offices (Accra, Ghana).Nerissa studied Economics and French at Bates College, Maine, USA and International Marketing at Hult International Business School in Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA. While at Bates, she studied abroad in France, Scotland, Hungary, Turkey and the Czech Republic and during this time she also traveled to Canada, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Ireland, Spain, Belgium and Austria.She has continued to paint as a hobby. Upon the last count, there are about 400 works of art made by her at her residence.

item.title: Ngollo Mlengeya
item.description: Ngollo Mlengeya is a visual artist based in Arusha,Tanzania. Working primarily with mixed media, she creates textured artworks that draw inspiration from the rich tapestry of everyday life. Through her practice, Mlengeya seeks to explore the grand meanings that underlie our quotidian experiences. By incorporating diverse materials and techniques into her pieces, she crafts visually striking compositions that reflect the complexity and beauty of the human condition.Born and raised in Tanzania ,Mlengeya’s unique perspective is informed by her lived experiences in Tanzania. Yet her themes of connection, identity, and the search for meaning resonate with audiences from all walks of life. Through her multifaceted practice, she encourages a greater appreciation for the transformative power of art to illuminate the extraordinary within the ordinary. Ngollo mlengeya’s pieces can be found in private collections around the world. As she continues to push the boundaries of her medium, Mlengeya remains dedicated to creating art that celebrates the richness and complexity of the human experience.

item.title: Nic Human
item.description: Natasha Carstens is a South African contemporary artist whose practice explores the relationship between art, ecology, and the changing natural environment. Her recent body of work forms part of her PhD research at Durban University of Technology, where she investigates the Anthropocene and its implications for understanding humanity's impact on the planet. Through painting, Carstens contributes to broader ecological conversations, encouraging viewers to reflect on the interconnectedness of human activity, wildlife, and the environment.Her latest series comprises nine large-scale paintings depicting sea turtles along the KwaZulu-Natal coastline. These works draw attention to the vulnerability and resilience of marine life in an era characterised by environmental change. By focusing on these creatures and their coastal habitats, Carstens explores the consequences of human intervention while highlighting the importance of ecological awareness and conservation. The scale and subject matter of the paintings invite viewers to engage closely with the natural world and consider humanity's responsibility towards it.Through her research-driven artistic practice, Carstens brings scientific and environmental concerns into dialogue with visual expression. Her work positions painting as a means of examining contemporary ecological challenges, creating space for reflection on the delicate relationships that sustain life on Earth. Her artworks are available to discover and collect on Latitudes Online.

item.title: N’cho Jean-Louis
item.description: Jean-Louis N’cho (b. 1994, Yopougon), who operates creatively under the noble name Kpèhin, is an acclaimed contemporary Ivorian visual artist, photographer, and filmmaker. Currently based in France, N'cho’s multi-disciplinary studio practice fluidly bridges fine art street documentary, digital post-production, and conceptual portraiture. He began his photographic journey in 2016 as a tool for personal expression and a sanctuary to process emotional challenges. Lacking access to professional DSLR equipment, he initially photographed exclusively with his mobile phone, intentionally transforming this limitation into a core creative philosophy: that impactful storytelling is defined by the artist's vision rather than expensive tools.N'cho’s compelling visual style acts as a deliberate material bridge between ancestral heritage and modern daily life. His work explores the fluid textures of identity, grief, memory, and cultural continuity across the African continent. This spatial exploration is beautifully anchored in his celebrated photographic series, Les Abidjanais. Initiated in 2023 upon his return to Côte d'Ivoire for his father’s funeral, the project captures raw, spontaneous street scenes of Abidjan's overflowing energy. Back in his studio, N'cho reworks these snapshots by overlaying digital masks, traditional textiles, Akan cultural motifs, and Adinkra symbols to frame everyday citizens as carriers of historical and spiritual legacy.

item.title: Olivia Babel
item.description: Olivia Babel is a French artist specializing in fiber art, whose practice explores cartography and the concept of territory. A graduate of the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts de Lyon and the École Supérieure des Beaux-Arts d’Angers, she reimagines geographic representation through a deeply personal and multicultural lens shaped by her diverse heritage across Europe, Africa, Asia, and South America. Using traditional French savoir-faire and handwoven techniques, Babel crafts tactile landscapes that question humanity’s relationship with its environment. Her work has been exhibited internationally, including at Contextile (Portugal), the Biennial Objet Textile (France), and solo shows in Abu Dhabi and Dubai.

item.title: Ololade Lawal
item.description: Based in Lagos, Nigeria, Oloade Lawal is a visual artist who inquires' through lens-based mediums, abstract paintings and currently exploring an interdisciplinary practice. Her works mostly are personalized commentary on detachment, with situational evidence based on her lived experiences. .She studied Mass Communication at Yaba College of Technology. She has participated in both group exhibitions and Art fairs. She had her first solo show in 2023 and she features in Ake Review that same year. She is a Kuta Arts Residency Alumna and was recently a partiipant at G.A.S foundation Imora Arts Intensive Fellowship. .

item.title: Palesa Motheo
item.description: Palesa Motheo is a multimedia artist working in sculpture and painting whose practice draws on Sotho and Matebele heritage. She explores cultural memory, the matriarchive, and the intersections of tradition and modernity in post-colonial Southern Africa, investigating how histories are archived, erased, and reimagined.Her work engages with locality as a living archive, examining how streets, homes, and landscapes carry ancestral memory alongside contemporary negotiations of identity and belonging. Working in wood, stone, paint, and mixed media, Motheo creates sculptural and wall-based works that reference domestic and ritual objects, holding space for the interweaving of heritage, memory, and environment.

item.title: Pia Truscott
item.description: Pia Truscott is a Cape Town–based visual artist whose delicate blue drawings thoughtfully map the personal landscapes of memory, emotion, and place. Departing from traditional, clinical cartography, her inventive memory maps trace intimate geographies—capturing quiet, specific moments like a snake in the garden, a crooked cypress tree, or fallen avocados—that vividly evoke the sensory essence of the Karoo, the Cederberg, and Cape Town’s diverse natural surroundings.Rendered on an intimate scale, each postcard-sized work becomes an evocative love letter to place, skillfully blending nostalgia, observation, and playfulness. Through these intricate compositions, Truscott explores how dynamic environments shape our sense of identity, belonging, and connection to the world around us. Her practice invites viewers to reflect on their own physical and emotional landscapes, reconsidering how subtle everyday details and natural elements anchor our enduring personal histories.

item.title: Quinton Mawila
item.description: Born in Limpopo and raised in Gauteng, Quinton Mawila is a multidisciplinary artist working across photography and cinematography. His work explores individuality, healing, and the human experience, examining how identity is shaped through the body, memory, and lived experience. Through his lens, Mawila redefines vulnerability and strength as interconnected, creating visual narratives that celebrate humanity in all its diversity. He has exhibited with BCX, Kameraz at Open Window, and in group shows at the Open Window Institute.As an emerging artist, he continues to expand the language of lens-based storytelling, using his art as a meditative space for reflection, connection, and transformation.

item.title: Ribka Sisay
item.description: Ribka Sisay is a self-taught photographer and mixed-media artist whose practice grew out of a period of deep personal rupture. Originally a writer, she turned to photography during a time when depression made words feel unreachable. Through self-portraiture, weaving, and hand-stitching, Ribka began reconstructing her inner world—one image at a time.Her current body of work involves woven self-portraits, photographic prints that are physically cut, threaded, and sewn together. The result is both vulnerable and intricate: layered compositions that reflect a self in transition, fragmented but reassembling. Influenced by craft traditions and emotional survival, Ribka uses tactile processes to explore identity, isolation, and healing. In The Weight of Soft Things, her work becomes a kind of visual journaling, intimate and process-driven, inviting viewers to witness the often-invisible work of becoming whole.

item.title: Ricardo Akhona Pieterse
item.description: Ricardo Akhona Pieterse is a self-taught visual artist and photographer from Victoria West in South Africa’s Northern Cape. His landscape photography explores memory, heritage, and identity within the vastness of the Karoo. Drawing from his rural upbringing and family of creatives, Pieterse weaves storytelling and architectural motifs into his imagery. His practice captures the quiet poetics of rural life while situating local histories within a broader cultural context.

item.title: Roanna Tella
item.description: With each brushstroke, Roanna Tella maps the shifting terrain between emotion and memory, vulnerability and resilience. Rooted in introspection, her practice reimagines the human form through gestural abstraction, inviting us to witness how the body can carry both rest and rupture.In her newest body of work, Foreboding Tales, Roanna turns inward, tracing the delicate rituals that tether us to joy and grounding, even in the midst of uncertainty. Through the symbolism of plants and quiet daily gestures, she asks: how we hold beauty and distress in the same breath?Roanna holds a B.A in Visual Arts from the University of Lagos and has exhibited widely across Nigeria and internationally. Her evolving practice continues to deepen through mentorship and a commitment to emotional truth in visual form.

item.title: Rosalie Boka
item.description: Boka Amenan Rosalie was born in 1997, in Ouellé, Côte d’Ivoire. Her early discovery of her artistic talent led her to enroll in a high school for art training, and after graduating , she entered the Ecole Nationale des Beaux-Arts d'Abidjan, where she had the opportunity to benefit from the knowledge of several Ivorian masters and contemporary artists. Above all, she discovered her unconditional love for painting.Rosalie's works lie at the crossroads of dreams and memories, where roots become veins, and foliage becomes skies hiding timeless stories. By combining vibrant textures, dreamlike palettes, and organic forms, each painting transports us to a universe where nature becomes a living theater, inhabited by presences that are both familiar and elusive.

item.title: Ruth Getachew
item.description: Ruth Getachew is a collage and mixed-media artist whose work explores the emotional and energetic imprints we carry. A graduate of the Alle School of Fine Arts and Design, her practice is shaped by personal experiences with emotional burnout and a deep interest in quantum theory and vibrational healing.In her series, Ruth uses abstraction, color, and texture to reflect on how memory, media, and environment shape internal states. Her works function as emotional maps urging viewers to reflect on what they absorb and emit daily. In this exhibition, her collages challenge the notion that emotional life is peripheral, insisting instead that it forms the foundation of how we live.

item.title: Shadai Moonsamy
item.description: Shadai Moonsamy is a South African contemporary visual artist based in Durban. Working across painting, printmaking, and mixed media, she develops a multidisciplinary practice that explores the relationships between identity, memory, and urban life. Through her work, Moonsamy reflects on the experiences, environments, and personal histories that shape how individuals understand themselves and the spaces they inhabit.Her artistic approach is characterised by layered textures and expressive forms, which bring depth and complexity to her visual compositions. By combining different materials and techniques, Moonsamy creates works that invite viewers to look beyond the surface and consider the layers of meaning embedded within everyday experiences. Her exploration of memory and identity opens up questions about how personal histories intersect with the social and cultural environments in which they unfold.Drawing on the energy and complexity of urban life, Moonsamy’s practice considers the ways places influence perception, belonging, and self-expression. Her use of varied media allows her to approach these themes from multiple perspectives, creating a visual language that balances material experimentation with personal reflection. Through her evolving practice, she contributes to the diverse landscape of contemporary South African art.

item.title: Sheila Bayley
item.description: Sheila Bayley (b. 1986, Nairobi) was raised in a culturally diverse environment that continues to shape her artistic practice. Holding a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology from the United States International University–Africa, she is a self-taught artist whose work explores themes of identity, urbanization, and the delicate balance between nature and nurture in shaping human behavior.Working primarily with acrylic and paper collage on canvas—and on paper for her smaller pieces—Sheila draws inspiration from memory, personal experience, and poetry to create evocative compositions that invite viewers on an introspective journey of thought and emotion.In 2021, she was the guest artist at the Kobo Open Studio Art Sale & Exhibition in Nairobi. Two years later, she presented her first solo exhibition at Peponi Hotel in Lamu, followed by her first international duo show at Gallery Brulhart in Geneva, Switzerland. She has also participated twice in the Affordable Art Fair organized by the National Museum Society of Kenya. Her artworks are held in private collections locally and internationally, including in Zanzibar, the United States, France, the UAE, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Switzerland.Sheila is deeply committed to the growth and development of the East African art scene and envisions establishing an educational system that positions art as both a life skill and a viable career path. As her practice continues to evolve, she remains open to local and international collaborations, residencies, and exhibition opportunities.

item.title: Simphiwe Fuwe Molefe
item.description: Simphiwe Fuwe Molefe (b. 1990, Nquthu, KwaZulu-Natal) is a documentary and narrative photographer based in Katlehong, South Africa. He joined the Of Soul and Joy photography programme in 2019, where he was introduced to photography as a tool for storytelling and social reflection.Molefe’s work has since been widely exhibited as he recently presented his project Ungowakwethu wena in a group exhibition at the JSE,. In 2025, his photographs were featured in I Put My Hand on My Chest to Feel My Heartbeat at Constitution Hill, a milestone that led to coverage in the Mail & Guardian. In 2024, he exhibited at the Joburg FNB Art Fair.In 2023, he was named Global Citizen’s Emerging Creative of the Month, and he is also the recipient of the 17th Tierney Fellowship, one of South Africa’s most respected photography awards.His projects have appeared in numerous group exhibitions, including Through the Lens Collective (portrait exhibition), Uhambo at Umhlabathi Gallery, and in the Of Soul and Joy tenthanniversary book, where his project Dikarabo was published alongside the work of nine other South African photographers. A graduate of the Market Photo Workshop’s Advanced Photography Programme, Molefe continues to build a distinct voice within contemporary South African photography, exploring themes of identity, community, and lived experience.

item.title: Simphiwe Ndzube
item.description: Simphiwe Ndzube (b. 1990, Johannesburg, South Africa) is an acclaimed contemporary multidisciplinary artist whose visionary practice spans painting, low-relief collage, performance, and boundary-pushing installation sculpture. Ndzube formalised his creative education at the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town, graduating with a Bachelor of Fine Arts in 2015.His vivid, surreal worlds explore themes of agency, radical transformation, and the psychological weight of post-apartheid South Africa. Drawing heavily from African mythology, magical realism, and local folklore, Ndzube reimagines conventional narratives of identity and systemic power through dynamic, theatrical figures and landscapes. He currently splits his time, living and working between Los Angeles, California, and Cape Town.A defining hallmark of Ndzube's oeuvre is his ongoing construction of an expansive, mythological eco-system known as The Mine. Populated by a cast of gravity-defying, hybrid characters called The Echoes, this fictional universe serves as a deeply layered metaphorical space to examine the history of migrant labour, colonial exploitation, and the search for spiritual freedom.His paintings frequently burst past the edges of the traditional canvas frame, incorporating three-dimensional elements such as found clothing, second-hand ties, synthetic hair, and industrial gloves. By combining the high energy of South African Pantsula dance with the dramatic flair of Western boundary-pushing theatre, his figures capture a state of perpetual motion and morphing identity.Ndzube’s distinctive approach to Afro-surrealism has garnered massive global visibility and critical acclaim. He was awarded the prestigious Tollman Award for the Visual Arts in 2015 and has held major solo museum exhibitions worldwide, including Oracles of the Pink Universe at the Denver Art Museum and Like the Sun Departed at the CC Foundation in Shanghai. Represented by premier galleries including Stevenson and Nicodim, his works reside in esteemed permanent public collections, including the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA), the Rubell Museum in Miami, and the Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa (Zeitz MOCAA) in Cape Town.

item.title: Sina Sulger
item.description: Sina Sulger is a mixed-media artist whose practice combines MDF, acrylic paint, laser cutting, and vector design to create bold, graphic compositions. Originally from Germany and based in South Africa for nearly two decades, she draws inspiration from the vivid colours, distinctive character, and often-overlooked beauty of everyday local scenes. Her work captures moments that feel quintessentially South African, transforming familiar surroundings into vibrant visual interpretations of place and belonging.Drawing on her background in graphic design and special effects make-up, Sulger brings together technical precision and painterly expression. Her process balances the structured language of digital design with the spontaneity and richness of colour, resulting in works that are both carefully constructed and visually engaging. Through her art, she explores her relationship with South Africa as her adopted home, using everyday observations to reflect on identity, connection, and the experience of belonging. Each composition becomes a colourful tribute to the places and moments that have shaped her life and continue to inspire her practice.

item.title: Sipho Radebe
item.description: Sipho Radebe is a mixed-media artist whose practice explores memory, identity, and cultural inheritance. Working with traditional fabrics such as Umbhaco and Shwe Shwe, she combines acetone transfers, archival imagery, and layered materials to create tactile compositions that reflect on grief, remembrance, and continuity. Drawing on her AmaHlubi, isiXhosa, and Swati heritage, Radebe investigates the ways cultural traditions and personal histories shape our understanding of belonging.Her series Sunshine (2024) explores loss and renewal following the passing of her grandfather, using collage as a means of preserving memories and navigating the emotional complexities of grief. Through the interplay of fabric, image, and texture, she brings together fragments of personal experience and collective history, allowing the past to remain present while making space for transformation. Radebe holds a Fine Arts degree from the University of Cape Town and has completed internships at Circle Art Gallery in Nairobi and AVA Gallery in Cape Town. Her work positions belonging as an evolving dialogue between memory, heritage, and the present.

item.title: Stella Ekpe Samuel
item.description: Stella Ekpe Samuel is a multtidisciplinary artist based in Lagos, Nigeria. She holds a degree in Fine Arts and Design from the University of Port Harcourt, with a focus in painting. Her work explores themes of identity, womanhood, memory and personal storytelling, often using her own image as a central subject.Known for her rich textures and layered surfaces, Stella works with materials like paper, broken glass, and fabric to create emotionally charged, tactile paintings. Through personal experimentation, she develoed a unique texturing technique using paper, layering and maipulating it to create ripplie like effects that echo waves of thought and feeling.Her art reflects both quiet introspection nd cultural depth, drawing inspiration from everyday life and artists like Njideka Akunyili Crosby and Frida Kahlo. Stella has exhibited in several group shows, inculding October Rain at Gemini Gallery (2023), Artist Commune ot OneArtt Gallery (2024), and Plus234Art Fair in collaboration with Soto Gallery (2025). Her practice continues to evolve as she explores new ways to tell stories through material, form and emotion.

item.title: Sundus Saad
item.description: Sundus Saad is a Cape Town-based South African-Arab fibre artist specialising in on- and off-loom weaving. Her practice explores life, relationships, and interconnectedness through the tactile language of fibre. Using yarns of varying textures and colours, she creates expressive woven works that reflect her intuitive approach to material and form. Green features prominently in her palette, symbolising peace and prosperity.Guided by intuition and energy, Saad approaches weaving as a meditative and personal process, allowing each work to emerge organically from a state of calm. She embraces the relationship between material, process, and emotion, finding personal fulfilment in the act of making. While her practice is rooted in individual experience, her finished works are intended to be shared and appreciated by others. Through the textures, colours, and rhythms of her woven forms, Saad invites viewers to reflect on the connections that shape human experience, exploring the relationship between personal expression, emotional wellbeing, and a shared sense of belonging.

item.title: Tesfahun Kibru
item.description: Tesfahun Kibru, (b.1970) is a 2000 sculpture graduate of the Alle School of Fine Arts and Design, is a dedicated artist committed to a philosophy of complete immersion in art. Rejecting the ordinary, Kibru has consistently sought to express his unique artistic vision and individuality across all aspects of his life, resulting in a versatile and adaptable approach to creative challenges.For the past two decades, Kibru has worked as a full-time studio artist, transforming experience into wisdom and nurturing self-confidence as both a person and an artist. He has cultivated a distinct voice in contemporary Ethiopian art, marked by numerous solo and group exhibitions. A pivotal relationship with Asni Art Gallery served as a launching pad for his career, where he gained valuable exposure through solo shows, group exhibitions, and an artist residency.

item.title: Thando Salman
item.description: Thando Salman (b. 1997, Eastern Cape) is a highly compelling contemporary South African visual artist and storyteller currently based in Kempton Park, Johannesburg. Salman formalized his creative practice at the University of the Witwatersrand (Wits), graduating with a Bachelor of Fine Arts and earning the prestigious Anya Millman Scholarship for Artistic Excellence. His multi-media studio practice—spanning oil painting, mixed media, and complex installation—delves deeply into the lived realities, vulnerabilities, and contemporary coming-of-age experiences of Black youth in South Africa, with a particular focus on young men navigating urban and cultural environments.Operating through a visual framework that mirrors dark fairy tales and modern mythologies, Salman frequently positions his figures within isolated natural landscapes juxtaposed with beautiful yet poisonous flowers. This surreal layering acts as a bold critique of traditional macho culture and corporate rigidity. A landmark example includes his highly acclaimed 2025 solo presentation with BKhz Gallery at the RMB Latitudes Art Fair, titled Les Fleurs du Mal. Inspired by Charles Baudelaire's poetry, the exhibition features a curious cast of grown men dressed in colourful onesies wandering a strange forest, examining how adults struggle to engage with childhood imagination and vulnerability.

item.title: Themba Mwanza
item.description: Themba Mwanza (b. 1999) is a highly compelling Johannesburg-based contemporary South African multidisciplinary artist whose evocative studio practice explores the fluid boundaries of memory, nostalgia, and personal identity. Born in Mpumalanga, Mwanza formalised his visual vocabulary at the University of the Witwatersrand (Wits), where he graduated with a Bachelor of Fine Arts in 2020 and was awarded the prestigious Anya Millman Scholarship for Outstanding Work in Fine Art. His work operates as an intimate space of communication between his present and younger self, incorporating a distinct softness, curiosity, and playfulness rooted in childhood vision.During his undergraduate studies, Mwanza achieved sudden national recognition through a landmark collaboration between BMW South Africa and the Wits School of Arts. He designed his own iteration of the prestigious BMW Art Car series—a mixed-media installation on a classic E30 325i titled Mangobe Gado Gusheshe. Drawing heavy inspiration from his daily working-class commute on the Metrorail locomotive systems, the automotive piece was later acquired into BMW’s private art collection and exhibited at the NIROX Sculpture Park.

item.title: Themba Nhlapo
item.description: Themba Nhlapo’s work explores nostalgia, memory, and identity through painting, collage, and assemblage. After completing a Bachelor of Fine Arts at the University of Pretoria (2023), Nhlapo developed a practice that examines how objects – family photos, drawings, or heirlooms – carry the emotional weight of Black queer experience. Their recent series, created after returning to their childhood home, evokes the innocence and joy of youth through naïve drawings and symbolic motifs like the red speckled bean. Blending personal history with collective memory, Nhlapo’s art transforms ordinary materials into poetic meditations on resilience, belonging, and the fluidity of self.

item.title: Theresia
item.description: ,p>Theresia is a self-taught emerging artist from Tanzania whose expressive paintings draw inspiration from everyday life, African traditions, and personal experience. Her passion for art began in childhood, influenced by cartoons and local newspaper illustrations, and was reignited during her medical training amid the COVID-19 lockdown. Working primarily with acrylics—while also exploring oil pastels, charcoal, and graphite—Theresia’s art celebrates beauty, emotion, and colour.Influenced by Jean-Michel Basquiat and Henri Matisse, she experiments with diverse styles to create vibrant, reflective works. She has exhibited widely, including at Rangi Gallery, Nafasi Art Space, and DARCH (Old Boma), where she held her first solo show in 2023.

item.title: Turakella Editha Gyindo (Tura)
item.description: Turakella Editha Leonard Gyindo (Tura) is a Tanzanian artist and curator whose multidisciplinary practice spans painting, performance, video, and installation. Her work examines human adaptability in a rapidly changing world, challenging colonial and societal constructs around identity, intersectionality, and belonging. With a background in Chemical and Processing Engineering from Université de Badji Mokhtar in Algeria, Tura transitioned into the arts and completed the Curatorial Practices and Art Management Program at Nafasi Art Space Academy in 2021.She later founded Deja Vu Studios, an experimental platform for artistic research and collaboration. Her work has been featured in the East Africa Biennale (2021), FNB Art Joburg, and a solo exhibition at Alliance Française in Dar es Salaam (2024).

item.title: Valerie Asiimwe Amani
item.description: Valerie Asiimwe Amani is a Tanzanian artist and writer whose anti-disciplinary practice investigates the relationship between body, language, and myth; exploring how they shape belonging, memory, and collective imagination.Drawing from personal contemporary experiences, feminist theory, and spiritual ecologies, Amani explores the permeable boundaries between the political, domestic, and intimate. She has exhibited internationally, with presentations in Lagos, New York, Paris, Cape Town, London, Leipzig, Zanzibar, and Dar es Salaam. Recent exhibitions include Immortal Apples, Eternal Eggs at Hastings Contemporary and Amani: Kukita Kungoa at Museen Stade, Germany.She is the 2023 Foundwork Art Prize Honouree and a 2022 Ingram Prize winner. Her work has appeared in Art Monthly, Hyperallergic, and Texte zur Kunst. Amani is currently based in Oxford, where she is pursuing a practice-led DPhil in Fine Art at The Ruskin School of Art, University of Oxford.

item.title: Van Andréa
item.description: Van Andréa is a Congolese (Congo-Brazzaville) painter and sculptor. He graduated from the Ecole Nationale des Beaux-Arts in Brazzaville, where for his final examination he presented works based on the world of the "sapeurs" from his Bacongo neighborhood.These pieces, made with papier-mâché on canvas and as sculptures, were titled "Sape Art and the Sapeurs of Brazzaville." This led to his first national solo exhibition at Ateliers Sahm in 2013, titled "Smoke Without Fire." A year later, he won first prize at the second edition of RIAC in Brazzaville, earning him a creative residency at the Blachère Foundation in France. His first international solo exhibition took place in Switzerland, at Gasteateliers Krone Aarau in 2015. Beginning in 2019, Van Andréa began revisiting masterpieces from the Italian Renaissance, reinterpreting them based on the inspiration each one evoked. From Caravaggio’s "The Cardsharps," retitled "Damoiseau," to Lucien Melingue’s "The Provost of Merchants Étienne Marcel and the Dauphin Charles," renamed "The Bourgeoises," his new collection, titled "Renaissance," explores the theme: Corruption of Morals. The use of Ankara fabric for the headscarves of his female figures remains his artistic signature. These women, with their carefully tied headwraps, reflect the artist’s admiration for his grandmother. Van Andréa has emerged through a remarkable journey that can be summarized as follows: Initially introduced to the Congolese public at Ateliers Sahm in 2013 with a solo exhibition, he went on to win the second edition of the International Contemporary Art Meeting (RIAC), which led to his participation in the Dakar Biennale in Senegal in 2014.

item.title: Vita Malulu
item.description: Vita Malulu, born in Kabila village, Magu district, Mwanza, Tanzania, is a multidisciplinary artist working in painting, sculpture, and ceramics. From childhood, he was inspired by his surroundings and the expressive sketches of a local mute herder, which sparked his lifelong passion for visual storytelling. After training at Bagamoyo College of Arts (TASUBA, 2003–2006) and engaging with artist collectives such as Nafasi Art Space and 14+ Artists, Malulu has developed a practice that blends traditional techniques with experimental forms, often using recycled and found materials. His work interrogates social and political realities, highlighting the struggles and resilience of marginalized communities in Tanzania and beyond. Malulu’s art is both a reflection of personal memory and a dialogue with broader society.Through painting, sculpture, and music, he explores themes of inequality, labor, and the human experience, creating works that resonate locally and internationally. His exhibitions and residencies across Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda, Sweden, and Norway have further shaped his vision of art as a transformative and communal practice. Today, he continues to produce work that challenges, provokes, and inspires, using creativity to give voice to those often overlooked while fostering engagement and reflection through his installations and performances.

item.title: Waleed Mohammed
item.description: Waleed Mohammed (Wamo) (b. 2000, Khartoum, Sudan) is a Sudanese visual artist based in Nairobi, Kenya. His work explores memory, migration, and identity through reimagined archival photographs and layered materiality. Deeply influenced by Sudanese heritage and the evolving narratives of displacement, Waleed’s practice engages with vintage studio portraits and photographs from the 1950s–70s, recontextualizing them through contemporary textures and color palettes to bridge generations and geographies, combines painting, mixed media, and cotton yarns to transform personal and collective memories into a contemporary visual language that questions belonging, absence, and cultural continuity.He holds a Bachelor’s degree in Fine and Applied Arts from Sudan University of Science and Technology. Since his first solo exhibition in 2022 in Khartoum, his work has been presented in various group exhibitions across Sudan, Spain, Germany, Portugal, the United States, Kenya and Egypt. In 2024, he was awarded the MRI Fund for Artists Under Risk by the Goethe-Institut in Nairobi, Waleed works from his studio in Nairobi, where he is also co-founding a Sudanese art collective with fellow artists to foster artistic exchange and community engagement.

item.title: William Joseph Kachinjika
item.description: William Joseph Kachinjika is a Harare-based artist working with textiles and found materials to explore memory, hybridity, and the transformative power of objects. Inspired by childhood lessons in basket weaving from his grandmother, he creates large-format woven pieces from rope, cables, and mutton cloth, bridging indigenous craft and contemporary practice.His series Country Game Game reflects on Zimbabwe’s power crisis, resilience, and history, drawing on a childhood game that combines geography, culture, and play. Kachinjika trained at the School of Visual Art and Design, National Gallery of Zimbabwe, and continues his practice at Mbare Art Space under mentorship from Moffat Takadiwa and others.

item.title: Zimkhitha Tshaka
item.description: Zimkhitha Tshaka’s practice uses drawing and printmaking to document the emotional realities of the workplace. Inspired by Eartha Kitt’s remark, “I have no dream job; I do not dream of labour,” her work challenges societal attitudes toward work and questions the hierarchies that define productivity. Using oil and soft pastels on Fabriano, Tshaka foregrounds the overlooked experiences of the working class – their joys, frustrations, and aspirations – bringing their humanity to the forefront. A 2022 Bachelor of Visual Arts graduate from Nelson Mandela University, her art reimagines labour as a site of dignity and shared experience.

item.title: Emma Thompson
item.description: Emma Thompson is a contemporary South African visual artist and printmaker based in the Limpopo province. Her studio practice is deeply rooted in the meticulous, historically rich traditions of intaglio printmaking, specializing heavily in the medium of etching and fine-line drypoint. By pairing these traditional techniques with modern, fluid mixed-media applications—including hand-applied pigments, ink washes, and textile elements—Thompson creates multi-layered works on paper that investigate the raw textures, light, and changing ecological landscapes of her surrounding northern South African environment.Operating outside the traditional urban art hubs of Johannesburg and Cape Town, Thompson’s creative practice embraces the quietude and expansive geography of Limpopo. Her works act as an intimate dialogue with nature and memory, using the slow, acidic bite of the etching process as a metaphor for time and environmental transformation. Her distinctive mixed-media prints explore themes of domesticity, local flora, and geographical boundaries, carefully preserving fleeting moments and natural artifacts. Through her dedication to contemporary printmaking, Thompson has established a vital regional voice, contributing to group showcases and print portfolios that connect rural South African storytelling with broader national fine art dialogues.

item.title: Emma Wootton
item.description: Emma Wootton is an acclaimed contemporary South African multidisciplinary artist whose compelling practice is deeply rooted in the coastal landscapes of Cape Town. Born in 2002, Wootton’s unique approach to three-dimensional art is profoundly shaped by a lifelong fascination with fibre arts. This foundational passion drives her core focus on soft sculpture, manipulating textiles to explore themes of fragility, resilience, and emotional architecture. In 2024, she completed her formal training with distinction at the Michaelis School of Fine Art, where she successfully double-majored in sculpture and printmaking.Wootton's early career has been marked by significant institutional acclaim.She was named the co-recipient of the prestigious Michaelis Prize in 2024, following back-to-back honours as the winner of the Simon Gerson Prize in both 2023 and 2024. Conceptualised through monochrome, ghostly aesthetics, her larger body of work—including notable installations like Spectre and her solo show Whale Fall at Vela Projects—expertly subverts the doomist narratives of climate anxiety. By constructing tactile, hybridized creatures that blend organic animal forms with machinery, she visualises complex global tensions through a beautifully delicate and meticulously hand-crafted lens.

item.title: Maphoso George Mokwena
item.description: Maphoso George Mokwena is an emerging visual artist born in 1997 in Lephalale, Limpopo Province, South Africa. He graduated from Tielelo Secondary School in 2017 and was awarded a full bursary to study art by Elegant Fuel in 2020. In 2021, he enrolled at the Artist Proof Studio in Johannesburg to study printmaking.Mokwena’s body of work is deeply influenced by his journey between Lephalale & Johannesburg and make people to rethink how we measure worth by honouring both economic struggle and personal triumph rooted in family and resilience.He works with various media, including pen, charcoal, acrylic, digital and oil paint. Mokwena has participated in numerous group exhibitions and was featured in publications such as Art Times, Hyper Blog Magazine and Ntshabele Newspaper. In 2024, Mokwena travelled to Italy to paint 90metre long community memorial mural, in 2025 he completed internship in printmaking at Artist Proof Studio and practice as an artist and printmaker.

item.title: Michaele van den Heever
item.description: Michaele van den Heever (also known as Michaele Cooper) is a South African contemporary visual artist and operational strategist working primarily in monotype, drypoint etching, and print-based processes. Her minimalist, process-heavy practice explores faces, stark silhouettes, and deeply shadowed forms to navigate the intricate boundaries of human presence, sudden absence, and emotional visibility. Intimately drawn to the ideas of limitation, vulnerability, and imperfection, Van den Heever creates her work through a rigorous physical methodology of adding and removing ink from the plate, allowing calculated erosion, erasure, and creative restraint to shape each final image.Faces without eyes recur consistently throughout her practice, deliberately refusing direct engagement with the viewer to instead hold a profound sense of tension, internal quietness, and lingering ambiguity. Through an intentionally reduced palette, stark monochromatic tones, and an intuitive, tactile approach to ink on Hahnemühle and Fabriano paper, her striking print work acts as a visual journal reflecting inner psychological landscapes, shifting mental states, and the subtle marks left behind by lived experience.

item.title: Misa Boshoma Tinkie
item.description: Misa Boshoma Tinkie is a South African Artist, her art stems from a deeply personal journey and a desire to express the complex emotions of womanhood and social struggle. She explore the expectations placed on women and the silent battles they endure- between self-blame, judgment, and the search for freedom.Working mainly in printmaking, especially cyanotype, monotypes and linocuts, she embrace both control and unpredictability. The process often produces smudges or fading, symbolizing the fragility of emotions and the shifting nature of identity. Her recurring blue floral patterns, inspired by Chinese vase designs, represent how women are often valued like delicate objects-cherished until “cracked”, when their worth is questioned though their essence remains intact.Through her work, she challenge these perceptions and reclaim the authenticity pf womanhood. She aim to create a space where silenced emotions can be seen, shared, and understood-reflecting both her own experiences and those of countless others.

item.title: Mncedisi Mchunu
item.description: Mncedisi Mchunu is a visual artist from Soweto, Johannesburg. He began his formal artistic training at the renowned Artist Proof Studio in 2023. and is currently in his third and final year of study. Mchunu is recognized for his distinctive graphic, non-traditional drawing style, primarily realized through printmaking techniques including monotype, drypoint, linocut, and etching.His practice explores themes of mental health, emotional well-being, and personal experience, seeking to articulate the unconscious mind through symbolic and religious imagery. Drawing on intersectional identities, Mchunu’s work invites viewers to engage both intellectually and emotionally, fostering reflection and connection.

item.title: Moeketsi Motlhabe
item.description: Moeketsi Motlhabe (b. 2003, Centurion, South Africa) is a visual artist currently based in johannesburg. Born and bred in Pretoria, Motihabe developed a deep appreciation for the cultural and historical layers embedded within his surroundings. He completed his secondary education in 2020 and is currently pursuing a Bachelor of fine arts at the University of Johannesburg ,with a primary focus on printmaking. Motihabe's printmaking and drawing practice engages with the complex legacies of colonial architecture in South Africa-structures whose beauty and craftsmanship stand in stark contrast to histories of land dispossession, exploitation, and systemic oppression.Rooted in his identity as a Black South African descendant of the colonized, he navigates the tension between appreciating formal elegance and confronting the violent realities these buildings embody. Through the layered processes inherent to printmaking, reproduction, multiplication, and overlay.

item.title: Nazeerah Jacub
item.description: Visual Artist, Jacub Nazeerah (1993.) born in the heart of Johannesburg spent her early life in a predominantly Muslim community, wherein the pursuit of art was inaccessible and discouraged. Jacub. N, began oil painting from the tender age of fourteen following her passion for painting and graduated with a Visual Art Honours degree from the University of Johannesburg in 2016. Jacub. N, won a merit award from Thami Mnyele and as well as the Sasol New Signatures competition.She has featured in the Emerging Painters show at Turbine Art Fair and was selected top 100 artists to exhibit at the ‘Other Art Fair, Australia. Her artworks are featured on Saatchi Art and she has also exhibited at Pretoria Art Museum along with numerous group-shows in galleries in and around Gauteng, such as Art it is, UJ Gallery, Art Lovers to name a few with a group exhibition at the RMB Think Precinct with the ‘Talent unlocked’ residency in 2024.Nazeerah is an independent artist, wife and mother of two young girls and runs her studio from Johannesburg. Nazeerah has graduated from International Sculpture-Painting school and is currently working on her new body of work for her upcoming solo show ‘(Un)Natural Bloom’ in her awarded studio at the Bag Factory in Newtown through the Young Womxn Studio Bursary 2025.Drawing on the preservation of stories passed through generations,’(Un)Natural Bloom’ follows her body of work ‘(Un)Belonging’ addressing the notion of transcending boundaries across cultural landscapes. ‘(Un)Natural Bloom’ is an invitation to see how life, experience and memory persist in natural forms that were once fragile and enduring, echoing the tensions of growth in disrupted landscapes and of the resilience of the female blooming under constraint.

item.title: Ndivhuwo Marubini
item.description: Ndivhuwo Marubini was born on 9th April in South Africa. She completed her primary and secondary education at St. Vincent School for the Deaf. In 2023, she enrolled full-time at Artist Proof Studio, where she is currently completing her third year of printmaking. Recently, she received an award for exhibiting her work at the Wits Centre for Deaf Studies’ Deaf Art and Film Festival.Ndivhuwo looks forward to completing her stu00dies and pursuing a four-year internship at Artist Proof Studio to deepen her experience in printmaking. She aspires to build a successful artistic career both locally and internationally, using her art to inspire and empower others within the Deaf community.

item.title: Noluthando Ntsuntsha
item.description: Noluthando Ntsuntsha (b. 2001, Soweto, Johannesburg) is a South African visual artist and printmaker. She completed her studies at St. Vincent School for the Deaf in 2021 before beginning her artistic journey at Artist Proof Studio in 2023, where she is currently in her third year of study. Ntsuntsha works primarily with printmaking techniques including linocut and drypoint, exploring image-making through material and process.In 2025, she exhibited an earlier artwork at the Deaf Art and Film Festival at Wits Art Park, Parktown. Deeply inspired by her teacher Raymond Fuyana, her practice is shaped by the cultures and lived experiences of Deaf communities in Johannesburg, Soweto, and Newcastle. Newcastle’s rich history and diversity have had a particularly strong influence on her artistic perspective, informing her engagement with identity, place, and community. Ntsuntsha aspires to complete a fourth-year internship at Artist Proof Studio to further develop her printmaking practice and establish herself as a professional Deaf artist.

item.title: Poloko Mosoeunyane
item.description: Poloko Mosoeunyane is a South African visual artist born in Orange Farm, Gauteng (Vaal). His multidisciplinary practice brings together collage, painting, drawing, original writing, and printmaking processes including drypoint, linocut, silkscreen, and lithography. Through the layering of image, text, and material, Mosoeunyane investigates themes of rights and responsibility, as well as memory and time.His work reflects a thoughtful engagement with social consciousness and personal reflection, using process as a means of examining how histories are constructed, remembered, and carried forward.He treats his artistic process as a tool to examine how specific histories are built, remembered, and passed down through generations.

item.title: Renneth Mhlongo
item.description: Renneth Hlawutelo Mhlongo was born in Thomo village, located in Giyani, Limpopo. He attended Mashengani Primary School and Hanyani Thono High School, where he honed his skills under the guidance of his art teacher and motivator, Mr. Khosa. Currently, he is practicing printmaking at the Artist Proof Studio, mentored by Kim Berman, Osiah Masukameng, and the late Nhlahla Xaba. He began his studies in 2023 and is now in his third year, training to become a professional printmaker. His work focuses on landscapes and animals, where he combines elements from rural and urban areas to celebrate his roots and current surroundings.

item.title: Simphiwe Dlamini
item.description: Simphiwe Dlamini is a South African printmaker born in KwaZulu-Natal and currently based in Johannesburg. Her artistic practice explores themes of memory, loss, and grief, creating visual narratives that reflect on the emotional complexities of human experience.
