Themes of social issues, personal identity, and memory are intricately woven into her work, exploring the notion of "this too shall pass," a sentiment often experienced by mothers navigating the challenges of raising children.Sharday's artistry has earned her recognition within the photographic community, with her work being showcased in various group exhibitions. Notable exhibitions include the 2023 Portrait Show hosted by Through The Lens Collective and 'The Wildest Most Beautiful Ugly,' hosted by Too Tired Project and Open Studio Kommetjie in 2023. As a stay-at-home mother of four, Sharday's photography serves as a means of documenting and preserving her own stories, as well as those of others, creating a powerful narrative that resonates with many.Sharday Swanepoel's work is an introspective exploration of the human experience, capturing the beauty and complexity of life's fleeting moments through her lens.

item.title: Shayma Idris
item.description: Shayma Idris (b. 1986, Saudi Arabia), is a documentary and street photographer. A native of Sudan, she grew up in Khartoum and earned a Bachelor of Dental Surgery. In 2013, she moved to Cairo to pursue her postgraduate degree. It was in the alleys of Old Cairo that she discovered her passion for capturing sceneries with her phone camera.In 2014, she joined a photojournalist initiative to create the EverydayCairo online photo project and participated in numerous national photography exhibitions. Shayma returned to Sudan in 2017 and started the EverydayKhartoum project, continuing to exhibit her work nationally. Due to economic difficulties, she moved to Saudi Arabia, where she lived in a small town with colleagues from 10 different nationalities, gaining insight into diverse cultures. In 2023, Shayma relocated to Spain to continue her life journey in a new continent, with a memory full of images that encapsulate her experiences.

item.title: Sibonelo Chiliza
item.description: Sibonelo Chiliza (b. 1979, Mtwalume, Port Sheptsone) is a renowned botanical artist known for his exceptional focus and artistic skill. His early artistic endeavors included making intricate wire cars and clay sculptures. Chiliza studied Textile Design and Technology at Durban University of Technology, where his talent was recognized by artist and mentor Jean Powell. In 2004, he interned at the Durban Botanical Garden and later at the National Herbarium under botanical artist Gillian Condy. His work with the African Plants Initiative included managing the SANBI Pretoria art collection.Chiliza's botanical art captures the freshness and colour of plants, ofen using Lyra pencils. His meticulous approach involves drawing from live plants to scale. He has contributed illustration to several books and participated in numerous exhibitions, including the SANBI Kirstenbosch Biennales, where he has won multiple awards. Chiliza's serene presence and dedication to his craft make his work both inspiring and technically precise.

item.title: Sibusiso Gcaba
item.description: Sibusiso Gcaba (b. 1989) is a Johannesburg-based photographer known for his diverse expertise in photography and multimedia. After studying photography at the Market Photo Workshop in 2016, he furthered his education in Advertising at Umuzi in 2017, specializing in multimedia. In 2019, he completed a Photography Narrative Building course at Through The Lens and is currently studying film at Sky Rink Studios.Gcaba's work has been featured in both local and international group exhibitions. He was a finalist in the Lagos Photo and National Geographic Portfolio Review Award in 2018. His notable exhibitions include the Street Culture group exhibition at Agog Gallery in 2017, a group exhibition about Johannesburg at Through The Lens Gallery in 2018, The Yaounde Photo Festival in Cameroon in 2019, and the 2019 Summer Salon Exhibition at Bag Factory in Johannesburg.

item.title: Silindokuhle Shandu
item.description: Silindokuhle Shandu (b. 1998) is a Johannesburg-based artist whose work intricately weaves together themes influenced by her upbringing in a small mining town and her diverse experiences across urban, suburban, and rural South Africa. Raised in Empangeni, KwaZulu-Natal, and eMalahleni, Mpumalanga, Shandu's artistic journey reflects the complex interplay between womanhood, human existence, industrial landscapes, and the contrasting worlds she has encountered.Shandu completed her diploma in Fashion Design and Technology at Tshwane University of Technology in Pretoria. Shandu's work captures the nuances of her experiences, largely shaped by the women who raised her. Through her use of color, texture, and composition, she invites viewers to explore the tension between belonging and otherness, familiarity and the unknown. "My work is the vehicle I've chosen to reflect on my personal journey and the intricate connections between self-discovery and the ever-evolving environment," she states.

item.title: Simon Attwood
item.description: Simon Attwood (b.1997) is a young artist who became interested in printmaking while working on his high-school art portfolio. He is currently studying at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago, USA where he has been awarded a Presidential Scholarship."As an artist, I am interested in the relationship between the individual and their environment (namely the sociopolitical structures they interact within and the natural environment that they eke sustenance from). In my work, I aim to make the viewer reflect on their own interactions in these fields and the impact that they have on the world. I do this by criticizing the shortfalls of the politically powerful and addressing the devastating impacts of human greed on the environment."

item.title: Simon Venter
item.description: Simon Venteris a multidisciplinary artist who bridges traditional fine arts with emerging technologies to explore creativity in the digital age. With a foundation in classical oil painting, Venter incorporates artificial intelligence into his work, creating a dialogue between human ingenuity and machine-driven processes. This interplay critically examines how technology redefines creative boundaries, focusing on the tension between human agency and AI’s transformative presence in artistic production.Central to Venter's work is an engagement with archetypal themes and existential questions. Drawing from global traditions and cultural memory, his art weaves together symbols and narratives that speak to the timeless human pursuit of meaning and individuality. By juxtaposing traditional techniques with AI-generated elements, Venter addresses fundamental questions about the essence of creativity and the ways technology mediates our connection to history, identity, and the meaning of life.Venter's projects often highlight critical themes, such as the myths surrounding AI’s perceived autonomy and intelligence, while challenging its status as a colonizing force in contemporary culture. His recent works include explorations of still life, existential symbolism, and architectural motifs, serving as metaphors for humanity’s complex relationship with technology.A graduate of a Master’s program in Creative Media and Production, and a 'self-taught' artist, Venter has exhibited work both locally and internationally. His practice is deeply influenced by his South African heritage, rich in oral storytelling and visual traditions, which he combines with European art historical references to create a globally resonant dialogue. Venter’s art is a testament to the enduring relevance of traditional artistic techniques as a critical lens for understanding the rapid technological shifts shaping the 21st century, making him a compelling voice in contemporary art.

item.title: Simone Verfaille
item.description: Simone Verfaille (b. 1995, Cape Town, South Africa) is a visual artist whose practice explores the interplay between memory, transformation, and self through layers of abstraction. Her work, grounded in abstract expressionism, is characterised by fluid brushstrokes, rich textures, and dynamic compositions.For Simone, art is a living, intuitive process centered on experimentation and self-discovery. Focusing less on outcome and more on meaning, fulfilment, and resilience in the making process. She blends painting and textile-based abstraction to explore her inner landscapes.Simone was named one of the ten winners of the WORLDART10 competition in 2024, and her recent body of work, spanning painting and textile-based abstraction, has been exhibited in both solo and group exhibitions across Cape Town. In 2023, she completed a solo residency in South West France, which further expanded her visual vocabulary and direction.She currently lives and works in Cape Town.

item.title: Sinalo Ngcaba
item.description: Sinalo Ngcaba is a visual artist from East London and Bizana, South Africa, currently based in Johannesburg. A self-taught artist, she developed an understanding of the creative industry while studying advertising design at Umuzi Academy. Her practice is continually evolving as she experiments with different mediums, including oil pastels, ink, digital art, and paint, embracing exploration as an essential part of her creative process.Ngcaba describes herself as a creative, storyteller, and artist. Her work explores the intersections of Black joy, Black popular culture, womanhood, and human rights within the contemporary world. Through her art, she seeks to evoke emotion, encourage reflection, and document the experiences and stories that shape the present. She views creativity as a powerful tool for social change, believing that art can move beyond representation to inspire meaningful conversations and a deeper engagement with the world around us.Her collaborations include Nike, Piano People UK, Aperol Spritz, Comedy Central Africa, NATIVE Mag, Amref International, and the Gauteng Department of Sport, Arts and Culture, alongside artists and creatives such as Sindiso Khumalo and Bam Marley.

item.title: Sitaara Stodel
item.description: Sitaara Stodel (b.1991) is a Cape Town-based contemporary artist whose practice spans photography, collage, video, and printmaking. Her unique artistic perspective is deeply influenced by a lifetime of frequent relocations, having moved house forty times. This transient lifestyle profoundly shapes her work, where she often reconstructs personal and collective memories through found family photographs sourced from antique stores and markets.Stodel's pieces are marked by her meticulous process of tearing, cutting, and reassembling these photographs, often using gold thread to symbolize the preciousness of memory. Her collages depict domestic scenes, integrating her ideals of home—complete with fresh flowers, framed artworks, houses with sea views, and shiny cars.After graduating from the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town in 2014, Stodel received the prestigious Tierney Fellowship. She has since exhibited her work in numerous Cape Town galleries, including Zeitz MOCAA, SMAC Gallery, Smith Gallery, Gallery MOMO, and Everard Read. Stodel also contributes to the Michaelis photographic department as the technical officer of photography, utilizing her extensive knowledge of analogue photographic methods to influence her varied approaches to image-making

item.title: Sizwe Khoza
item.description: Sizwe Khoza was born in Mozambique towards the end of the Civil War and moved to South Africa with his family in 1995. He matriculated in 2010 from Nkumbulo Comprehensive School and during his matric year he attended Saturday classes at Artist Proof Studio. Thereafter, he studied printmaking for three years and graduated in 2012. In 2013 he was awarded a residency through Artist Proof Studio at William Humphrey Art Gallery (WHAG) in Kimberley under the mentorship of the late Dumisani Mabaso. Khoza was then offered an internship at Artist Proof Studio in 2014 as a facilitator in Printmaking for first and second year students attending full time and chose to be a full-time artist from 2016.Twice a year Khoza travels to Mozambique to take photographs and sketch people and upon return creates new works inspired by his visit home. Khoza specializes in painting, monotype and combined printmaking techniques. In 2017 he was commissioned by Rand Merchant Bank Holdings to create an artwork for their boardroom. He donates two artworks a year to auction initiatives that raise money for education and continues to have exhibitions and shows around the country.

item.title: Sizwe Nyanga
item.description: Sizwe Nyanga, an artist and community activist, merges creativity and social impact. Hailing from Vosloorus (South Africa), he sees art as a transformative force, blending research, education, and culture to reshape society's outlook through his photographs, paintings, drawings and multi-medium installations.Educated at Umuzi.org in Multimedia, he has delved into the digital art space for over a decade, crafting a unique artistic voice. In 2018, his daring expedition backpacking from Johannesburg to Malawi with only R1300 a tent and a camera, captured in "Mayendo Abwino" (Photo-Essay), revealed his narrative through powerful imagery. This year, Sizwe exhibited twice in Bonn, Germany, leaving an indelible mark.Firstly, with "the holy trinity," presenting "Please Don't Pinch", at Alanus Hochschule für Kunst und Gesellschaft and later, an artist-in-residency project called "Homeless in The Global Village" at the Kunst Museum Bonn.Sizwe's art transcends borders, reflecting his dedication to preserving culture, fostering creativity, and creating conversation through his stories and photographs. His journey showcases art's transformative potential and its ability to shape a better tomorrow. Now, he expands his artistic horizon into music, film, and performing arts as mediums to convey his evolving ideas.

item.title: Sophie Smith
item.description: Sophie Smith (b. 1988) is a lifestyle photographer based in Kenton-on-Sea in the Eastern Cape, South Africa. Her creative journey is a mirror of her personal evolution, embarking on a path of introspection and healing while documenting tender moments of motherhood and her children's lives. This journey has fueled her fascination with the intimate dynamics between women, children, and nature, particularly the healing properties of water.Trained as a photojournalist, Sophie practiced documentary-style photography for many years. However, it was only after having children that she began to blend documentary photography with fine art, creating images that evoke emotion rather than just capturing moments. Sophie's work is an artistic documentation of life, capturing both the big moments and the small, seemingly mundane ones, in a way that allows viewers to relive the depth and soul of those experiences.Sophie's philosophy revolves around the collaboration between the photographer and the subject, capturing authentic and intimate moments in the most beautiful way when the subjects feel relaxed and confident. She believes in creating a sweet spot between storytelling and art, capturing the magic that already exists within her subjects.Deeply inspired by life, nature, and her children, Sophie is obsessed with light and shadow and how they dance together. Her ability to blend storytelling with art has been nurtured over the years, allowing her to see what others might not notice and turn it into magical photographs. Living near the ocean in Kenton on Sea, Sophie finds daily inspiration and a sense of freedom, but she also loves the feeling of being on the road in search of new adventures.

item.title: Stephen Langa
item.description: Stephen Langa (b. 1995) is a South African Contemporary Artist from the Limpopo province. Langa currently lives and works in Johannesburg, South Africa.Stephen practiced art at a very young age, from drawing cartoon characters to becoming a professional artist who specializes in different mediums such as charcoal drawing, watercolor, and oil paintings. He studied Art & Design at the Tshwane North College in Pretoria. Furthermore, he studied Printmaking at Artist Proof Studios (APS).His body of work explores diverse stories of black people and experiences of those around him and personal journey of life. His work is Inspired by the Impressionism art period from the 20th Century, he researches and explores ways to capture his emotions and fuel his artworks. Inspired by profound artist such as George Pemba, Claude Monet, Gerald Sekoto and Vincent Van Gogh, my charcoal linework’s and oil paintings have become pictorial visions that has a mesmerizing effect that is inspired directly by my emotive feelings that one can immediately identify and engage with the characters portrayed in such a way one would like to know them better in person.Langa's work seeks to galvanize and has intimacy of black cultural experiences, composition’s that have questions for the viewer and highlights of his own experiences of his hometown and the city as visual detailed in his journey, experiencing life in both worlds from moving to one place to another.‘’There’s a lot of intimacy when I’m engaging with my practice, and how I can evolve as an artist and myself" states Langa.

item.title: Strijdom van der Merwe
item.description: Strijdom van der Merwe is an award-winning South African land artist and sculptor whose practice explores the relationship between people and the natural environment. Working with materials found on-site, including sand, water, wood, rocks, and stone, he creates site-specific artworks that respond to the character and conditions of each location.His practice is shaped by an ongoing dialogue with the land, allowing natural materials, spatial relationships, and the surrounding environment to inform his artistic decisions. Through temporary interventions, sculptures, installations, and limited-edition prints, van der Merwe examines how people experience and interact with the spaces they inhabit. His work has been included in international art collections, sculpture parks, art routes, and private residences, extending his engagement with landscape across diverse contexts. By working with the materials and features of a site, he invites viewers to reconsider their relationship with the natural world and the ways art can reveal new perspectives on familiar environments.

item.title: Sue Martin
item.description: Johannesburg based artist, Sue Martin, has been honing her painting and printmaking skills since the 1980s when she completed a BA Fine Arts degree at the University of Natal in Pietermaritzburg. Sue writes about her recent body of work, "My African Garden"Over the past year, my studio transformed and became what I like to refer to as my ‘magic garden’. An environment of fantasy and wonder where I found myself spending hours exploring and playing. I found beauty in my artworks and the various materials that surrounded me.Like a garden I need light, and I allow this light to shine out of my work. Love is light.This body of work is a celebration of life and its fragility.This show comprises a body of new paintings, monoprints and etchings. The series of monoprints began evolving last year as a response to the death of my Mother. Her passion was her garden. Unlike the wild indigenous garden that I have surrounding my home, my mother’s garden was an English country-style garden, comprising of many exotic plants carefully pruned into compliance. She spent hours maintaining her garden, she planted in ‘beds’, along boundary walls and around the house: neat, orderly and clipped back.My images of peonies, poppies and dahlias are a nostalgic reference to these past memories. Juxtaposed with images from my own indigenous garden, which is wild, unruly and left to self-seed and regenerate, as the seasons come and go. The Iris, referenced in my “Lie of the Land” series, represents a colonial, bygone era, blooming only for a short period of time. Its exotic, foreign beauty strangely out of place in the harsh highveld landscape.In the “Cartographer’s Notes” series, I have worked onto the surface of found maps, which take on a more botanical theme. Plants and places that I have seen and visited, have re emerged onto the surface, in a bright and spontaneous way. The limited edition of etchings, with their sketch-like quality, denotes a field study, capturing the essence of a plant seen in nature, to be taken home and reworked in the studio.“But I believe above all that I wanted to build the palace of my memory, because my memory is my only homeland.” - Anselm KieferAll the prints were done in collaboration with printer Bevan de Wet at Eleven Editions.

item.title: Sylvester Falata
item.description: Born in De-Aar in 1985, and raised across Taung (Magogong) and Mafikeng, Sylvester Falata moved to Johannesburg in 2006. he moved to Johannesburg, where he currently lives and works. His artistic journey officially began during his time at Mmabatho High School, where he pursued art as a subjects. He has maintained his commitment to art creation ever since, even as his creativity expanded into the realm of fashion.Falata's artworks are profoundly influenced by his extensive background in fashion, which commenced in 2005 under the mentorship of Annah Getaneh and Eric Raisina. He launched his eponymous fashion label in 2010, showcasing collections at both South African Fashion Week and internationally. This fashion sensibility is clearly visible in his art, particularly in his sophisticated use of colour, texture, and experimental approach to proportions.

item.title: Tamara Osso
item.description: Tamara Osso (b. 1983) is an artist and educator whose practice explores the relationship between the immediacy of performance and the physicality of painting. Her artistic approach is deeply informed by her background in dance, having trained and worked extensively as a ballet and contemporary dancer. During her career as a performer, Osso collaborated with and performed for numerous local and international theatre companies, experiences that continue to influence her understanding of movement, gesture, space and the body.Following her career in dance, Osso transitioned into the visual arts, pursuing her interest in translating the energy and immediacy of performance into a material and visual language. In 2014, she completed her Master of Arts in Fine Art (MAFA) degree with distinction at the University of the Witwatersrand (WITS) in Johannesburg. She later completed a Postgraduate Certificate in Education (PGCE), also with distinction, further developing her commitment to education.Osso currently works as both an educator and practising artist, continuing to develop a body of work that brings together her experiences in dance, painting and teaching. Her multidisciplinary background informs an ongoing investigation into the ways movement and physical experience can be captured, transformed and expressed through painting.

item.title: Tayhe Munsamy
item.description: Tayhe Munsamy,a Johannesburg-born artist, graduated with First-Class Honours in Fine Art and History of Art from Goldsmiths University of London in 2020. Her multidisciplinary practice encompasses painting, video, performance, and digital media, exploring themes of creation, displacement, transformation, and fantasy.Tayhe's work is deeply rooted in her identity as a mixed-race woman, drawing from the Coloured and Indian communities in South Africa. She masterfully combines cultural specificity and historical archives with fictional elements to craft fantastical worlds that celebrate her nuanced identity. Her artworks unravel connections, memory, time, and traditions, exploring how mythology and folklore create stories that bind us together in a world that has fragmented our ancestry.In 2021, Tayhe was selected for the RMB Talent Unlocked mentoring program and group show at Everard Read CIRCA Gallery in Johannesburg, in association with Strauss & Co South Africa. She continues to showcase her artworks in group exhibitions across South Africa and internationally.

item.title: Thabo Skhosana
item.description: Born in the East Rand in 1996, Thabo Skhosana has always had a love for art particularly drawing from an early age. He was inspired by the animation and comic books that his father would give to him. He studied graphic design at Rosebank collage and subsequently joined the Artist Proof Studio. He completed his third year in 2019.Skhosana has been part of a number of joint exhibitions with the Artist Proof Studio which include, Strauss & Co at Turbine Art Fair 2018/19, The Legacy exhibition 2019, and JoburgArt Fair 2019, TAF 2022, Art Joburg 2022 to name a few. When Thabo isn’t printing artwork he is either busy with a beat, producing music with friends or working on his ongoing comic book series, that one day he hopes to publish. Having learned many different printing mediums, he has focused on of linocut, etching and combination printing with colour.

item.title: Thato Makatu
item.description: Thato Makatu (b. 2000 Oslo) is a South African artist/cultural producer in training and printmaker from Boksburg. Makatu completed their Honours in Curatorship at the Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town (UCT). Born in Norway and having moved across the world several times during their childhood, their artistic work is concerned with working through notions of home and stability through the physical aspects of domestic spaces.They Engage with questions of how these spaces interact with evocations of memory and formation of identity.Because of their dislocated upbringing, Thato has used their art to work through howthe home is constructed both physically and socially. Focusing on how the domestic space interacts with our memories, and how objects in the home are activated in our memories through time, the many interactions we have with these objects and with other people. Through their Hons in Curatorship, they have become increasingly interested inhow homemaking practices exist culturally, and how the family can be a way to navigate research and access cultural identity in the home.Thato's work thinks through how the domestic space interacts with our memories, how objects in the home are activated in our memories through time and the many interactions we have with these objects and with other people.

item.title: Thato Toeba
item.description: Thato Toeba is a Lesotho artist and legal scholar currently called flattendacurve (b.1990, Maseru). She shares visuals of continuing thoughts on personhood, politics, propaganda, nationality, globalisation, law and culture. Her work is influenced by her suspicion of formal things (culture law, politics, institutions,) as sober, objective, neutral tools in resolving growing crises of being here in the world today. She speculates on the intrusion of formal things in the emancipated joy of life, womb to tomb and fantasises about some kind of sweet chaos to be master in a less theorised life. She is a LLD candidate at UWC.

item.title: Thato Tlatsi
item.description: Tshegofatso Tlatsi (1999), is a visual artist from Johannesburg who specialises in drawing and painting using mainly ink, charcoal, chalk and acrylic on raw canvas.Her work is mainly centred around her personal experiences as a black female existing. She uses her work to explore themes related to chaos, death, sexuality and mental health.In 2022, Tlatsi received her Bachelors in Fine Arts from the University of Johannesburg and currently resides in Roodepoort.

item.title: Themba Khumalo
item.description: Themba Benedict Khumalo was born on 16 February 1987 in Soweto, Johannesburg, South Africa. He graduated from Artist Proof Studio in printmaking, where he obtained a Design Foundation Certificate. He went on to do a professional printmaking development course under the sponsorship of Pinpoint One, at Artist Proof Studio in 2009 where he was an intern in the silkscreen unit and special project team. Khumalo is interested in exploring different mediums, such as charcoal drawings and painting. Khumalo’ work is inspired by everyday day life. His visuals are stimulated by events he witnesses daily in the city such as everyday struggles, prospects and desires. He documents his interaction with the city as both an outsider and a city dweller. This dual tension is evident in his work; as he takes note of people who have come to the city in seek of the unknown. This is reflective in his work through his intense dark mark-marking and subtle texture of clouds, which evoke specific moods and emotions. Khumalo’s work explores the dangers of Johannesburg while reflecting its beauty through its architecture and cityscape. Khumalo identifies in his work the importance of family and how they play an important role in one’s life. Although he hardly depicts human figures in his work, he uses pylons, cranes, and electric wires to represent movement, energy, and unity: portraying how electricity connects us all. Thus, informing his audience of his relationship with people, exploring feelings of connectivity and isolation within the city. He has been involved in number of group exhibitions, commissions and special projects; such as painting murals in the Eastern Cape and being invited to exhibit in a group show at Isolate del Cinema festival in Rome, Italy. He has exhibited widely and been on various residencies internationally since 2016. Khumalo works as an independent artist.

item.title: Themba Sibeko
item.description: Themba Sibeko (b. 1994, Johannesburg) is a self-taught artist who studied Analytical Chemistry at the University of Johannesburg. Inspired by his studies, which focus on the bonding between atoms and elements, Themba translates this concept into his art practice to explore human connections. Influenced by the people around him, his work is a contemplative study of the unknown possibilities of entering new scenarios, situations, relationships, and territories in people's lives.The removal of facial features in his art signifies the need for recognition, approval, and a sense of belonging. Themba's work also questions authentic human interactions by removing the stigmas attached to human connections, reminding everyone that we are humans first. His work was recently featured in a group exhibition titled “My First Love.”Inspired by people around me, my work is a contemplative study of the unknown possibilities of walking into new scenarios, situations, relationships and territories in peoples lives. Removal of facial features signifies the need for recognition, approval and sense of belonging. My work also questions authentic human interactions by removing all the stigmas attached to human connections, reminding everyone that we are humans first. My work has recently been featured In a group exhibition titled “My first love”.

item.title: Thembi Mthembu
item.description: Born in 1992 in eNseleni, Kwazulu Natal, Thembi Mthembu is a multi-disciplinary artist who lives and works in Durban. She completed her Bachelors of Technology in photography at the Durban University of Technology in 2017.Thembi has participated in a number of notable local and international group exhibitions. Being part of the Pride and Loss collaborative exhibition, curated by Prof. Zanele Muholi at the Jenkins Johnson Gallery in Brooklyn, New York in 2018, is a particular highlight in her career to date. Thembi is also a member of visual arts collectives in Durban, Amasosha Art Movement. Thembi’s artistic practice spans a variety of different disciplines and mediums.Her work explores the notions and politics surrounding ‘the body’, with her often using her own body as a site for her artistic exploration of these themes. Although initially trained as a photographer, she now explores various artistic mediums such as paint and Digital art.

item.title: Thero Makepe
item.description: Thero Makepe (b. 1996, Botswana) is a multimedia artist whose practice spans photography, video, and installation, rooted deeply in the exploration of memory, history, and identity. Based between Gaborone, Cape Town, and Johannesburg, Makepe's work delves into the nuanced spaces between collective and personal memory, exploring how historical and cultural narratives shape contemporary identity.His imagery often weaves together elements of spirituality and regional histories, focusing on the liminal spaces of social and familial relationships. Makepe reflects on his experiences and heritage in Botswana and South Africa, using visual storytelling to navigate themes of spirituality, diaspora, and transformation. His project have received international attention; he was awarded the prestigious MEP residency in Paris (2023), participated in the Invisible Borders Trans-African Road Trip (2022), and received the Diane and Charles Frankel Fellowship (2020). Makepe also co-founded The Botswana Pavilion, an initiative dedicated to amplifying Botswana's artistic voice on a global scale, most notably commissioned for the Unfinished Camp project by Hans Ulrich Obrist and András Szántó (2021).

item.title: Thokozani Madonsela
item.description: Thokozani Madonsela was born in 1988 in Daggakraal – Mpumalanga, South Africa. Madonsela Graduated from Artist Proof Studio in Printmaking, where he obtained a certificate. He is a mural artist, painter and a printmaker. Madonsela specialises in different mediums such as charcoal drawings, painting and mosaic art. He has participated in a number of group exhibitions such as the SA Taxi Foundation Art Awards and Absa L’Atelier to name a few; he has also been involved in special projects and commissions.Artist StatementMy work has been most recognizable for its iconic nude, faceless, often laughing figures. This has been a bold statement I have used to depict neutrality in human identity. Through these figures, one cannot tell what gender, economic status or age the people I represent are. This has allowed everyone who looks at my work to take it as personally as they see fit, seeing themselves through the experiences of the figures on the canvas. This year, I have not veered far from my iconic figures. This body of work will tell everyday stories of people in the City we reside in. With the use of various accessories, I wish to depict lives from serval walks of life, with the emphasis that we are all visitors in the urban spaces we have grown to call home, that none of us really belong here

item.title: Thuli Lubisi
item.description: Thuli Lubisi, a Johannesburg based visual artist and printmaker, was born in 1993 in Atteridgeville, Pretoria. In 2011 Lubisi completed her matric at P.J Simelane Secondary School and in 2013 she obtained a Computer Literacy certificate at Birnam Business College. Thuli then went on to study Visual art at Funda Art Centre in Diepkloof, Soweto during 2015.During 2016, Lubisi enrolled at Artist Proof Studio for a printmaking programme and, upon graduating, she began an internship at the Studios Education unit, assisting as a printmaking facilitator.Since 2017, Lubisi has been involved in various printmaking and mural projects as well as being part of group exhibitions such as the Joburg and Turbine Art fairs with Artist Proof Studio, in collaboration with Cartier and Strauss & Co respectively. In 2019 Lubisi was one of the artists commissioned by The Trinity Session to make artworks to be installed at the Leonardo Building; in addition Lubisi’s artworks have also been commissioned by the Bidvest bank SA and the HSBC bank.Artist StatementMy work is a celebration of African heritage and embraces our diversity. I combine patterns that derive from fabrics/textiles that are associated with different cultural groups, to make them hybrids. No pattern dominates or overpowers the other (suggesting cohesion); they create shapes that are a metaphor for a new landscape that is free from its historical, political and cultural constraints.‘Segregated’ and ‘Apart’ represent the new norm which has been created by this pandemic. The lives that we were accustomed to have been interrupted; because we’re separated from each other and there is now a void. As we slowly resume more normality I’m hoping that, with our differences, we can and will be able to form stronger and cohesive relations and keep the bonds that we have formed ‘intact’.

item.title: Tinyiko Makwakwa
item.description: Tinyiko Makwakwa(b. 1984) is a Johannesburg-based artist whose process-driven studio practice is a deep investigation into African indigenous science and realities. Working primarily with textiles, she creates layered compositions of vibrant colour using ochre, glass beads, and stitch embroidery on umbaco, a fabric used in traditional Xhosa attire.At the heart of Makwakwa’s work is the exploration of cultural materiality as a form of language. Her practice is centered on what she terms "Matrilineal Methodologies"—rituals and spiritual practices that promote circularity and link generations. She champions ancestral knowledge systems as a valid science in and of itself, examining how these indigenous perspectives and lived experiences build and sustain cultures over time.Through a visual language of curvilinear abstract shapes and forms, Makwakwa explores the interwoven narratives between her materials, the landscape, and her artistic process. Her work seeks to create a seamless blend between the physical and the spiritual, functioning as a continued, natural synthesis of tradition and contemporary expression.

item.title: Troye Alexander
item.description: Troye Shannon Alexander (b. 1990) is a Johannesburg-based South African photographer whose work delves into the complexities of identity, masculinity, and sexuality. Working primarily with various forms of film photography, Shannon is drawn to the medium's expansive techniques, using them as a powerful tool to deconstruct and reform his personal narrative.Having been raised in a radicalized conservative community, Shannon's art serves as a direct response to the traditional norms that shaped his formative years. His photography is a deeply personal process of challenging ingrained beliefs, confronting past trauma, and coming to terms with his own identity.Shannon was a participant in the 2022 Through The Lens Collective mentorship program under the guidance of Michelle Loukidis. His work has gained recognition through features in online publications such as Bubblegum Club and Weirdson. Notably, he has exhibited in group shows with the Through The Lens Collective and was featured in the prestigious Shutterland exhibition by the FirstRand group, where his work was shown alongside acclaimed artists Roger Ballen, Justice Mukheli, and Pierre Crocquet.

item.title: Tsako Hobyani
item.description: Tsako Manuel Hobyani (b. 2000) is a multi-disciplinary artist who grew up In Freedom Park, Johannesburg, South Africa. His artistic journey began with an innate love for illustration, painting and printmaking, which has now become his primary mediums of expression. Tsako thrives on conceptualizing his art by infusing a re-imagination of a future flush with art, culture and technology through a black lens. Through his work he aspire to reinvent the past and the future using traditional patterns in a digital manner incorporating elements of black history and culture.Tsako’s artistic journey reached a turning point during his time at Artist Proof Studio. This pivotal experience allowed him to embraced his interests in various printmaking processes like Linocut and silkscreen and this uplifted him as a well determined and vigorous artist and also improving his skills to being a professional printmaking artist and hones his artistic voice.His talent and dedication have earned him recognition and numerous exhibition opportunities, including being a featured artist in the Investec Cape town Art Fair 2025 .Tsako’s work has been celebrated in the art community, earning him a spot in the nationally recognized “Art Times” magazine. Notable group exhibitions, such as the Bon A Tier (BAT) and “Where you are” graduate exhibition in Constitution Hill, and FNB Art Fair have further showcased his compelling creations.

item.title: Tshepo Moloi
item.description: Tshepo Moloi is a contemporary photographer and filmmaker whose work is deeply rooted in his upbringing in the rural community of Daggakraal, Mpumalanga. Since becoming interested in the lens in 2015, Moloi has developed a practice that critically unpacks complex social themes, including migration, belonging, identity, consumerism, and community. His art serves as a powerful medium to navigate and understand the world around him.Feeling a sense of isolation from his own community, Moloi uses his photography and filmmaking as a deliberate means to reconnect and foster dialogue. This personal mission infuses his work with a poignant sense of searching and engagement.Moloi has built an impressive exhibition record, participating in numerous group shows both in South Africa and internationally. His work has been shown in diverse locations, from Johannesburg ("Fluxus Now," 2016; "The Portrait Show," 2020) and Amsterdam ("URBAN MYTHS") to Switzerland, Pakistan, and New York. He was also a participant in the 2021 Kampala Art Biennale. His photography has been featured in notable publications such as the Mail & Guardian and Amsterdam-based Africanah.org, underscoring his growing international recognition.

item.title: Tshepo Phokojoe
item.description: Tshepo Sizwe Phokojoe (b.1995, Soweto) is a multidisciplinary artist with a background in Visual Arts and Fashion. Phokojoe's artistic journey includes participation in the 2017 Peer Mentoring program at Assemblage Studios under the guidance of Bronwyn Lace. He then went on to further enrich his professional experience through his roles as a studio assistant to esteemed artists Nkhensani Rihlampfu and Nicholas Hlobo.Phokojoes talent and dedication have been recognized with several prestigious awards and residencies. He was honored with the 2017 Merit Award by PPC IMAGINARIUM for the Fashion category and more recently, the 2023 Winner of the Blessing Ngobeni Art Prize; where he had his debut solo exhibition titled " Woven Comforts" at Everead Read Circa in Johannesburg. Additionally, he was the recipient of the 2023 Bag Factory's Young/Unframed residency which also o?ered an opportunity for him to have his solo exhibition titled ' TO: IDENTITIES ' which was held in the Women's Jail at Constitutional Hill. In 2024 he was selected as a participant of the RMB Talent Unlocked mentored by Ntate Kagiso Pat Mautloa and was also part of the 2024 cohort for the Rele Arts Foundations' Young Contemporaries residency hosted in Nigeria - with both residencies culminating into group shows. He is currently part of the Bag Factorys' Studio community, lives and works in Johannesburg.

item.title: Tshepiso Moropa
item.description: Tshepiso Moropa is a visual artist from Johannesburg, South Africa, who works across photography, collage, and film. Her practice is deeply inspired by themes of identity and storytelling, which she explores through a unique contemporary lens influenced by the historical Baroque art form. Moropa channels the drama, complexity, and elaborate detail characteristic of the Baroque to evoke powerful human emotions.Her collage work, in particular, is defined by its intricate forms, bold ornamentation, and the skillful juxtaposition of archival imagery with contrasting materials. This method creates a palpable sense of movement, tension, and theatricality, aiming to appeal directly to the viewer's emotions through a dramatic and often exaggerated visual language.Moropa has been featured in numerous local and international exhibitions, including a showcase at the Oakstop Gallery in Oakland, California. Her compelling work has also been recognized in prestigious publications such as the British Journal of Photography's 1854 Photography and the Mail & Guardian, marking her as a significant voice in contemporary art.

item.title: Tumisang Khalipha
item.description: Tumisang Khalipha's work is a profound investigation into the complex and often fraught relationship between societal actions and the industrial processes that fuel the modern world. His art serves as a critical reflection on how these powerful forces shape human existence and impact the very essence of life on our planet. By closely examining the interplay between our collective behaviors and industrial practices, Khalipha seeks to awaken a deeper awareness of their far-reaching consequences.Through his creative practice, viewers are invited to contemplate the delicate interconnectedness of human activity and the natural environment. The work encourages a vital dialogue about our shared responsibility to preserve the planet. This exploration is driven by a personal and philosophical quest, as Khalipha states, “I am in search of finding the inner peace that is tend to be destroyed by our social and industrial activities in the hopes of restoring the health of mankind and the source of life.”

item.title: Visule Kabunda
item.description: Visule Kabunda (b. 1997, Zambia) is a Zambian-born photographer and graphic designer. His work delves into the intricate dynamics of belonging and identity, shaped by his personal experiences of displacement. Kabunda's creative process involves a skillful blending of photography, collage, and self-publishing, allowing him yo articulate his evolving understanding of self and place.He is committed to amplifying personal narratives and fostering critical dialogue around cultural heritage, aiming to challenge dominant perspectives. Kabunda's dedication to independent publishing and artistic expression is evident in his founding of Muchuzi Press, an artist-run platform that serves as a vital hub for innovative and inclusive storytelling within Zambia and Southern Africa.Through Muchuzi Press, Kabunda strives to cultivate a community that values and supports creative freedom and diverse voices. His artistic practice is driven by a desire to explore and articulate the complexities of identity, using visual mediums to bridge personal experiences with broader cultural narratives.

item.title: Walter Oltmann
item.description: Walter Oltmann (b. 1960) is a celebrated South African artist renowned for his mastery of line in both two and three dimensions. He holds a BA in Fine Arts from the University of Natal (1981) and an MA in Fine Arts from the University of the Witwatersrand (1985). His unique aesthetic is deeply influenced by his migratory childhood across remote areas of KwaZulu-Natal, which exposed him to the region's rich craft traditions.Oltmann’s practice is primarily divided into intricate drawings (using pencil, ink, and bleach) and delicate wire sculptures. A conceptual and visual thread runs through all of his work, seamlessly connecting the drawn line to the sculpted wire form. This exploration extends into his printmaking, as seen in his work with The Artists’ Press. Reflecting on this process, Oltmann notes how "the thread of the pencil line moves into wire which moves into polymer plate." He successfully found a way to translate the "delicacy of lace and wire work" into print media, a discovery he describes as both unexpected and welcome.Through his meticulous and innovative approach, Oltmann continues to explore the boundaries between drawing, sculpture, and printmaking.

item.title: Wessel Hamman
item.description: Wessel Hamman is a South African painter living and working in Pretoria. A designer by trade, Hamman brings the principles of deliberate visual communication to his artistic practice, creating works that signal with clarity while rejecting what he calls the "cheap mystery of over-abstraction." This background has profoundly influenced his unique aesthetic.Hamman employs a distinctive masking technique to produce figurative works that are visually reminiscent of the stained-glass depictions of saints. In a nod to Andy Warhol’s hero worship, he portrays contemporary cultural heroes alongside anonymous faces, drawing inspiration from social media's blurring of the lines between icons and ordinary people. He then juxtaposes these "holy" figures against screen prints of real-world graffiti. This contrast between a revered, high-art style and the accessible, often discarded form of street art allows him to grapple with complex questions of relevance, accessibility, and the nature of "fast fame" in a world dominated by fleeting digital celebrity.

item.title: William Kentridge
item.description: William Kentridge (b. 1995, Johannesburg) is a multidisciplinary artist known for his work in print-making, animation, theatre, and opera. His art blends traditional and modern techniques, exploring themes of historical trauma, social justice, and the legacies of apartheid and colonialism in South Africa. Working mainly in charcoal and ink, his animated films are created through drawing, erasure, and reworking, giving his work a haunting, layered quality.Kentridge's pieces often intertwine various media, with film, print, and theatre projects influencing one another in a seamless narrative flow. This approach is exemplified in the The Nose series, which draws inspiration from his adaptation of Shostakovich’s opera for the Metropolitan Opera, New York, and carries traces of The Magic Flute and other past projects.His film series 9 Drawings for Projection (1989-2003), set against Johannesburg's industrial landscapes, established Kentridge as a master of politically charged, autobiographical storytelling through expression gesture and rich symbolism.

item.title: Winston Thekiso
item.description: Winston Thekiso (b. 1978, Evaton, Gauteng, South Africa) is an artist and graphic designer known for his exploration of belief systems and impact of human behaviour. Graduating with a Diploma in Graphic Design from Technikon Witwatersrand in 200, Thekiso relocated to Mbombela in 2007, where he has worked for the Department of Human Settlements. His largely self-taught artistic journey includes mentorship under Karin Daymond and the White River Gallery.Thekiso's work, characterized by abstract forms and geometric shapes, addresses social, political, and moral issues. His notable series of lithographs produced with The Artists' Press has garnered significant attention, including a feature in Art Africa magazine's 'Bright Young Things', His piece 'Silence' was the cover of Thabo Jijana's book, 'Failing Maths and my other Crimes'. Thekiso's first solo exhibition, 'Timeless Moments', was hosted by the White River Gallery in 2019. His art is part of the High Court collection in Mbombela.

item.title: Xhanti Zwelendaba
item.description: Xhanti Zwelendaba is a South African multi-disciplinary artist whose practice spans sculpting, printmaking, installation, performance, and video art. His work confronts the complex tensions between traditional Xhosa culture and the contemporary forces of capitalism and nationalism, all while interrogating the enduring legacies of colonialism and apartheid. This exploration is deeply informed by his own experience of navigating and balancing these often-conflicting cultural paradigms.Each of Zwelendaba's works is a testament to his commitment to questioning both his personal identity and the collective identities of Black people in South Africa. By employing diverse materials and collaborative processes, he allows each idea to unfold with unique nuance. His practice is overtly situated within a decolonial framework, constantly pushing the boundaries of art-making from the African continent within a contemporary art sphere that remains largely dominated by Western European traditions.Zwelendaba's career has been marked by numerous significant achievements. He was featured as the Artist of the Year at the Turbine Art Fair in 2021 and has participated in major art fairs, including Investec Cape Town Art Fair and FNB Art Johannesburg. His work has been shown in solo and group exhibitions such as Chamber of Mines (2016), Familial Threads (2019), and Tongues (2021). He has completed prestigious residencies at NIROX (2017) and the Leipzig International Art Programme in Germany (2022).

item.title: Yassmin Forte
item.description: Yassmin Forte (b. 1980, Quelimane) is a distinguished Mozambican artist, curator, and communication professional based in Maputo. With a degree in Communication Sciences from ISPU, Forte has cultivated an impressive 11-year career spanning Mozambique, Portugal, Cape Verde, and Brazil, working in both urban and rural contexts.Passionate about art and cultural diversity, Forte is an accomplished photographer who has presented several solo exhibitions, including 'On the Stage' and 'In Stage 1' at BCI Mediateca and 'Mulheres com Pinta' at Livraria Minerva. Her work has also been featured in numerous collective exhibitions over the last eight years.Beyond her artistic practice, Forte is a respected curator. She has curated significant projects such as the UN Women Photography Contest and a homage to Jorge Almeida (in collaboration with Filipe Branquinho) at the Franco-Mozambican Cultural Center. She is also committed to community development, leading photography workshops like "Olhar da Rapariga" and serving as a juror for various photo contests.Her global perspective has been further enriched through participation in three international artistic residencies: Catchupa Factory in Cape Verde, and Gineceu/Legado and Up Cycle in Maputo.

item.title: Yasmine Amal
item.description: Yasmine Amal is a self-taught artist and political scientist with Moroccan heritage, born in Germany. Currently an art fellow at laba Berlin and Künstlerhaus Bethanien, Yasmine's work reflect her commitment to intersectional feminism and social cohesion, particularly between Jewish and Muslim indigenous life in Morocco. Her art is profoundly influenced by her Afro-Arab heritage and her connection to the ocean, often drawing from the vibrant dynamics of coral reefs and Amazigh symbols.Through Yasmine's work, she honours traditions, embraces environmental responsibility, and fosters spaces for cross-cultural dialogue. By understanding her role as an ancestor-in-the-making, Yasmine seeks to harness the transformative power of art to contribute to collective pursuits and create a future steeped in shared values.

item.title: Yonela Doda
item.description: Yonela Doda, born in 1998 is a Cape Town based collage mixed media artists. Doda work is premised on the Catharsis Theory and the deep connection she has with her physical and emotional aspect of her life as well as the things she wishes to fix within herself. Doda does this by dealing with the distortion, healing and purification of her own pain and the pain caused by others onto her.Doda’s interest in looking at the fragmented and distorted body (particularly the woman body) by experimenting with collage and thread has led her to her interest in extended and prosthetic bodies as well as ritualistic and transgressive body. Doda explores and confronts the violence towards women in South Africa, how and why the body comes to matter, what the body can and is able to do as a material, bodies that she comes in contact with, how sometimes these bodies are welcome and invited and how sometimes they are not. Doda also speaks of the process of going through to get through that result in Self-Knowledge which is strongly influenced by her interest in the Catharsis theory which was first used in a psychological context by Josef Breuer.Doda’s collage work is influenced by the creating of the hybrid body beyond the physical limitations of the human scale; extending and distorting the body to create new identity. Doda also uses stitching in her work(s), a way to communicate the process of healing and purification.Doda’s ways of recalling her vulnerability through herself and her own experiences, it’s heavens and hell might sometimes view as violent, which in some cases is. This helps Doda not reject self but instead visit and highlight those vulnerabilities and help herself heal. Finding a home in self is one of the important subjects that Doda highlights in her works. Doda describes “ It was when I found home within myself that I realized the importance of self-love, peace and nurturing self before others”.EXHIBITIONS Group exhibited at The Move Gallery, 2019. And So The Stories Ran Away Exhibition at the Zeitz MOCAA, 2019 – 2020. Winner of the Dreams Realities competition at ORMS Cape Town School of Photography 2020. Virtual Group Exhibition at ORMS Cape Town School of Photography titled Dreams Realities, 2020.

item.title: Mira Jaan
item.description: Mira Jaan is an emerging artist born in Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal and raised the majority of her youth in Cape Town, South Africa. Mira Jaan was first introduced to the art world by her father Ashram Jamal who remains a great inspiration to her. His affinity with. Bright colours which covered the walls of her childhood home, appreciation of art history and his own heritage has reflected itself in her work. Her primary medium is gouache paint on paper but she is transitioning into using more acrylic paints on canvas. Mira Jaan is inspired by the art of the past specifically of ancient India. And parts of East/South East Asia. Within her art her core concern is a blend of. Felinity and androgyny and how these factors can exist along side each other in one person.She often paints two figures mirroring each other but holding different characteristics in the same frame. For her no body is every one thing, we are all split genetically, spiritually and emotionally into multiple manifestations of ourselves. She feels as though one can become frustrated with maintaining a singular identity, unable to embrace certain an aspect of themselves as they might contradict the other. By portraying these dual manifestations in the same frame living alongside and supporting each other she hopes to create an acceptance within the viewer of all the different versions of themselves within them as as well as an acceptance. And love within herself.

item.title: Kamogelo Sebopa
item.description: Kamogelo Sebopa is a South African contemporary artist whose work reflects themes of memory, identity, and culture. Using expressive techniques and layered storytelling, Sebopa creates artworks that engage viewers with both personal and collective narratives.

item.title: Zandile Makroti
item.description: Zandile (Zandi) Makroti is a multidisciplinary storyteller, qualified production designer, aspiring curator, creative director, and certified UX/UI designer based in Johannesburg, South Africa. Her work is deeply rooted in personal experience, spiritual growth, and the quiet power of becoming, reflecting a journey of self-discovery through art.Working across film photography, fine art materials, fabric, performance, and installation, Zandi builds visual worlds that explore womanhood, ancestry, and identity. Each piece is a fragment of her journey, a mirror of emotional, creative, and spiritual transformation.She has exhibited at the Open Window Institute and Kameraz, and was nominated for the Pangolin Awards at Open Window for Best Production Design Project. Her background in production design and user experience informs a practice that is both visually immersive and emotionally resonant, bridging the disciplines of film, design, and fine art to tell stories that honour where she comes from, who she is, and who she is still becoming.

item.title: Abel Beyene
item.description: Abel Beyene (b. 1995, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia) is an interdisciplinary visual artist living and working in Addis Ababa. He studied at the Abyssinia Art and Vocational Training Centre before continuing his education at the Teferi Mekonen School of Art between 2015 and 2018, where he developed his distinctive artistic practice. Working across painting, collage, photography, and digital media, Beyene primarily uses acrylic and oil while embracing experimentation across multiple disciplines. His practice investigates the fluid nature of human identity and its relationship to an ever-changing world, exploring themes of history, migration, diversity, and the production of knowledge. Through layered compositions and a multidisciplinary approach, Beyene creates works that reflect on the complexities of contemporary society, inviting viewers to consider the intersections of personal experience, collective memory, and global transformation.

item.title: Almogera Abdelbagi
item.description: Almogera Abdelbagi (also known as Almogera Abdalbagea, b. 1994, Al-Manaqil) is a highly compelling contemporary Sudanese visual artist, painter, and researcher whose practice is deeply rooted in the socio-political realities of postcolonial East Africa. Abdelbagi formalised his visual vocabulary at the Sudan University of Science and Technology (SUST), earning both an Illustration Design Diploma and a Bachelor’s in Painting from the prestigious College of Fine and Applied Arts. His research-heavy studio practice operates as a powerful mechanism for peaceful dialogue, investigating how national identity is forged through the historical trauma of colonisation and how it manifests in the contemporary Sudanese landscape.Working fluidly across mixed media collage, thick oil texturing, and expressive abstraction, Abdelbagi focuses intensely on topics of ethnic diversity and group dynamics. Driven by a mission to democratise contemporary fine art, he frequently paints on unconventional, local organic surfaces—such as clay, palm leaves, raw wood, and leather—ensuring his imagery resonates across diverse socio-economic communities. Deeply committed to grassroots art development, he has driven multiple creative workshops partnered with UNESCO and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), using visual expression to educate communities on critical healthcare issues.

item.title: Delman Kazembe Matola
item.description: Delman Kazembe Matola (b. 1996) is a highly compelling Botswana-born, Malawian contemporary visual artist whose multidisciplinary practice explores complex themes of spirituality, community, and cultural identity. Currently based in Cape Town, South Africa, Matola fuses figurative painting, ceramics, and sculpture into powerful psychological and diasporic narratives. Through dynamic, vibrant compositions and deeply layered symbolism, his art captures both the heavy systemic resilience and the radiant beauty of contemporary African life.Matola is widely celebrated for constructing a surreal, dreamlike visual universe inhabited by his signature "Blue Face" characters. Emerging from personal memories and cross-border observations, these distorted figures use striking palettes of blue as an emotional register to navigate universal human struggles with alienation, vulnerability, and the pursuit of selfhood. Operating within a contemporary African futurist framework, his canvas work explores what survives displacement and what is inherited across generations.Represented on major digital art platforms and showcased at institutions like the Camps Bay Gallery, Matola's rapidly growing body of work continues to gain global attention, offering viewers a profound mirror into identity construction and the collective modern state of mind.

item.title: Gabrielle Kannemeyer
item.description: Gabrielle Kannemeyer is a photographer and visual storyteller based in District Six, Cape Town. Her practice moves between portraiture, documentary photography and long-form research to explore identity, belonging, memory and cultural preservation. Rooted in personal history and community, her ongoing work traces South African horse culture as a living archive of intergenerational knowledge, heritage and care. Working from within her community, Kannemeyer builds a counter-archive of presence, cultural survival and continuity. Her images foreground the everyday rituals, relationships and landscapes that shape collective identity, offering nuanced narratives often absent from mainstream historical records. Through a careful and collaborative approach, she creates work that honours lived experience while encouraging deeper reflection on the intersections of place, ancestry, resilience and the enduring significance of cultural traditions.

item.title: Guy Du Toit
item.description: “My objects come from my immediate environment, selected for their non-heroic, open-ended meaning. Bells, for instance, may refer either to slavery or liberty. My overriding concern is that of reality and illusion; the fusing of Western and African realities is somehow reflected in this ambiguity.”Guy du Toit uses a wide range of media in his sculptures, including bronze, stone, wood and steel, and draws in pen, ink and charcoal. He has exhibited extensively, both locally and internationally, and has been consistently supported by private and public collectors, institutions, academics and fellow artists.Honoured with several awards, he curates and adjudicates exhibitions and lectures at a number of institutions, including Pelmama Academy in Soweto, Pretoria University, Johannesburg and Pretoria Technicons, and the Johannesburg School of Art, Ballet, Drama and Music. He gives workshops throughout South Africa and has been involved in community projects, seminars and symposia.The past few years have increasingly been spent on private and public commissions and in working closely with artists and businesses, especially those involved in design, communications, architecture, advertising and entertainment. Guy currently teaches part-time at the University of Pretoria and works full-time from his new home and studio in Zwavelpoort.Guy du Toit’s apparent irreverence can obfuscate the fact that he is undoubtedly one of South Africa’s most accomplished sculptors. “Liberated” (as he says) by the advent of democracy in South Africa from having to concern himself and his art with the notions of identity, he has happily turned his attention to “less provincial” pursuits like revelling in form, concept and media for their own sakes. Du Toit uses the unexpected juxtaposition of bronze casts of universal, everyday found (and made-to-look-found) objects to invite his audience to invent dialogue themselves.

item.title: Ina Maria Shikongo
item.description: Ina Maria Shikongo ((b.1979)) creates striking textile works that reflect her deep commitment to climate justice. Born in Angola as a refugee and raised in Namibia, her practice is shaped by a life of resilience, activism, and care for the planet. Her textile collages—often crafted as protest banners—are both art and advocacy, calling for a shift in humanity’s impact on the environment.Having started her artistic journey in 2000, Ina’s focus on textile collage emerged from a deeply personal place, driven by a dedication to reusing materials after the loss of her aunt to gender-based violence. Her creative practice extends beyond the studio: as a climate justice organizer, educator, and movement builder, she works across local and international platforms including Fridays for Future Africa, Extinction Rebellion, and Debt for Climate.Recent exhibitions include Unresolved Memories at Guns & Rain in Johannesburg (2025), Slow Burn: A Look at Contemporary Art in Stellenbosch, her solo show Echoes of Resistance at The Project Room in Windhoek (2024), FNB Art Joburg (2024) and the Africa Speaks show at Zee Gallery in Mauritius (2023). She received first prize in the Textile Art category at the Bank Windhoek Triennial in 2021. Her writing and activism have been featured internationally, including in The Climate Book edited by Greta Thunberg (Penguin, 2023). The artist also features in the documentary Temperature Rising, which tracks the climate justice work of Shikongo, Gabriel Klaasen, and Kumi Naidoo as they campaign against fossil fuel projects in Southern Africa. It focuses on grassroots activism and the fight for a just transition.Ina’s art is a form of storytelling—interweaving fabric, memory, and resistance into a visual language that speaks for justice, regeneration, and hope.

item.title: Keonah Nyembe
item.description: Keonah Nyembe is an evocative contemporary South African artist currently based in Johannesburg, whose practice deeply delves into interconnected themes of identity, memory, and the shared environment. Through a nuanced and reflective creative approach, Nyembe continuously challenges conventional perceptions of reality, encouraging viewers to reconsider how personal histories and physical surroundings shape everyday human experience. Working primarily within printmaking and spatial installation, Nyembe crafts immersive visual environments that establish an intimate, felt experience for the observer. The tactile processes inherent in printmaking, marked by repetition, pressure, and subtle variation, mirror the fragile ways memories construct, alter, and fade over time. When combined with thoughtfully scaled installations, these works transform physical spaces into contemplative, narrative-rich arenas. By seamlessly bridging conceptual rigor with deliberate material experimentation, Nyembe constructs a deeply resonant dialogue exploring the quiet intersections between an individual's sense of self, surrounding landscapes, and the shifting boundaries of our lived reality.

item.title: Koooooos
item.description: Koooooos is a South African contemporary artist whose practice encompasses painting and mixed media to critically reflect on landscape, memory, and the multifaceted human experience. Through an evocative use of expressive colour, tactile texture, and dynamic form, his work investigates the complex intersections between physical environments and internal psychological terrains. By transforming natural topographies and ordinary vistas into layered visual compositions, he creates engaging works that encourage viewers to reflect on both intimate personal memories and broader collective narratives.Grounded in a deep engagement with materiality and physical process, Koooooos’s practice invites audiences to reconsider their connection to space, place, and heritage. His textured canvases gracefully capture the subtle tension between gesture and representation, offering quiet moments of introspection alongside striking visual statements. By synthesising personal reflection with wider social histories, his body of work makes a meaningful contribution to the ongoing richness and diversity of African contemporary art.

item.title: Mapopa Hussein Manda
item.description: Mapopa Hussein Manda, Mapopa Hussein Manda, B.1982 in Lusaka, raised and living in Lusaka, Zambia. Manda is an alumni of Asiko Art school that is run by the Center of Contemporary Art of Lagos, Nigeria. Manda participated in the 2015 edition that was held in Maputo, Mozambique, also going through the apprenticeship programme at Stary Mwaba’s studio from 2006 to 2009.Manda works predominantly in mixed media and has developed his own mock newspaper style and techniques of painting that is influenced by the specificity of the Zambian political environment, colonial experience, traditional culture, history as well as social commentary that is encompassed with satirical humor.His work is inspired by artists like Stephen Kapata, Jean-Michel Basquait, Banksy Salvador Dali, Michelangelo and Diego Rivera. He works with manipulating text, collage and drawing, through developing complex tableaux of political satirical humor, which become points of conversation and platforms for investigating issues and ideas rather than delivering prescribed answers. Mapopa creates his own ‘mock newspaper' paintings and uses these newspapers to turn real local newspaper headlines from the colonial times to the present into mockery of Zambian politics in relation with societal development.

item.title: Masoud KIbwana
item.description: Masoud Kibwana, born 1988, is a painter from Dar Es Salaam, Tanzania. Kibwana received training as an artist from the Dar Youth Art (DYA) Vocational Training Center and worked under the mentorship of renowned Tanzanian painter, Max Kamundi.Through a seamless blend of cubism and African figurative paintings on abstract backdrops, Kibwana’s paintings on canvas capture the beauty, culture and traditions of the East African people. His meticulous attention to detail gives life and depth to the subjects in his work. Incorporated in his art are the intricate tribal patterns that can still be seen tattooed into the faces of the Makonde people of Tanzania and Mozambique.His work is characterised by movement, intertwining of subjects and colour combinations not immediately identified as African. The detailed 3D applications along the edges of the paintings, usually with white detail, give his paintings an interesting aspect. Kibwana hopes his work brings to light a dialogue regarding the challenges that have hampered development and sustainability in the Tanzanian community.Kibwana has exhibited his work both locally and internationally. He has shown his work in Tanzania, Kenya, Rwanda, Taiwan, China and Italy. Kibwana’s work is in the collection of The Silesian Museum in Opava in Czech Republic. He has a working studio at Nafasi Art Space in Dar Es Salaam.

item.title: Nuits Balnéaires
item.description: Nuits Balnéaires was born and raised in Abidjan in an Akan Agni-bona and Malinké family. A multidisciplinary visual artist and poet from Côte d'Ivoire, his work is deeply rooted in tradition, culture and spirituality.He attempts to capture the multiple mechanisms that underlie time and the correlation between life and death. Nuits Balnéaires attempts to create a parallel space-time outside geographical constraints, while embracing the universality of the oceans and the way they connect worlds and universes. Nuits Balnéaires' works have been exhibited in multiple exhibitions in Côte d'Ivoire, South Africa, France, Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Australia.His series ‘The Power of Alliances’ 2021, inspired by the symbols of the seven founding families of the N'zima Kôtôkô community of Grand-Bassam, was exhibited at ArtXLagos, at the 1-54 contemporary art fair at Christie's in Paris, and revealed in its complete version during his first solo exhibition in Canada, presented at the 2024 Contact Photo Festival in Toronto.

item.title: Maja Maljević
item.description: Maja Maljević (b. 1973, Belgrade, Serbia) is a multidisciplinary artist currently living and working in Johannesburg, South Africa. After completing her Masters in Fine Art at the University of Belgrade in 1999, she relocated to South Africa in 2000 to escape political turmoil in her homeland. Since then, Maljević has been refining her unique style that merges gestural abstraction with a vibrant palette.Maljević begins her creative process by 'dirtying' the canvas with bright paint, breaking the starkness of the white surface and creating a foundation her intuitive jigsaw of colours and shapes. She meticulously builds up surfaces with drips, blocks, bands, and waves of colour, seeking harmony between form, line and detail. Physical movement is integral to her method, ensuring her compositions remain dynamic and engaging.Drawing inspiration from German Expressionists and modern artists like Philip Guston, Cy Twombly, and Jean-Michel Basquiat, Maljević's work reflects her diverse influences. She integrates fragments of contemporary life into her work without dictating their significance, allowing viewers to find their own meanings. Her art spans painting, printmaking, and sculpture, always striving for coherence and interplay between conflicting elements.Maja Maljević’s art is a visual symphony of figurative and abstract, organic and geometric, obvious and elusive elements. Through her works, she aims to create a visual language that resonates with the viewer, much like music communicates emotion through sound.

item.title: Doyle Wham
item.description: Doyle Wham is the UK's first and only contemporary African photography gallery. The gallery was founded in 2020 with an itinerant programme of physical and digital exhibitions. Doyle Wham launched its permanent London location in February 2022.Doyle Wham is dedicated to celebrating photography in all of its forms and to developing the global infrastructure for contemporary African photography through regular exhibitions, events and international collaborations, the introduction of new artists, and building a robust collector-base. The intersection of photography and culture, including fashion, art and music, is a particular focus of the gallery's programme.The gallery’s represented artists include Angèle Etoundi Essamba, Trevor Stuurman, Yannis Davy Guibinga, Denisse Ariana Pérez, Morgan Otagburuagu, Puleng Mongale and Water Dixon.

item.title: Mayowa Lawal
item.description: Lawal Mayowa was born in August 2002 in Lagos, Nigeria. He is a multi-genre artist whose practice explores the dynamic relationship between art, style, and color, transforming captivating concepts into uniquely instinctive and surreal visual experiences. Drawing on his background as a model, he thoughtfully incorporates objects, fashion, and muses into his creative process, using them as tools to investigate identity, emotion, and contemporary culture. His work synthesizes traditional artistic influences with modern aesthetics, resulting in compositions that balance familiarity with experimentation. This versatility is reflected in his choice of subjects, as well as in their styling, fashion, and vibrant color palettes, creating works that are visually striking, expressive, and deeply engaging.

item.title: Meritblessing Ibrahim
item.description: Meritblessing discovered her artistic talent at an early age, creating unique crafts for herself. Her passion for art led her to secure a position as a studio attendant at the prestigious studio of a renowned painter Mr. Duke Asidere. Pursuing her formal education, she enrolled at Auch Polytechnic in Edo State, where she graduated in 2009 with a degree in Art and Design, specializing in Graphics and Textiles. After completing her youth service, Meritblessing's love for textile design and fabric exploration inspired her to join Abiodun Omolayo Art Gallery, where she facilitated the "Young at Art" initiative as a textile facilitator. In addition to her role at the gallery, she has taught art in various schools, passionately sharing her knowledge and creativity with her students. Continuing her journey in fabric exploration, Meritblessing has focused on the art of recycling discarded fabrics, crafting innovative pieces that reflect her commitment to sustainability and creativity. Her work embodies a unique blend of traditional techniques and contemporary design, making her a distinctive voice in the Sogal world of textile art.

item.title: Michael Shorunke
item.description: Shorunke Michael Oluwatimileyin is a Nigerian artist whose practice spans drawing, painting, and sculpture, driven by a lifelong passion for creative expression. He earned a National Diploma in General Art from Yaba College of Technology, where he developed a strong foundation in artistic practice. An industrial training programme at Universal Studios of Art and mentorship under artist Femi Samuel Okediji further shaped his creative direction, encouraging experimentation while cultivating a distinctive visual language. His work blends abstract and figurative approaches to explore emotion, identity, and the human condition.
