Through thoughtful composition and expressive colour, Shorunke creates deeply personal works that invite reflection and emotional connection.

item.title: Moyosore Jolaolu
item.description: Born in 1993 in Lagos, Nigeria, Moyosore is an artist whose paintings convey profound emotion and introspection. Through his masterful use of colour and composition, he invites viewers into worlds of longing, memory, and unspoken truths, reflecting on issues affecting his immediate community and society at large. He holds a degree in Graphic Design from Yaba College of Technology and previously worked as an art director in advertising before pursuing a full-time studio practice. Largely autobiographical, his work features self-portraits, portraits, and intimate depictions of familiar people and places. His work has been exhibited at the National Museum Onikan, AMG Projects Gallery, Soto Gallery, and he completed a residency at DiDA Gallery in Côte d'Ivoire in 2022.

item.title: Musa Ganiyy
item.description: Born in 1993 in Lagos, Nigeria, Musa Ganiyy is a painter, illustrator, designer, and photographer whose multidisciplinary practice explores identity, memory, satire, and social justice. Working across drawing, painting, and mixed media, he combines expressive colour, bold text, and figurative forms to examine contemporary African life, celebrating overlooked moments and the resilience of marginalized communities. A graduate of the University of Lagos (2014), his influences range from science fiction and comic books to urban Nigerian culture. Ganiyy has exhibited extensively across Africa and internationally, with solo exhibitions in Lagos, Abuja, and Abidjan, while also collaborating with fashion brands, musicians, and filmmakers.

item.title: Omolola Coker
item.description: Born in 1992, Omolola Coker is a Lagos, Nigeria–based figurative and batik artist working with dye, oil, and acrylic. Her practice explores themes of home, rest, heritage, identity, and relationships, creating an intimate dialogue between the physical and spiritual. Incorporating adiré, the traditional Yoruba wax-resist dyeing technique, she layers historical motifs of hope and resilience with realistic figurative painting. Her work reflects on cultural inheritance and the evolving nature of identity in a global context. Coker was shortlisted for the inaugural Myma Art Prize (2026), presented her debut solo exhibition In Bloom (2025), and has participated in numerous group exhibitions in Nigeria and the United Kingdom.

item.title: Paul Ayihawu
item.description: Paul Ayihawu is a Lagos-based contemporary artist whose practice explores the relationship between the physical and spiritual dimensions of human existence. Known for his distinctive finger-stroked figurative compositions and vibrant abstract forms, his work is deeply rooted in personal experience and spiritual conviction. Through expressive colour, texture, and symbolism, Ayihawu creates balanced visual narratives that reflect on identity, humanity, faith, and interconnectedness. His paintings seek to capture the idea of "one in all and all in one," inviting viewers to contemplate shared human experiences and inner transformation. Ayihawu has exhibited both locally and internationally, engaging audiences in thoughtful conversations surrounding identity, history, spirituality, and the enduring power of artistic expression.

item.title: Salami Azeez
item.description: Salami Azeez (b. 1993, Lagos, Nigeria) is a visual artist whose figurative and expressionistic paintings explore the human condition. Working with oil, acrylic, and mixed media, he combines vibrant color, texture, and symbolism to reflect on resilience, vulnerability, and identity. The motif of chess recurs in his work as a metaphor for life, revealing strategies, sacrifices, and unpredictability. Influenced by his communal upbringing in Lagos, Azeez draws from everyday human stories to foster reflection and connection. He holds a diploma in Fine Art from Yaba College of Technology and a degree in Visual Arts (Painting) from the University of Lagos. His work has been shown in Nigeria and abroad, including in Austria and South Africa. In 2025, he was commissioned by Tikera Africa to paint Queen Mary of Denmark.

item.title: Samuel Inalegwu
item.description: Samuel Inalegwu (b. 1993) is a Nigerian visual artist from Benue State whose practice explores themes of memory, displacement, home, and identity. He studied Painting at Benue State Polytechnic, Ugbokolo, where his formal training strengthened a lifelong passion for visual storytelling. Now based in Lagos, Nigeria, he draws inspiration from the city's dynamic and complex character. Inalegwu's work is deeply rooted in personal experience, examining the emotional layers of everyday life through references to family archives, personal history, and familiar domestic spaces. His intimate yet expansive paintings invite viewers to reflect on belonging, remembrance, and the ways individual stories connect to broader collective experiences.

item.title: Taiwo Owoyemi
item.description: Taiwo Owoyemi, a multidisciplinary visual artist born in the early 80s, received academic training at the Obafemi Awolowo University and the University of Benin, earning a B.ED in 2006 and an MFA in 2015, respectively.He observed the phenomenon of his society's large digestive system that constantly rejects used materials. Owoyemi delved into investigating various options for these perceived junks as alternative materials in creating his art. He discovered the splendor in discarded aluminum soda cans, which come in different colors and shades. Through his constant engagement with this material, he developed a new formal technique, "Repoussé Assemblage Sculpture" (RAS), exploring the possibilities and audacity of artistic posturing. In addition to his media exploration, his works reflect his conscious concern about human choices in relation to psychological and social affairs.Taiwo has three solo exhibitions to his credit, with the most recent titled "One Man’s Junk," held at the Didi Museum in Lagos, Nigeria, in May 2021. He has also participated in several workshops and group exhibitions.

item.title: Adetutu Adediran
item.description: Adetutu Adediran (b. 1999) is a Nigerian conceptual photographer whose practice explores themes of migration, home, identity, and memory. Through the use of symbolism, she translates complex and often intangible ideas into compelling visual narratives, while her bold and vivid colour palette evokes emotion and creates a strong visual impact.Adediran’s work reflects an ongoing interest in storytelling and the ways personal and collective experiences shape our understanding of place and belonging. Her photographs have been featured in exhibitions and platforms such as Rele Gallery, the +234 Art Fair, and the Abuja Photo Festival. She continues to experiment with photography as a medium for discovery, expression, and cultural reflection.

item.title: Adaoma Nnabeze
item.description: Adaoma Nnabeze, a rising Nigerian artist, got her foundation from her artistic upbringing. Born into a family of creatives, Adaoma's early exposure ignited her passion for art. Trained at the Nsukka Art School, she observed diverse styles under renowned artists like Ozioma Onuzulike, Chijioke Onoura, Eva Obodo. The institution, with its illustrious history and associations with luminaries like Uche Okeke, Chike Aniakor, and El Anatsui, played a pivotal role in shaping her artistic voice.Adaoma's work is a captivating blend of tradition and innovation, reflecting her profound connection to nature and a fearless embrace of experimental art forms. Her artworks not only showcase technical mastery but also convey deep appreciation for human circumstances and cultural nuances.Her journey has been marked by accolades, including the Anton Chekhov Russian International Art Contest's honorary award, recognition at the Spanish Art and Culture Competition, and winning the Chevron Art Competition.

item.title: Benson Apah
item.description: Apah Benson (b. Warri, Delta State, Nigeria) is a Nigerian visual artist whose multidisciplinary practice spans photography, poetry, collage, and installation. Working primarily through portraiture, he explores the relationship between identity and environment, examining how social, political, ecological, and spiritual contexts shape contemporary African experience. Raised in the oil-producing Niger Delta region, Benson’s early exposure to environmental degradation and economic imbalance continues to inform his work. His projects frequently investigate the lingering effects of colonial structures, extractive economies, and cultural transformation within Nigerian communities. While grounded in documentary realities, his practice incorporates conceptual strategies and symbolic construction, creating images that move between realism and metaphor.Benson’s work has been exhibited internationally at Art Basel Miami, Paris Photo with Kahmann Gallery, Haute Photographie Amsterdam, and Africa Foto Fair in Abidjan. His photographs have received significant recognition, including 1st Prize at the Earth Partner Prize 2025 and the Siena Creative Photo Awards (People Category). He has also been shortlisted for the Kuenyehia Prize for Contemporary Art and named a finalist or semi-finalist for several international art prizes.In addition to his studio practice, Benson is active in curatorial and institutional work. He is the Founder and Director of Chaos Art Foundation, an initiative supporting emerging and underrepresented African artists through exhibitions, grants, and community-driven programming. He currently serves as Development Associate at the Museum of West African Art, contributing to fundraising strategy, partnerships, and institutional growth.Benson holds a B.Sc. in Industrial Chemistry from the University of Benin and has participated in professional development programs including the Imọ̀ra Art Intensive with the Guest Artist Space Foundation and workshops at the Centre for Contemporary Art, Lagos. Through his practice, Benson positions photography as both documentation and inquiry—an instrument for examining how histories persist within the present.

item.title: Caroline Useh
item.description: Caroline Useh is a multidisciplinary artist from Delta State, Nigeria, currently based in Lagos. A graduate of Auchi Polytechnic in Edo State, she works across a wide range of media, embracing experimentation without material restrictions. Her mixed-media practice offers an alternative approach to painting, using diverse materials to explore emotional relearning, mental transformation, and the fluidity of human experience. Through her work, Useh creates space to educate, advocate, question, challenge, and provoke conversations around behaviour and society. She is the winner of the Chinwe Russell Art Prize (2025), completed a residency at Farmhouse in Iseyin, Oyo State (2025), was a finalist in the Kuenyehia Art Competition (2024), and was selected as one of the ten finalists for the Next of Kin Series 5 art competition and exhibition in 2023.

item.title: Chidinma Mordi
item.description: Chidinma Yemisi Mordi is a Nigerian multidisciplinary artist based in Abuja whose practice explores cultural observation, storytelling, and the everyday realities of Nigerian life. Born in Kaduna to Igbo and Yoruba parents, she draws from a rich blend of traditions that shape her visual language. Her early interest in drawing developed into a sustained practice, supported by her family, who preserved her childhood works and encouraged her creative path.Trained as an architect with both a Bachelor’s and Master’s degree from the Federal University of Technology, Minna, she brings a strong sense of structure and spatial balance into her paintings. Working across acrylic, ink, mixed media, and digital illustration, she translates everyday scenes—markets, public transport, and social gatherings—into expressive figurative works that reflect identity, memory, resilience, and cultural pride. She is also a children’s book illustrator and author of the Fruit of the Spirit Colouring Book.Her exhibitions span Nigeria and international platforms, including shows in Lagos, Abuja, London, and Paris. Selected highlights include Onyemaechi: Who Knows Tomorrow (Solo, 2023), Give Tomorrow a Chance (Solo, 2023), EmpowerHER (London, 2024), L’été Parisien (Paris, 2024), the NES30 Art Exhibition (2024), Art for Governance at the Nigerian National Assembly where she was First Runner-Up (2025), and the +234 Art Fair (Lagos, 2025 & 2026). She is also a NES30 Art Competition finalist and a British Airways Art & Essay Competition awardee.Her work continues to document and celebrate Nigerian life while contributing to contemporary African art conversations across global spaces.

item.title: Damilola Joy
item.description: Damilola Olusegun Joy, a visual artist from Ogun State, Nigeria, found her love for art during her teenage years, encouraged by her father. Following his passing in late 2016, she committed to pursuing art as a tribute to his memory. By 2018, Damilola had created a substantial portfolio and debuted her work through a self-funded art exhibition at her science academy, involving family and friends support and showcasing talents from her institution and others. The success of the event reinforced her path, earning her the title of Best Young Visual Artist in 2019 by The Everyday Chapter. Damilola honed her skills through YouTube tutorials, inspired by professionals and while her art does not depict her likeness, it powerfully conveys emotions of loss, heartache, and the struggles of young adulthood, reflecting her journey after her father’s death. Simultaneously, her pieces radiate themes of hope, joy, and love, offering a narrative that resonates deeply with viewers. Damilola’s artistic evolution continues to be driven by a desire to connect emotionally and visually with her audience.

item.title: Ehinomen Okoeki
item.description: Ehinomen Okoeki is a self-taught Nigerian-based artist born in 1992 in Benin City, Edo State, Nigeria. He lives and works in Lagos, Nigeria. He earned a BSc in Information Technology from Sikkim Manipal University, India (Ghana Campus) in 2016.In 2017, he interned at the studio of Victor Ehikhamenor, where he explored various forms and mediums of art. This formative experience propelled him to pursue a professional art career shortly afterward. Okoeki is a multidisciplinary artist whose practice is deeply influenced by the cycles of life, particularly as they relate to childhood memories, nostalgia, and ongoing political, sociocultural, and relationship concerns, as well as their decadence. His work explores and interrogates how society, culture, and religion shape human thought and lifestyle.His early artistic ideals were shaped by photographs and crafts displayed on the walls of his parents’ home, paintings by his uncle—a renowned artist—and images from lifestyle and fashion magazines. He saw himself reflected in these images because they embodied boldness, heroism, beauty, and power. This fascination led him to begin ripping images from magazines and combining them with others. He also experimented with fabrics and various forms of art and craft.With the advent of the internet, Okoeki expanded his visual archive by collecting digital images that conveyed the same powerful attributes he admired in magazine imagery, thoughtfully piecing them together to further evolve his distinctive artistic language.

item.title: Faith Omole
item.description: Faith Omole is a Nigerian visual artist based in Lagos whose practice draws on the rich symbolism of African visual traditions to explore themes of love, unity, and collective memory. She studied Microbiology at Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, graduating in 2022, and her scientific background informs her careful attention to process, detail, and preservation. Her work has been exhibited internationally, including the Pilot African Indigenous Mural Project in Manhattan, New York, and AKKA Project in Venice in 2024. In 2025, she participated in a group exhibition in Paris through Maison Kala by Windsor Gallery and exhibited at the Abu Dhabi Art Fair. Among her notable achievements, Omole is one of the youngest artists in decades to have works commissioned into the Nigerian National Archives, reflecting her commitment to preserving and advancing African visual heritage.

item.title: Gbolahan Ayoola
item.description: Gbolahan Ayoola is a Nigerian contemporary artist known for his expressive figurative paintings that explore themes of identity, culture, and the human condition. Working primarily in painting, Ayoola combines bold colour palettes with layered textures and dynamic compositions to create emotionally resonant works.His practice often reflects on everyday life, drawing inspiration from his surroundings and personal experiences within Nigerian society. Through stylised figures and symbolic elements, he examines ideas of belonging, memory, and transformation, offering viewers a deeply introspective yet relatable visual narrative.Ayoola’s work is characterised by a balance between abstraction and representation, allowing him to communicate complex emotional states while maintaining a strong visual presence. His evolving style continues to push the boundaries of contemporary African art, positioning him among a new generation of artists shaping the global art landscape.

item.title: Ibrahim Bamidele
item.description: Ibrahim H. Bamidele is a Nigerian contemporary visual artist; works in photography and painting. He was Born 13, February 1992 in Lagos state, hailed from Osun state. He trained as an Apprentice at Talents art kingdom while in secondary school and formal training at Yaba College of Technology. Ibrahim is a versatile artist who had worked with various medium and materials as a mixed media and experimental artist. His subject and inspiration evolves around his immediate environment, personal experiences and cultural and societal perception. His works addresses political, religious, societal and daily humanity themes. His painting style is characterized with the use of Ankara fabrics, newsprint and more recently an intense dark skin tones combined with brushless techniques he had earlier explored.

item.title: Jemiye Ugwujide
item.description: Jemiye Ugwujide (b. 2003, Westminster, UK) is a Black, queer, non-binary artist of Igbo and Sotho descent, currently completing a BA Honours in Fine Arts at the University of the Witwatersrand, Johannesburg. Working across photography, printmaking, collage, video, and installation, they create visual narratives exploring the intersection of Blackness, queerness, and the African diaspora.Ugwujide’s practice is deeply rooted in personal experience, each work functions as both intimate reflection and collective recognition. Each piece serves as a visual timeline mapping their experiences, struggles, and growth, creating dialogue between who they were, who they are, and who they are becoming. Their practice incorporates their cultural heritage, language (particularly Igbo), and symbolism, imagining these frameworks through the contemporary queer experience. They examine what it means to hold multiple identities while existing between worlds.Working independently, Ugwujide shoots, edits, and creatively directs their own photographic work, which ranges from self-portraiture and conceptual photo shoots to documentary projects. Their printmaking and collage work layers personal imagery with cultural symbols, creating new visual languages for identity and belonging.Ugwujide has exhibited at Turbine Art Fair (Cape Town), Gala Archive (Johannesburg), and Wits Art Museum, with work featured in GAY- TIMES “Queer Joy” exhibition in London. Their photography has ap- peared in GAYTIMES, Homeschool Mag (Berlin/New York), and Daily Maverick. They have also worked professionally as a photographer and assistant for Mail & Guardian, Daily Maverick, and Homeschool Mag.

item.title: Jessica Soares
item.description: Jessica Soares (b.1990) is an artist working primarily with paint. Mixing drawing and painting techniques, her works stem from personal experiences in questioning the complexities and social notions around women's hair in contemporary society. Featuring elaborately detailed figures swathed in colourful fabrics, her works also apply Adire fabric in exploring issues of legacy and familial bond.In 2021, she was selected to be part of the Rele Arts Foundation Young Contemporaries Residency and has gone on to take part in the group exhibition Good Things Come In Threes, (2022), Rele Gallery, Los Angeles, as well solo exhibition Who We Are When The Glory Is Gone (2023) Rele Gallery, LagosJessica holds a BA degree in Marketing from Redeemer's University. She lives and works in Lagos, Nigeria.

item.title: Tola Wewe
item.description: Tola Wewe (b. 1959, Okitipupa) is a Nigerian contemporary artist whose practice is deeply rooted in Yoruba cosmology, symbolism, and visual traditions. His work draws from Ona motifs, folklore, mythology, and spiritual narratives, constructing richly layered compositions that explore the relationship between the visible and invisible worlds, as well as the continuity of cultural memory.Wewe’s distinctive visual language fuses traditional Yoruba aesthetics with elements of European art history, creating a dynamic interplay between heritage and modernity. Influenced by his formal training at Ile-Ife, his research on Ijaw water spirit masks, and his engagement with traditional Yoruba society, his work reflects a deeply spiritual and philosophical approach. Describing himself as a conduit rather than an author, Wewe positions his practice as a medium through which ancestral forces and unseen entities manifest, inviting viewers into a realm of imaginative and metaphysical exploration.Wewe holds a Bachelor’s degree in Fine Art from the University of Ife (now Obafemi Awolowo University, 1983) and a Master’s degree in African Visual Arts from the University of Ibadan (1986). After an early stint as a cartoonist, he established an active studio practice in 1991 and has since become one of Nigeria’s leading contemporary artists. He has exhibited extensively both locally and internationally, and his works are held in significant private and public collections. He also previously served as Commissioner for Tourism and Culture in Ondo State. He currently lives and works in Nigeria.

item.title: Laju Sholola
item.description: Laju Sholola is a visual artist whose practice explores the inner landscape of self-discovery, identity, and human vulnerability. Drawing inspiration from the human form, intimate emotional states, and personal experiences, her work extends beyond representation, inviting viewers into spaces of reflection, connection, and emotional recognition. Through both drawing and painting, Laju examines the delicate beauty found within our fragility and shared humanity.Her artistic process embraces experimentation, incorporating unconventional materials such as tea leaf extracts to create rich, fluid brown tones that echo the warmth, complexity, and impermanence of human existence. This distinctive material language adds depth and symbolism to her work, reinforcing themes of memory, transformation, and self-awareness.Born in Lagos, Nigeria, Laju Sholola is currently based in London, UK.

item.title: The Printing Girls
item.description: The Printing Girls (TPG) is an empowered community of 83 diverse female printmakers from all corners of South Africa. Together, our creative voices resonate with each other as well as the contemporary printmaking community at large. At the heart of TPG we believe in supporting and encouraging each other to keep pushing the creative boundaries of printmaking within our own studio practices. We strive to produce contemporary prints that embody an excellence in technicality and conceptuality. Our exhibitions are celebrations of printmaking and the female voice.TPG aim to develop a strong professional network of female South African printmakers, to cultivate a generous culture of sharing skills and information among the TPG members, Equip and enhance the printmaking skills of the TPG members, help advance the TPGs as a credible community of female printmakers within the art world, grow a network of galleries, promoters, and suppliers who are supportive of our aims and will facilitate our exhibiting goals, and provide information to the public about the processes of printmaking by facilitating interactive workshop engagements at TPG exhibitions.The ethos behind The Printing Girls is, essentially, each of us makes original prints as a significant part of our ongoing creative output. And as women we are flexible, innovative and encourage each other to follow our own paths – no taboos. Some of us use traditional printmaking methods – etching, relief printing, screenprint - while others exploit contemporary digital, and when in an adventurous mood we'll try out combinations of both.We are committed to the idea of the multiple – except of course for monotype and experimental one-off prints … as we said, flexible! But – and no exceptions here – we are committed to the professional presentation of prints and to scrupulous documentation.

item.title: Neo Ramushu
item.description: Neo Mokgoshing (preferred name Neo Ramushu) is a South African abstract visual artist based in Johannesburg. His work explores the complex intersections between politics, identity, and the human condition through bold, layered abstraction.Drawing on the material and emotional textures of his environment, Mokgoshing uses coal, ferrochrome, chrome, and other raw elements to construct deeply tactile surfaces that embody both struggle and transformation. His paintings merge the physicality of industrial materials with the fluidity of paint, creating compositions that speak to South Africa’s social evolution and its layered historical memory.Through a balance of intensity and intuition, Neo’s practice questions systems of power while reimagining hope and identity within the abstract form.

item.title: Resego Sefora
item.description: Resego Sefora (b. 2003) is a fine artist based in Cape Town, South Africa. Working at the intersection of sonic installation and camera-less photography, Sefora’s practice investigates the materiality of sound and the body as primary, formative languages. By expanding on the "sonic" and physical imprints as tangible media, she utilises these registers as a decolonial tool to subvert traditional Western art-making methodologies. Her work seeks to unfix postcolonial subjectivities, challenging the perceived silence of her colonial foundations through resonance and vibration and light-sensitive documentation. Sefora’s broader ways of making explore the tension between labour and leisure, utilising time-consuming, traditional chemical processes to record moments of stillness and sound. Drawing inspiration from the auditory and domestic landscape of her family home in Dwarsberg, North West, Sefora explores themes of belonging and collective voice. She holds a BA in Fine Art from the Michaelis School of Fine Art, where she developed a unique approach to depicting sound through photograms. Influenced by contemporary critical theory, her practice remains centred on interpretations of belonging and collective force, articulating potential futures where Black existence are fully realised through the convergence of sound, image, and time.

item.title: Jan Neethling
item.description: Jan Neethling is a South African artist whose practice is marked by a quieter, more introspective engagement with the human condition. Though often under-recognised, his work offers a nuanced and sensitive exploration of everyday human interactions and emotional states.Working with an expressive and gestural visual language, Neethling’s figures frequently appear fragmented or loosely defined, evoking a sense of vulnerability and transience. His compositions resist spectacle, instead favouring an observational intimacy that captures the subtleties of presence, relationship, and internal experience.Through this restrained yet evocative approach, Neethling contributes a contemplative voice to South African art, foregrounding the poetic within the ordinary..

item.title: Chinecherem Ifedilichukwu
item.description: Chinecherem peace Ifedilichukwu is a community-based textile artist from Enugu Nigeria; she explores isijiakwa as her medium, in 2017, she graduated as the Best Graduating Student in the Department of Industrial Design (Textile) at the School of Arts, Design, and Printing Technology, Institute of Management and Technology (IMT), Enugu. Her work has been featured in numerous exhibitions including the 2026 She-nergy II Alliance Francaise de Lagos/Mike Adenuga Centre Lagos, 2026 “Inclusivity”, +234 Art fair Exhibition, Lagos, 2025 Kuenyehia Prize for Contemporary Art Exhibition Lagos, 2025 Top 100 Life in My City Art Festival, Enugu, 2025 “Patronage”, +234 Art fair Exhibition, Lagos, 2025 Rele Arts Foundation Young Contemporaries Exhibition Lagos and the 2021 My View From the Other Side: Dreams/Reality exhibition at the Embassy of Spain, Abuja. Winner 2024 Kuenyehia Prize for Contemporary Art Ghana, 2025 1952 Art Accelerator Shortlisted, 2025 Top 12 Finalist Anna Award. She is also a 2024 Fellow of both the Rele Arts Foundation Young Contemporaries Residency in Ekiti State and the Kuta Art Residency in Abeokuta, Ogun State.

item.title: Chuma + Sichumile Adam
item.description: Chuma Adam and Sichumile Adam (both b. 2001) are a dynamic sister duo of emerging contemporary visual artists based in Johannesburg, South Africa. Having both graduated with Honours degrees in Fine Arts from the University of the Witwatersrand (Wits), they operate as celebrated individual practitioners and as co-founders of the prominent, all-women Veto Collective. In addition to their standalone studio practices, they actively produce collaborative fine artworks under the joint moniker Chuma + Sichumile Adam, blending their vastly different visual languages to map themes of sisterhood, shared domestic memory, and Black womanhood.When working together as a duo, the sisters bridge Chuma's deep abstract restraint with Sichumile's rich, decorative figurative impulses. A landmark example of their shared output includes celebrated paintings like Where The Bees Don't Sting, which famously marked Chuma's return to color painting after a six-year focus on monochromatic abstraction. Their joint works explore the patient beautification of gardens, familial gift-giving, and matriarchal lineages.

item.title: Claire Johnson
item.description: Claire Johnson (b. 1986) is a contemporary artist and designer based in Cape Town, South Africa. She earned a Bachelor of Arts (Creative Brand Communication) with honors in graphic design from the AAA School of Advertising in 2009, followed by a Post-Graduate Diploma in Art with distinction from the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town in 2010. Alongside maintaining a vibrant solo fine art practice, Johnson is the co-founder of the Cape Town creative design studio Hoick, which she established in 2015 alongside Dale Lawrence. Over her career, she has held two solo exhibitions at SMITH in Cape Town, Changing Hands (2016) and Remnant (2019)and participated in numerous collaborative and group exhibitions across South Africa and abroad. Her work has been showcased at notable international art fairs, including the Investec Cape Town Art Fair, RMB Latitudes Art Fair, Zsonamaco in Mexico City, AKAA Fair in Paris, and 1-54 New York.

item.title: Ditiro Mashigo
item.description: Ditiro Mashigo (b. 1990, Lebowakgomo, Limpopo) is a South African textile artist and fashion designer based in Pretoria. She is the founder of Serati Ltd, a fashion and textile label recognised for its exploration of spirituality, heritage, craftsmanship, and sustainable design. Mashigo studied textile and fashion design before completing an Advanced Diploma in Fine and Applied Arts at the Tshwane University of Technology. Inspired by nature, traditional craft practices, and her Sepedi heritage, her work blends fashion, fibre art, and fine art through intricate textures and material experimentation. Mashigo gained national recognition in 2019 for designing costumes for the Soweto Gospel Choir. Her collaborative projects include work with #10MillionMasks during the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2023 “uMsamo” collection with Mr Price.

item.title: LAJA
item.description: Laja (Oladotun Oshilaja) if a visual artist who lives and working in Lagos, Nigeria. After completing his studies in Fine Arts at both the Yaba College of Technology, Lagos and the University of Lagos, Nigeria, he chose to pursue a full-time studio practice and explore his artistic style.Laja’s work is a manifestation of the abstract expressionist influences and expressive figurative work. Using visual metaphors to investigate ideas on existential philosophy and identity, he often uses bold strokes of paint and charcoal to explore the extensive possibilities of form, colour and line. Laja has exhibited in both solo and group exhibitions in Lagos, Nigeria including; JCAA, 2021; Tribexxla, 2021, Treehouse Lagos, 2020.

item.title: Matthew Koster
item.description: Matthew Koster (b. 1993, BA Visual Communication, Open Window Institute)Matthew Koster was born in 1993 in Middelburg, South Africa, and currently lives and works in the Lowveld. His creative journey began at a young age, evolving through multiple disciplines including music, design, and fine art. After matriculating from Nelspruit High School in 2011, he pursued his passion for music at the Campus of Performing Arts, where he qualified with an NQF 5 in Guitar in 2015. During this period, he performed in several local bands before turning his focus to visual creativity.In 2016, Matthew enrolled at Open Window Institute, majoring in Graphic Design and Illustration. What began with traditional artistic mediums soon developed into a deep passion for illustration, which in turn informed his design sensibility. He strives to create something beautiful rather than what is simply needed. With this approach, he explored the Adobe suite and expanded his creative ability — leading him to the belief that form and function are one and the same. Each part, he notes, should be explored as an element that complements and works within the other to form a single, cohesive entity, ultimately creating a successful design, illustration, or work of art.Since 2017, Matthew has worked professionally as a designer and illustrator under the alias Lazy River, collaborating with both local and international brands. His portfolio spans editorial illustration, poster design, and commercial work. He has exhibited illustrated posters at various galleries and has been featured in Color Bloc Magazine in relation to design and fashion. His creative practice also includes contributions to the local comic book Art & Life.In 2020, Matthew expanded into mural painting, collaborating with prominent South African muralists such as Johnny Allison. That same year, he began attending Carl Jeppe’s monthly figure drawing sessions at Scouts Hall, where he refined his technical skill and developed a strong appreciation for the human form. He later joined the Lowveld Figure Drawing Community, a space that has continued to nurture his artistic voice.Immersed in music, art, and creative collaboration, Matthew continues to evolve as a multidisciplinary artist whose work bridges design, illustration, and fine art — celebrating the beauty of form, the harmony of function, and the emotional depth of human expression.

item.title: Mhlonishwa Zulu
item.description: Mhlonishwa Zulu is a contemporary South African artist, born in 2002. Storytelling has been a steadfast companion in the artist’s life since childhood, ignited by the captivating narratives woven by their cousin and uncles. Their tales - imbued with intricate details of distant lands and enigmatic figures - transported the artist beyond the boundaries of their KwaZulu-Natal environment, inviting them to explore the richness of imagination and the potential for transformation. This early exposure shaped the artist’s understanding of identity and place, inspiring an ongoing exploration of what it means to create new narratives from lived experiences.The artist’s work seeks to explore the liminal spaces between thought and action, challenge perceptions, and invite viewers to reflect on their own internal dialogues. Through Christian religious sentiments and symbolic reconciliation, they aspire to create a visual lexicon that speaks to shared experiences, illuminating the moments in between where potential resides, and where stories are waiting to be told. Through this continuous journey of artistic exploration, the artist invites others to join in pondering the profound questions of existence, identity, and interconnectedness that emerge in spaces we occupy.

item.title: Michal Korycki
item.description: Michal Korycki is a Polish-born South African architect and sculptor. His venture into sculpture was supported by 20 years of a distinguished architectural career. Having co-founded Craft of Architecture and later Mobius, Korycki found himself needing to balance his professional service with a more personal outlook.The artist states: “my criteria was simple; it had to be hands-on and honest, no computers, no drafting and designing, no attachment to outcome or expectations.”Korycki’s interest in and familiarity with assemblage are evident throughout his work. Working with clay, he creates abstract and deconstructed ceramic sculptures rooted in architectural thinking. Material is often considered and expressed in the work, either through the heavily-grogged clay Korycki uses or through the form itself—showing off the material’s once-owned elasticity.Korycki focuses on exploring clay’s expressive potential in his sculptures. Through a meticulous process of manipulation, bending, and setting, Korycki captures specific moments of flexibility and motion within each artwork. He utilises cut slabs and blocks instead of moulding vessels or using a wheel.Clay, as a material, presents both malleability and sensitivity, shrinking and drying when exposed to air. Korycki embraces these inherent characteristics, emphasising the material’s self-correction and response to kiln firing. By incorporating multiple clay bodies and exploiting their differential shrinkage, he achieves a textured, aged aesthetic that adds a temporal quality to his sculptures.Korycki sees the pursuit of assemblage as a common thread connecting architects and artists alike. For him, it encompasses the act of gathering and constructing a cohesive object, building, or space, necessitating a profound exploration of the relationships that govern both architectural and artistic processes.

item.title: Nazeer Jappie Cypress
item.description: Nazeer Jappie (b. 1998, Cape Town) is a graduate of the Cape Town Creative Academy. His multidisciplinary practice is focused on performance, sculpture and painting.Jappie’s works are predominantly self-portraits. His obsession with storytelling allows the artist to weave into different narratives and frame himself accordingly. Drawing from the repetitive performativity of everyday life, the artist looks for ways to bring attention to the absurdity of routine by intensifying its intrinsically surreal characteristics.Artist statement:“I aim to walk the line between the mundane and the absurd. In a world that is overwhelmed with excess, it is the nothingness that fascinates me. The ghosts of those moments that are not witnessed are therefore as tangible as any other unspoken secret. The spaces in which nothing happens, the imagined and the fabricated, the realm of dreams. These are the non-moments I wish to reveal.”

item.title: Asanda Kupa
item.description: Asanda Kupa’s (b.1981, Molteno, Eastern Cape, South Africa) work is grounded by the experiences of those forced to the periph- ery of ‘The New South Africa’; despite its great re-birth. Born in Molteno – a semi-rural village in South Africa’s poorest province, the Eastern Cape – Kupa’s scenes depict the chaos and energy of life for many of South Africa’s subjugated black population, a life that is defined by struggle and by lack of access to basic resources.Kupa is concerned with how the new political regime has failed its people – the very people who brought it to power through their own sacrifice – whilst also celebrating the self-de-termining spirit that marks a long history of civic action. Protest, spurred by grass-roots community frustration, is a central theme of his work. His series of striking crowd scenes, inspired by the Marikana mine-worker massacre of 2012, shows militant action not only as an expression of fury, but also a place of refuge and hope in post-apartheid South Africa.

item.title: Raja Oshi
item.description: Raja Oshi is a Sudanese artist now living in South Africa. Graduated from the College of Fine and Applied Art at the Sudanese University of Science and Technology in Khartoum in 1994, her journey of diaspora, and that of her family, has taken her through Norway, Wales, France and Egypt. From 2004 to present, she has settled in Pietermaritzburg where she completed a postgraduate diploma in Fine Art from the Centre for Visual Arts at the University of KwaZulu-Natal in 2006, raised a family and has continued to paint.Raja’s work is inspired by her life context and what is happening in the world. Living in Sudan, her early work depicts the situation of Sudanese women and things going on in their lives. Being part of this moved her and this came out in her paintings. Her work from that period carries the pain and the desire to change things.Her recent, depicts a new moment. Emerging from the desert literally and figuratively, as an artist, she wants to find something different in her art and in the process of making it - to get out of that world of pain, to experience, enjoy and find happiness in the painting and colour at this time in her life. Her work explores colour, texture, shape and design, drawing from the rich profusion of colour in her South African environment. Her workweaves and overlaps different materials and layers of paint to reveal the colours coming up from underneath. As she finds her own signature, this body of work radiates a stilled centeredness, a vibrant visual record of this time in her life.

item.title: Talia Goldsmith
item.description: Talia Goldsmith was born in Israel and studied art at the Kalisher school of Art. She came to South Africa in 1984 and grew up with this country. She has an inner fascination with found materials and their use, influenced by her roots (Yemen) and her life in South Africa. Talia infuses her work with unusual and unique combinations of new and recycled materials. The organic forms, texture, weaving, stitching, manipulating and human labour are influenced by her roots. She always says "Roots are the Essence.” Her work is a story that bridges between material, religion, culture and history. Her latest body of work Sysiphus incorporates a range of materials in an unlikely combination which come together in an absurd dystopian vision of the human condition. Her focus as an artist is to comment on the human condition through means and metaphors of interrogating the human form, language, spirituality and music.Talia's work forms part of collections in South Africa, Israel, Canada and New York. She has had solo exhibitions as well as group exhibitions.

item.title: Toni-Ann Ballenden
item.description: Toni-Ann Ballenden is a South African artist whose work is born from a unique and deeply personal process of deconstruction and reconstruction. Her abstract compositions are meticulously reassembled from older, unresolved works that she has obsessively cut upa cathartic act that transforms destruction into a positive creative journey.This method is rooted in her personal history and a long-standing impulse to destroy figurative drawings she deemed "not good enough." This process, influenced by feelings of being undervalued in childhood, has become a way to cope with life's challenges. Guided by the principle articulated by Louise Bourgeois that art, no less than wisdom, waits on life, Ballenden allows her lived experience to be physically and metaphorically remade in the studio.A pivotal moment in her career came in 2015 with a residency at The Bag Factory in Johannesburg, which catalyzed her shift from figurative work into abstraction. It was here that she fully embraced her process, finding a way to use the cut-up pieces of her past to build a new, abstract visual language.Ballendens work is held in high esteem, evidenced by numerous accolades and significant collections. She holds a National Higher Diploma cum laude from Wits Technikon (1993) and was the winner of the prestigious Thami Mnyele Fine Arts Award in 1992. With nine solo exhibitions to her name, her work is included in major collections such as The Astrup Fearnley Art Museum in Oslo, the Sasol Collection, the Anglo American Collection, and the SAFFCA Collection.

item.title: Henrico Greyling
item.description: Henrico Paul Greyling (b. 2001, Pretoria) is a South African multi-disciplinary artist currently living and working in Pretoria. He completed his Fine Arts degree with distinction at the University of Pretoria. Greyling’s practice spans sculpture, installation, photography, painting, and drawing, reflecting a strong engagement with materiality and process. His work is recognised for its tactile qualities, often incorporating rocks, cement, and found objects to create layered surfaces and forms. Through these materials, Greyling explores themes of memory, environment, fragility, and transformation. His practice combines technical craftsmanship with conceptual depth, producing visually striking and immersive contemporary artworks within South African art.

item.title: Shana Ellappa
item.description: Shana Ellappa (b. 1999, Johannesburg, South Africa) is a multidisciplinary artist and researcher based in Cape Town. Her practice moves between visual art, life writing, and memory work, exploring personal and collective histories through acts of reclamation. Grounded in storytelling as both method and material, she constructs counter-archives that centre lived experience and familial memory. Drawing on oral histories and embodied knowledge, her work translates these narratives into visual forms through recurring symbolic languages. Informed by African feminisms, postcolonial theory, and autoethnography, Ellappa’s practice interrogates the intersections of identity, history, and belonging. She holds a Master’s degree in Art from Rhodes University.

item.title: Lily Waterkeyn
item.description: Lily Waterkeyn (b. 1999) is a South African artist based in Cape Town. Lily completed her Bachelor of Social Science at the University of Cape Town and is currently doing an Honours in Landscape Architecture. She works with a range of mediums to create colourful paintings inspired by the range of flora and hues in landscapes. Her works articulate a deep love for the natural world and the visible and hiding colours they hold. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

item.title: Welcome Danca
item.description: Welcome S'phiwe Danca is a contemporary artist hailing from the South Coast of Port Shepstone in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Mentored by Sibusiso Duma and influenced by the late legendary artist Trevor Makhoba, Danca has forged a distinct path in the visual arts. His work is a conceptual exploration of everyday life, delving into personal memories to navigate the profound contrast between his rural upbringing and his current urban lifestyle. Danca brings these themes to life through a versatile use of mediums, including oil paint, acrylics, charcoal, and recycled materials. With extensive experience and expertise, Danca has produced a significant body of work and has been featured in numerous visual art exhibitions across South Africa and internationally, including in London, United Kingdom. His paintings are sought after by both national and international art collectors and he is frequently commissioned for new works, marking his presence on the global art scene.

item.title: Givan Lötz
item.description: Givan Lötz is a painter, sculpture and musician working in Johannesburg. Lötz is interested in spaces of emotional resonance. In his work, he manipulates the capacity for paint to render organic forms and natural cycles of growth and decay. This process forms part of a personal visual shorthand, creating a world we recognise but cannot explain.Lötz has been included in the ABSA L’Atelier Top 100 in 2012, 2013 and 2014 and Design Days Dubai in 2014 and 2015 with five residencies in the last few years from locations as far ranging as Finland, New York and Cape Town. Lötz was selected for a solo showcase at RMB Latitudes 2025 (JHB) and recently included in a prestigious institutional group show titled "Abstract" at Rupert Museum (CPT).Solo shows: Memory Exposure (2018); Unearthly (2020); Close But Not Too Close (2021); Murmurs (2022); A Middle Distance (2024) and Notes from the Fire (2025).

item.title: Oh Weetie
item.description: Tamara Weetman is a South African illustrator, designer, and lecturer based in Stellenbosch. Working under her studio Oh Weetie, she creates vibrant, narrative-driven digital illustrations inspired by everyday life, human truth and connection, music, and the places people call home.Her practice spans illustration and design, with a particular interest in storytelling, memory, and placemaking. She also writes for academic conferences and journal publications, extending her practice into research-led reflection on design, illustration, and participatory creative processes. Alongside this, she is a watercolour illustrator, and loves capturing events, moments, and environments in real time through expressive, observational drawing.Through illustration, she documents and reimagines the people, objects, and environments that shape our experiences, often combining observation, humour, and nostalgia. Her work celebrates the joys of ordinary moments and the quirky human truths that connect us.Alongside her creative practice, Tamara lectures in visual communication and holds a Master’s degree in Design. Her work has been exhibited in multiple group and solo exhibitions, her graphic design has been used internationally and locally and she continues to explore illustration as a tool for connection, reflection, and storytelling.

item.title: Selwyn Steyn
item.description: Selwyn Steyn (born 1997) completed his undergraduate degree in architecture in 2019, ending as the winner of the Pretoria Institute of Architecture design award in his year. His passion and focus however has always been visual art. His work arises from the departure point of a knowledge base grounded in spatiality and place-making.Selwyn finds parallels between spatial theory and visual cultural whilst navigating multiple mediums in his pursuit of grappling with interpretations of our individual and collective understandings of psyche, identity, perception and ideology, within the context of South Africa. Selwyn has exhibited at the ABSA gallery with BKHZ, Turbine Art Fair with RMB Talent Unlocked, No End Contemporary, UJ Art Museum, and the National Arts Festival. He was a finalist in the 2019 PPC Imaginarium and 2019 Sasol New Signatures competitions as well as a merit award winner in the 2016 edition of the Thami Mnyele Fine Arts Awards and the winner of the 2020 edition of UJ and MTN’s Continuing Conversations competition.

item.title: Marlise Keith
item.description: Marlise Keith (b. 1972) is known for her mixed media collages; large-scale drawings in pencil, ink and acrylics; and most recently, for her small sculptures of fabric, embroidery and found objects. Her subject matter is vast, drawing inspiration from a mental medley of horrific news headlines, colonial history, friends’ pets, psychopathology, girlhood memories, dreams, her persistent migraines, and roadside memorials. Subjects too daunting, too confused, or too subliminal to articulate in neat words and sentences, are processed through mark-making; offering an alternative “understanding” of a world that often does not make sense in traditional, logical language. This violence emerges in plentiful paint; sometimes it is suggested by the very act of mark-making itself – paper is gouged, scratched, sanded, torn, folded, and nailed.

item.title: Thelma van Rensburg
item.description: Thelma van Rensburg was born in Pretoria, South Africa in 1969. She has a B.A Honours degree in physical education from the University of Pretoria and a B.A Honours degree in psychology from Unisa. In 2004 she decided to study art full time and received her B.Tech degree in Fine Arts at Tshwane University of Technology in 2007. She completed a further Honours degree in Fine arts at the University of Pretoria in 2013 and completed a Masters of Arts degree in Fine Arts at the University of Pretoria in 2016. She completed three artist residencies through Transart Institute for creative practice in Berlin and Mexico between 2015 and 2018. She has participated in nine solo exhibitions and numerous group exhibitions throughout South Africa. Her work has featured in prestigious competitions such as Sasol New Signatures, Thami Mnyele Fine Arts Awards and the Sanlam Vuleka Arts competition.

item.title: Mncedisi Mkhize
item.description: Mncedisi Mkhize (b. 1996, Pietermaritzburg) is a Durban-based visual artist whose practice centres on portraiture and figurative representation. He began his artistic training at the Tatham Art Gallery under the mentorship of Mrs Pinky Nkabinde before studying Fine Art and Design at Thekwini College. Mkhize later expanded his printmaking practice at Artist Proof Studio in Johannesburg. He has participated in various mural projects and group exhibitions, including presentations at KZNSA Gallery. His work explores the identities of Black people, particularly young people, within contemporary social environments, celebrating beauty, resilience, self-expression, and the complexities of everyday lived experiences and community narratives.

item.title: Takalani Mafumo
item.description: Takalani (b. 2001, Pretoria, South Africa) is a South African multi-disciplinary creative currently based between Pretoria and Johannesburg. Holding a BA in Visual Communication from OpenWindow, with a double major in Photography and Interaction Design, they work across photography, videography, and interaction design to create evocative visual narratives that blend portraiture and landscape, drawing deeply from cinema to connect with viewers on a personal level. That foundation in both lens-based art and UX/UI design shapes everything from how they approach a frame to how they think about the experiences their work creates, bringing a rare dual fluency to their practice. Beyond photography, Takalani is passionate about film, collaborative creative work, and continually pushing into new artistic territory. They believe in making art and design genuinely accessible, and carry that belief into every project, whether through a camera, a video production, or a digital interface. Mafumo's practice is built around connection, with people, with spaces, and with the moments that pass between them. Their work is an act of memorialisation, slowing time just long enough to preserve a feeling, so that no matter how far you travel from a place or how long ago a moment occurred, you can always find your way back to.

item.title: Nondumiso Shange
item.description: Nondumiso Shange (b. 2000, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa) is a South African photographer and visual artist whose practice bridges the worlds of commercial photography and contemporary fine art. While working across fashion, editorial and advertising, Shange's personal artistic practice turns inward, using photography as a means of exploring identity, heritage and her own belonging in South Africa as a Zulu woman. Drawing from her upbringing in KwaZulu-Natal and Johannesburg, Shange creates intimate portraits that reflect on family, cultural inheritance, and the ways in which identity is shaped by both her personal and collective histories. Her work often incorporates symbolic materials, traditional garments, and carefully constructed compositions to examine themes of ancestry and selfhood. Following an art residency in Japan in 2025, Shange's practice expanded to explore xenophobia, displacement and human connection across different cities. This research-driven approach continues to inform her work, balancing documentary observation with conceptual portraiture. By navigating both commercial and fine art spaces, Shange embraces two distinct visual languages: one driven by collaboration and storytelling for clients, and the other deeply personal, rooted in lived experience and the desire to preserve and reinterpret cultural memory. Through her work, she invites viewers to consider the complexities of identity while celebrating the beauty found within heritage and developed throughout her diverse upbringing.

item.title: Andile Bhala
item.description: Andile Bhala (b. Soweto, South Africa) is a Johannesburg-based documentary and commercial photographer whose work is rooted in powerful, human-centered storytelling. Informed by his upbringing in Soweto, Bhala brings an immersive and deeply sensitive approach to documenting contemporary South African life exploring themes of identity, memory, masculinity, spirituality, and everyday resilience with striking honesty and nuance.He has exhibited extensively across South Africa and internationally. Notable presentations include Inkumbulo (Cape Town, Paris), with exhibitions at Investec Cape Town, Kiff & Marais (Paris), FNB art fair and along the Sea Point Promenade (Cape Town); Seriti at the Rise Africa Festival; and Balelihle at COOP Gallery, Nashville. His work has also been shown at the Arles International Festival (France), Jakarta, Vienna, and London, with upcoming exhibitions scheduled for London (2026), Arles (2026), and Lagos (2025).Earlier career highlights include uBUDODA at the Market Theatre Art Fair (Johannesburg) and Addis Foto Fest (Ethiopia, 2018), God Moves at RMB Art About Gallery (Johannesburg, 2022), North-West University, and Thami Mnyele Fine Art (Ekurhuleni), where he was also recognized with the Thami Mnyele Fine Art Award.Bhala’s work has been widely featured in leading publications such as Mail &Guardian, Design Indaba, Bubblegum Club, and Creative Feel, solidifying his position as a distinctive and compelling voice in contemporary visual storytelling.

item.title: Daddy Tshikaya
item.description: Daddy Tshikaya (°1986, Lubumbashi) is a visual artist trained at the Academy of Fine Arts in Lubumbashi. He has participated in numerous collective exhibitions at the contemporary art gallery “Dialogues” in Lubumbashi. In 2004, his works are part of the exhibition titled “Nguyu ya Kazi” at the Royal Museum of Central Africa in Tervuren, Belgium. Two years later, he received the first prize in the United Nations AIDS Contest. In 2009, he organised his own personal exhibition “Nani Na Nini” at the Halle de l’Etoile in Lubumbashi and at the Halle de la Gombe in Kinshasa. In 2010, his works are included in an exhibition organized by the Asbl Dialogues and the Rachel Forrest Foundation following a donation of monumental sculptures to the City of Lubumbashi, on the occasion of the celebration of its centenary. Several solo and group exhibitions in Congo and Belgium have strengthened Daddy Tshikaya’s career as a visual artist.

item.title: Georges Senga
item.description: GEORGES SENGA Georges Senga (full name Georges Senga Assani, b. 1983, Lubumbashi) is a Congolese photographic artist whose work moves between documentary and fiction, using the image to probe history and the narratives that surface through memory, identity and heritage. He graduated in human sciences from the University of Lubumbashi (UNILU) in 2009, having already begun photographing the year before. His trajectory is inseparable from the artistic scene of his home city. He was discovered during the first edition of the Picha Biennale in Lubumbashi in 2008, at a workshop led by Marie-Francoise Plissart and Sammy Baloji, and in 2010 joined the Picha art centre, where he became one of its core photographers. His first sustained series, "Empreintes", was selected by curator Simon Njami for the 2010 Lubumbashi Biennale and subsequently travelled to Tarifa, Brussels, Nairobi and Bamako. He took part in Goethe-Institut masterclasses in Bamako, Lubumbashi and Lagos between 2011 and 2013. In 2012 he produced two further series, "Une vie apres la mort" - a meditation on Patrice Lumumba, on the passage of time and on the persistence of what Lumumba continues to signify - and "Kadogos", on child soldiers. The Lumumba series was shown at the Musee national de Lubumbashi in 2013 and later at the Kampala Biennale, Addis Foto Fest and MuZee in Ostend. A Pro Helvetia research grant took him to Zimbabwe in 2014 for the project "Transit", and in 2015 he undertook a residency at WIELS in Brussels. He has also worked with the Market Photo Workshop in Johannesburg and Akademie Schloss Solitude in Stuttgart, and in 2019 participated in "Rebel Lives" at FOMU in Antwerp. In 2020 he was awarded a fellowship at the Villa Medici, the French Academy in Rome, where he developed "How a Little Pagan Hunter Becomes a Catholic Priest". The project reconstructs the life of Bonaventure Salumu, a Catholic priest who died in 1989 and who, despite his vocation, fathered a child; Senga's encounter with Salumu's daughter set the work in motion. Positioned at the crossroads of Congo's pre- and post-colonial eras, it was presented at the 7th Lubumbashi Biennale (2022) and published as a book, later shown at WIELS. Senga now lives and works between Lubumbashi and Europe, most recently based in Rotterdam.

item.title: Megan Kaylor Bosson
item.description: Meg is a curious creative based in Cape Town. She is an advocate for creative living - because life and design are so beautifully intertwined. Meg creates under two sub-brands, namely MegKaylor, which focuses on her product design career, and Silly Goose Agendas, which is is a series of playful and explorative artworks featuring allegorical figures of geese, or “silly gooses.” At the heart of the series is Silly Goose, an allegorical character representing the artist herself. Through this character, the artist captures memories, experiences, emotions, and perspectives in a whimsical yet deeply reflective manner. The human experience is a tapestry of moments - complex, layered, blurred, and at times overwhelming. Yet, amidst the chaos lies a poetic simplicity: the idea that “life is simply for living.” Meg’s work seeks to convey this duality, embracing the intricacies of human experience while distilling them into moments of playful clarity. This collection draws inspiration from Meg’s life and travels, highlighting the intersections between work and play, connections across cultures, and the simultaneous highs and lows that shape our lives. Through this collection Meg has stepped out of her comfort zone, moving beyond her usual structured UX/UI work to experiment with diverse materials and fantastical ideas - creating a playground of reflection for herself and “The Silly Goose”. The result invites the observer to engage in a similar sense of exploration - piecing together their own “puzzle” of the human experience, even if the pieces don’t seem to fit perfectly. Meg is also the cofounder of a young collective called Side Quest Studios, founded with her creative partner Tamara Weetman (OhWeetie). Through this collective, these two creatives purposefully step away from the digital world they are so often a part of, to explore playful creation though various means of print-making methods, ink work, paint and other mixed-media.

item.title: Abigale Calisse
item.description: Abigale Calisse is a South African multidisciplinary artist whose work explores generational trauma, memory, and the inherited language of domestic craft. Having lived between South Africa and Mauritius before returning home, her practice bridges geography and emotion-anchored in the shared, silent legacies carried through womanhood.Working primarily in lithography and crochet, Abigale intertwines printmaking with tactile textile traditions to investigate themes of gender-based violence (GBV) and childhood trauma. Her work reflects on how trauma is not only experienced individually, but also passed down generationally-transmitted through the same hands that stitch, mend, and make. By printing lithographs on crocheted surfaces, she transforms the pattern itself into metaphor: each variation represents the shifting, cyclical nature of inherited pain and the resilience woven through it. At the core of her process is repetition-an act of quiet persistence. The meticulous, rhythmic motions of her mediums mirror the slow labour of healing Through this, her studio becomes both a site of making and a space of recovery.Each thread, each print, becomes an intimate offering-an invitation to witness, remember, and begin again

item.title: Zara Julius
item.description: Zara Julius (b. 1992) is a Johannesburg-based transdisciplinary artist whose practice spans sound, multimedia installation, performance, printmaking, and social practice. Working across research, archive, and performance, she explores Black cultural innovation, spirituality, memory, and collective forms of gathering, drawing on histories embedded in colonial archives, liberation movements, and personal memory. Her work investigates how embodied performance and sound can reshape understandings of time, affect, and historical memory. Julius has exhibited internationally at institutions including the Javett Art Centre UP (Pretoria), Akademie der Kunste (Berlin), Kunstinstituut Melly (Rotterdam), Wereldmuseum (Amsterdam), Darat al Funun (Amman), and the Weltmuseum Vienna, where she presented her debut solo exhibition Whatever You Throw at the Sea... (2023-24). She holds an MA in Fine Art by research and practice and has undertaken specialist training in documentary film and opera-making. Her work has been widely published, and her writing on "rapture" will appear in Thinking from Black: A Lexicon (Alchemy by Knopf Canada, 2026). She currently develops projects that bridge archival research, performance, and sonic experimentation.

item.title: Yasmeen Abdalah
item.description: Yasmeen Abdalah is a Sudanese visual artist, born in Qatar in 1992 and currently based in Muscat, Oman. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Painting from Sudan University College of Fine and Applied Arts, graduating in 2014. Working primarily through painting, Yasmeen explores memory, identity, displacement, resilience, and transformation, alongside the emotional and spiritual connections between humanity, nature, and the self. Deeply influenced by poetry, particularly the writings of Mahmoud Darwish, her work unfolds through layered figures, symbolic interiors, rich textures, and intuitive compositions that move between reality and imagination. Yasmeen approaches the canvas as a space of infinite possibility. Her creative process is meditative and instinctive, allowing figures, forms, and narratives to gradually emerge through layers of colour and texture. Having lived across Qatar, Sudan, and Oman, she draws from diverse cultural environments, bringing together contrasting elements such as light and shadow, nature and interior spaces, and the personal and collective experience. Through fragmented narratives and dreamlike visual worlds, Yasmeen reflects on the complexities of human experience and the capacity of the human spirit to endure, adapt, and evolve. Her work invites viewers into moments of reflection and connection, revealing the shared emotions and stories that exist beyond geographical and cultural boundaries.

item.title: Láura Viruly
item.description: Láura Viruly (b. 1997, Johannesburg) is a Cape Town-based sculptor working primarily in forged and formed aluminium, alongside installation. She completed her Master of Fine Art with distinction at the University of Cape Town in 2025.Viruly's practice explores sites of fantasy, spectacle, and cultural myth-making in South Africa, examining how colonial aesthetics, consumer culture, and inherited symbols continue to shape contemporary ideas of desire, entertainment and affluence. Drawing on autoethnographic research, she creates hollow sculptural replicas of ornamental forms and serial objects using labour-intensive metalworking techniques of 'copying', questioning the authority of the original through processes of repetition, replication, and material transformation. Her work investigates the tension between belief and artifice, revealing spectacle as both a source of enchantment and a mechanism of cultural erosion.

item.title: Chidimma Nwafor
item.description: Chidimma Nwafor (b. 1995, Onitsha, Nigeria) is a Lagos-based painter whose figurative oil paintings explore imagined memory, dreams, and the psychological space between absence and presence. Drawing from personal experience, she examines longing, sisterhood, loss, and transformation, creating dream-like compositions where memory, imagination, and reality intersect. Her work has been exhibited in Nigeria and internationally, including with Rele Arts Foundation, Kuenyehia Prize, and Mitochondrial Gallery. Nwafor was a finalist for the Art X Prize (2023) and Kuenyehia Prize (2024), and was shortlisted for the Cassirer Welz Award (2025). She holds a B.A. in Fine and Applied Arts from the University of Benin.

item.title: Bella Knemeyer
item.description: Bella Knemeyer (b.1991) combines a background in sculpture (BAFA Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town), landscape architecture (MLA, University of Edinburgh) and research to explore urban narratives and material flows. Based in Cape Town, her practice traces how materials transpire spatially; how places are made, broken and mended, and how art-making may document structures and landscapes in transition as an alternative method of archiving.In February 2025 she undertook her second solo exhibition with Reservoir Here, there and everywhere, following her debut solo with the gallery, Something about this place in 2023, both in Cape Town. She was a 2023/24 National Arts Council South Africa recipient in collaboration with POOL. Her work is included in the permanent collection of the Iziko South African National Gallery, Investec Collection and Yellowwoods.

item.title: Sithenjwa Luthuli
item.description: Sithenjwa Luthuli was born in Bothas Hill in 1991 and attended Thornwood Secondary School. In 2010, he joined Visual Art classes and says that these classes familiarized him with the industry of art and encouraged him to further explore and develop his creativity. In his early age he was challenged in school by the education system of which brought fear to him therefore he found peace within art and discovered that his fear was brought by the way his family and the people within his surroundings grew up.Luthuli is a Durban-based visual artist whose practice painting, muralism, and collaborative public art projects. He began his formal training in 2010 at Velobala Art School and the African Art Centre, building foundations under mentorship and through intensive workshops. From 2012, he studied at the Durban University of Technology, where he was selected for a mentorship program by Themba Shibase.Artist Statement My art delves into the complexities of contemporary African society, particularly in South Africa. Just as the universe's vastness extends infinitely into the unknown, so too do our own potentials and ambitions. The concept of infinity serves as a reminder that there are no boundaries to what we can achieve and no limits to what we can become.Within my work, headless figures symbolize our spiritual ancestors, individuals whose identities we cannot pinpoint as we belong to a newer generation. By incorporating these ancestral spirits into my art, I aim to honour their heroism and ensure that their stories and guidance continue to inspire us and future generations. Their legacy serves as a source of empowerment for us to carry forward.Amidst life's challenges and obstacles, the notion of infinity acts as a wellspring of inspiration and perseverance. It motivates us to persist, urging us to press on even when the road ahead appears arduous. Embracing the power of infinity enables us to access our inner fortitude and resilience, empowering us to surmount difficulties and achieve greater heights.The masks adorning the figures in my artwork symbolize the unity of diverse African cultures and religions, reflecting the interconnectedness of different tribes and communities. These masks serve as vehicles for storytelling, dance performances, and the celebration of the vast diversity and creativity present within African cultures across the continent. African masks stand as revered artistic expressions and cultural treasures, encapsulating the richness of heritage and traditions within African societies.

item.title: Scelo Mdladla
item.description: Scelo Mdladla is an award-winning multidisciplinary artist whose work explores identity, culture, and contemporary South African Black expression through a refined conceptual visual language. Working across visual art, film, music, and cultural programming, his practice bridges disciplines to create immersive and socially engaged artistic experiences.In 2014, he received the PROMAX DBA Africa Gold Award for excellence in short-form video production. His work has been featured in group exhibitions and gallery presentations, including Art On Sixth.He is the founder of Phinda Mzala Music and co-founder of Grassfed Jazz, initiatives dedicated to building socially engaged and cross-cultural creative communities through music, visual arts, and collaborative cultural exchange.

item.title: Dr. Esther Mahlangu
item.description: Dr Esther Mahlangu is one of the most influential African artists of her generation, internationally recognised for transforming the geometric mural painting of the Ndebele people into a contemporary global visual language. Her work spans canvas, mural, sculpture, and large-scale installation, bridging ancestral knowledge and modern artistic practice. Mahlangu began painting at the age of ten, taught by her mother and grandmother in the Ndebele tradition of decorating homes with bold colour and precise geometric form. Where that tradition belonged to walls, Mahlangu was the first to carry it onto canvas, ensuring the visual language could travel to global audiences.Her international breakthrough came in 1989, when curator Jean-Hubert Martin included her in the landmark exhibition Magiciens de la Terre at the Centre Pompidou and Grande Halle de la Villette in Paris, for which a full-scale Ndebele house was painted on site. In 1991 she became the first woman and first African artist commissioned for the BMW Art Car programme, transforming a BMW 525i into one of the most recognised collaborations between contemporary art and design. Further BMW projects followed, including painted interior panels for the 7 Series (2016) and Nostokana (2024), a colour-changing BMW i5 unveiled at Frieze Los Angeles, alongside the Rolls-Royce Mahlangu Phantom (2020).Her work has been exhibited at the British Museum, the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao, the Smithsonian National Museum of African Art, the Brooklyn Museum and the Venice Biennale. In 2024 the major retrospective Then I Knew I Was Good at Painting opened at the Iziko South African National Gallery before travelling to the Wits Art Museum, and her work featured in Giants: Art from the Dean Collection of Swizz Beatz and Alicia Keys at the Brooklyn Museum. That October, Umuntu ngumuntu ngabantu, her largest public artwork to date, was unveiled at the Serpentine Galleries in London: sixteen painted panels translating the philosophy of Ubuntu, "I am because we are".Her work is held in leading public collections including the Centre Pompidou, the Brooklyn Museum, LACMA, the Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden, the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts, the National Museum of Women in the Arts, the Pérez Art Museum Miami, the de Young Museum and Iziko South African National Gallery. She received the Order of Ikhamanga (Silver) from the South African government in 2006, was appointed Officer of the Order of Arts and Letters by France in 2019, and holds four honorary doctorates from South African universities.Representation and authenticity Dr Esther Mahlangu is represented globally by The Melrose Gallery, Johannesburg. Every work offered through The Melrose Gallery is recorded in the official Esther Mahlangu archive and supplied with a Certificate of Authenticity endorsed by the artist. Each certificate carries a unique numbered hologram, matched to a corresponding hologram on the work itself and to its entry in the archive, providing collectors with a secure and verifiable record of provenance. This system safeguards the integrity of Mahlangu's legacy and the long-term value of works acquired by collectors and institutions worldwide.

item.title: Athi-Patra Ruga
item.description: Athi-Patra Ruga is a South African artist whose transdisciplinary practice coalesces performance, video, tapestry, painting, and sculpture.Born ten years before South Africa’s first democratic elections, Ruga’s earlier work engaged with what 1994 meant for his generation. His work emerges from a generational experience of being raised within a hopeful miasma surrounding democratic transition, only to encounter the complex realities of post-apartheid South Africa.This foundation has grown into an exploration of precarity, place and identity through practices of world-making and self-invention, evolving to fundamentally centre queer, femme and Black experiences. The creation of Azania, a fictional world that began as a critique of post-apartheid nationalism, represents Ruga’s most sustained engagement with mythology. As a world-building project, the work explores Xhosa mythology while also being rooted in questions of belonging and displacement, where Azania functions as both a critique and a utopia.Performance and the performative, which Ruga describes as “a sense of immediacy and stepping into space”, are foundational to his practice. Yet performance, while immediate, is also paradoxically the most abstract medium in his work. Within his practice, he highlights processes of craftmaking, viewing craftsmen as inherently rebellious figures.
