His commitment to craftsmanship represents both material lineage and political resistance, connecting him to traditions of making that counter dominant narratives of production and value.Ruga’s practice is entangled in paradox and productive tensions with an approach that is inherently protean, constantly evolving across mediums and engaging with the “trans” - transformation, transience, transgression - as a movement that allows for a radical exploration of self.Athi-Patra Ruga’s solo exhibitions include Cameos from the Frontier at WHATIFTHEWORLD, Cape Town, Lord, I gotta keep on (movin’) (2025) at the Leslie Lohman Museum of Art in New York, Amadoda on the Verge (2024),BKhz gallery in Johannesburg and iiNyanga Zonyaka,(2022) Norval Foundation, Cape Town, In Travesti (2021), Eva Presenhuber Gallery in New York and Of Gods, Rainbows and Omissions ( 2018) Somerset House London. Notable Group exhibitions include, Here: Pride and Belonging in African Art, 2026 Smithsonian National Museum of African Art, Washington, DC, USA Améfrica: Diasporic Connections in the Jorge M. Pérez Collection Espasio 23, Miami 2025 TRULY RURAL (2024) at the Palazzo Re Rebaudengo, Italy, This is Not Africa – Unlearn What You Have Learned (2021) at the Aros Museum in Denmark, Kiss My Genders (2019) at Haywood Gallery in London, Radical Love, Ford Foundation,2019 New York, Transamerica/n: Gender, Identity, Appearance Today, McNay Art Museum, San Antonio, Texas, Ravelled Threads (2018) at Sean Kelly Gallery in Seattle, Art Afrique (2017) at the Louis Vuitton Foundation in Paris,

item.title: Débora Sandjai
item.description: Débora Sandjai (born in 1996, Luanda, Angola) is an angolan visual artist whose practice spans painting, installation, and video. Her work explores the relationships between territory, memory, identity, the body, and geographical freedom, drawing on both personal narratives and Angola’s social and historical context.After studying Architecture for three years at the Metropolitan Institute of Angola (IMETRO) and completing a Dressmaking and Tailoring course at MAPESS, she developed her artistic practice independently through research, studio experimentation, exhibitions, and collaborative projects. Sandjai is the co-founder of Ndako 2.2.4, an independent artist-run space in Luanda dedicated to artistic production, research, and cultural programming.Her recent projects include Acentus, an installation exploring family memory and female inheritance; CRIVO Witch Hunt, an interdisciplinary project examining historical and contemporary mechanisms of exclusion and social judgment; and Martires Is My Country, an ongoing artistic research project investigating territory, identity, and collective memory.In 2023, she participated in the ResiliArt Artist Residency, which included international mobility to Paris and participation in Africa Week at UNESCO Headquarters. Through her multidisciplinary practice, Sandjai continues to investigate how geography, memory, and belonging shape individual and collective experiences.

item.title: Beré Magalhães
item.description: Beré Magalhães is a Brazilian visual artist based in the city of São Paulo. Among his exhibition projects, notable ones include participation in the 1st São Paulo Naïf Art Salon at the Museu de Arte Sacra de São Paulo (MAS) in São Paulo in 2021, the GAS Project of Anita Schwartz Galeria de Arte in Rio de Janeiro (BR), where he took part in the exhibition Saravá in 2022 curated by Bianca Bernardo, the exhibition Burnt Orange at the Big Yin Gallery in Saint Leonards-on-Sea (UK), also in 2022, the exhibition Zona de Convergência at the Centro Cultural São Paulo (CCSP) curated by Victor Hugo Ezek in 2024 in São Paulo (BR), the exhibition how to build a global south conversation, at the RMB Latitudes Art Fair in Johannesburg (ZA), also in 2024, and the exhibition Funk: Um grito de liberdade, at the Museu da Língua Portuguesa in 2025 in São Paulo (BR).He has training in Visual Arts and Decoloniality in Brazil, taught by Renata Felinto and held by the Museu de Arte Moderna de São Paulo in 2023. Also in 2023, he received mentorship in the Visual Arts Project Guidance Program at the Sesc São Paulo Research and Training Center, taught by Claudinei Roberto and Gustavo Torrezan. He was one of the artists selected to teach the course Poéticas Contemporâneas at the Instituto Tomie Ohtake as part of the programming for the Calder+Miró exhibition in 2024.In his work, he seeks to reveal a point of view on the shaping of our species, using oil paint and exploring abstract expressionism, building intimate and immersive color compositions, seeking to sharpen the viewer's visual perception and produce feelings, thus opening paths to new readings through poetic denominations in his works. The artist has been initiated into the secrets of the Brazilian cult of the Orisás, candomblé, and the cult of Ifá. Therefore, many of the philosophies presented in his works are permeated by the oral teachings of the odus and ithans, oracular technologies of Yoruba religiosity and culture.

item.title: Boyd Bishonga
item.description: Bishonga is a prolific Zambian artist who lives and breathes through his work - sleeping, eating and painting in his small studio in Lusaka, Zambia. A prominent figure in the Zambian art scene, who’s expressive painting style has been compared to Jean-Michel Basquiat.His work explores the overcoming of fears, addictions and the fight for human rights. The expression of these complex concepts is done with a contrasting vibrancy. Boyd’s ability to be blunt both on and off the canvas allows his work to take its own direction, pushing beyond the boundaries of conventional imagery.Exhibitions include Bringing Dead Objects to Life, Solo show, Henry Tayali Gallery, Lusaka (2021); Between Italie and Zambia, Group show, Lusaka National Museum, Lusaka (2021); African Inspirations, Group show, Henry Tayali Gallery, Lusaka (2020); Bonanza, Group show, Henry Tayali Gallery, Lusaka (2019); Showtime, Group show, Henry Tayali Gallery, Lusaka (2019). Boyd made his London debut in November 2025 with his first open studio invitation event and later had his solo show in London June 2026.

item.title: Neemo Mungai
item.description: Neemo Mungai is a Kenyan artist working across photography and digital collage. Her practice is one of self-investigation, moving through the family photographs, archival documents and personal records to give image and form to the things she is working to understand, the cost of belonging to a family, a culture, a history. Her body of work forms an ongoing archive of inheritance: what is carried, what is contested, and what is finally claimed.She explores the complex and raw emotions of youth and angst, as well as themes of identity, awareness, and meaning in the contemporary African age. Her work is a captivating blend of vulnerability and strength, capturing the essence of her subjects as they navigate their place in society. With a unique eye for detail and a passion for storytelling, she sees her art as a voice for herself and as a medium for creating dialogue with viewers of her work.

item.title: Thuto Rammusi
item.description: Thuto Dumpworks is a self-taught artist from Benoni, Ekurhuleni, creating large-scale works from upcycled aluminum. Through Dumpworks, he collects waste material from dumps and transforms it into art that speaks to community, sustainability, and personal growth. His process is both collection and creation. Over 49 days, Thuto collected thousands of aluminum pull rings to create "From Pawn 2 QUEEN" - a 149cm x 102cm portrait that reclaims discarded materials as symbols of value and identity. Guided by the motto "built from these dumps," Thuto’s work challenges how we see waste, wealth, and where royalty comes from. He aims to exhibit locally and nationally, and to use art as a tool for environmental awareness and youth inspiration in Ekurhuleni.

item.title: Queila Fernandes
item.description: Queila Fernandes is a self-taught photographer based in Mindelo, on the island of São Vicente. Working across the realms of portraiture, memory, identity and everyday life, her practice is rooted in an intimate focus on people, place and the emotional textures of the Cape Verdean experience.Fernandes has exhibited in Cape Verde, France and Angola, including at the Catchupa Factory residency, the Afrika Sovoies festival and the IX Biennial of Young Creators of the CPLP. In 2024, she was selected for the Praia–Lisbon Artistic Photography Residency.She has developed through a close relationship with the archipelago, its domestic spaces, gestures, landscapes and ways of passing on traditions.

item.title: Beatriz Manteigas
item.description: Beatriz Manteigas (b. 1990, Lisbon) is a Portuguese visual artist, researcher and educator whose interdisciplinary, research-based practice explores cultural, social and ecological questions through drawing, collage, photography, installation and sound. Her work increasingly engages with ecology, permaculture, land and alternative ways of living, informed by her work at Quinta das Relvas, an ecological farm and arts organisation she co-founded in 2016.Manteigas holds a PhD in Drawing from the University of Lisbon and has received support from the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation, FLAD and Culture Moves Europe. She has undertaken international residencies, including in Brazil and the Amazon rainforest, and presented solo exhibitions at institutions including Casa da Cerca – Contemporary Art Centre and the D. Luís I Foundation.

item.title: Kganya Malatjie
item.description: Kganya Malatjie (b. 2001) is a South African visual artist currently completing their Honours degree in Visual Art at the Tshwane University of Technology (TUT). They graduated with an undergraduate degree in Visual Art from the University of Johannesburg in 2026. Working at the intersection of drawing and experimental mark-making, their practice is rooted in asemic writing; an abstract, script-like form that exists beyond the boundaries of language and legibility. Through asemic writing, Kganya explores the shifting nature of communication. Their work asks: what remains when language is stripped of meaning; what gestures, rhythms and traces does the body leave behind? Her drawings become an intimate record of thought and feeling, hovering between the readable and the unknowable.

item.title: Swaline Mkhonto
item.description: Swaline Mkhonto (b. 2002, Johannesburg) is a South African artist whose interdisciplinary practice spans printmaking, installation, material exploration, and writing. Rooted in process, her work engages with land as a site of memory, fragmentation, and transformation. Her practice considers the ways in which material, place, and language can hold traces of lived experience and histories that are often difficult to articulate.Through materials such as pulp, silk, copper, and Perspex, Mkhonto explores how language and listening can emerge from the land itself, treating objects—whether living or inert—as carriers of stories. Her works often emerge through a process of experimentation, allowing materials to guide and shape the development of ideas. In this way, she creates spaces for reflection, paying attention to subtle forms of communication between people, objects, and their surroundings. Mkhonto describes her practice as “a place where fragmentation resides, slowly allowing myself to listen to the quietness in which it speaks.”

item.title: Zovuyo Pendu
item.description: Zovuyo Pendu (b. 2003) explores the psychological negotiations that occur within the self. Using the body as both subject and language, she examines emotional conundrums and ongoing questions through fractured moments of despair, love, morality, resistance, reverence, and contradiction. Her practice positions the body as a site of evidence, reflection, and study, communicating experiences that can be difficult to articulate through words. Pendu’s personal faith becomes a form of translation, at times anchored in the Bible, as she navigates internal beliefs, identity, and the complexities of how faith is experienced, embodied, questioned, and represented within the world around her. Through her practice, she reflects on the relationship between inner experience and external perception, creating space for vulnerability, contemplation, and self-examination.

item.title: Keerera Nellie
item.description: Keerera Nellie is a Ugandan visual artist, photographer, and curator whose practice explores the intersections of culture, memory, materiality, and everyday life. With a background in industrial design and photography, her work is informed by an ongoing interest in how objects, images, and materials carry stories about people, places, and cultural histories.Her practice moves between photography, visual research, material exploration, and curatorial work. She is particularly interested in Ugandan cultural forms and the ways they can be re-examined, documented, and translated through contemporary visual practices. Her work often considers questions of identity, belonging, memory, and the relationship between people and the materials that surround them.Keerera’s approach is grounded in observation and curiosity, using image-making and material experimentation as ways of paying attention to overlooked narratives. Her interests extend to traditional craft, textiles, waste, and processes of making, particularly where material practices intersect with questions of cultural preservation and contemporary life.Alongside her artistic practice, Keerera works in the Ugandan art sector as a curator and cultural organiser. Her curatorial interests centre on creating spaces for artists and communities to engage with culture, history, and contemporary social questions.Through both her artistic and curatorial work, she is interested in contributing to a visual culture that is distinctly rooted in Uganda while remaining open to broader African and global conversations.

item.title: Laruni Diana Mary
item.description: Diana Mary Laruni (b.1998) also known as Mary.D is a multidisciplinary visual artist based in Kampala, Uganda; her work reveals the transformative power of natural materials, particularly maize husks. Often discarded and overlooked, maize husks hold immense creative potential, and her artistic practice explores their rebirth into new forms.Her work is deeply influenced by her personal experiences as an African woman navigating the complexities of traditional upbringing in the context of a rapidly evolving modern society. Diana’s practice integrates diverse techniques, such as stitching, which emphasizes themes of repair, mending, attachment and healing, reflecting layers of personal and collective human experiences.Her works explore contemporary visual narratives around identity, relationships, care, memory, and self-discovery which are reflected in artistic forms like sculpture, photography, digital art, fashion, and installation art.In 2022, Diana graduated with first-class honors in Industrial and Fine Art from Uganda Christian University- Mukono. Her works have been featured in group exhibitions, including By’abakazi at Umoja Art Gallery (2024), The Resilient Spirit Exhibition by Muumba Collective (2023), and Beyond Memories at Uganda Christian University (2022), Karibu exhibition by Njabala Foundation(2026) and Annual Njabala Exhibition (ANE 2026). She held her first solo exhibition, Mother of Child, at Agandy Studios (2023). Diana has also participated in the 32 Degrees East Artist Residency (2022) ,”The Resilient Spirit Workshop” by Muumba Collective (2023), Karibu Residency by Njabala Foundation (2026).

item.title: Darren Akoragye
item.description: Darren Akoragye is a multimedia artist and designer whose work centres on identity, connection, and the natural patterns that emerge from her intuitive practice over time. Working across illustration, film, printmaking, watercolor painting, digital art and design, she explores how personal and shared stories are woven together.Darren's style combines spontaneity with discipline. She uses rhythm and repetition to add depth to her work, moving between ink, watercolour, and collage on the page and moving image on screen. Each piece reflects her belief that the creative process is just as important as the final result.Based in Uganda, Darren is dedicated to supporting other artists in her community. She hopes her work inspires viewers to think about their place in the bigger picture and to feel connected to a broader story.

item.title: Namala Olivia
item.description: Namala Olivia, born in 1975, in the vibrant community of Lukuli Makindye in Kampala District, is a dedicated artist and craftsman with a passion for community development. Growing up in the family of Mr. and Mrs. Mutibwa Edward, Namala's artistic journey began early in life. She completed her Primary Leaving Examination in 1987, followed by an Ordinary Level Certificate of Education from Lubaga Girls Secondary School in 1991.With a commitment to enriching her community, Namala founded "Namala Art & Crafts for Community Development," located in Kisoga, Mukono District. Her work focuses on handcrafts, where she collaborates with local youth and women, fostering creativity and skills development. By utilizing local fibers, she not only preserves traditional craftsmanship but also empowers her community members through sustainable practices.In addition to her craftwork, Namala has recently launched a workshop that serves as a creative hub for artistic expression and collaboration in her local area. Through her initiatives, she continues to inspire and uplift those around her, making a significant impact in her community

item.title: Joseph Kojo Hoggar
item.description: Joseph Kojo Hoggar (b. 1999, Accra, Ghana) is a Ghanaian multidisciplinary artist based in Amherst, Massachusetts, whose practice engages painting, installation, and material-based inquiry. He is currently pursuing an MFA in Studio Art at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, following a BFA in Painting from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Kumasi in 2022. His practice considers the relationship between materiality, cultural representation, and identity.Hoggar’s material inquiry began with African wax print, which he incorporated into his paintings as both a physical and cultural element. His practice is now developing through the inclusion of denim and tartan alongside African wax print, creating relationships between materials with distinct cultural associations and embedded histories of production, circulation, and cultural meaning. Through painting, fragmentation, collage, stitching, and sewing, he examines how cultural identities are constructed, negotiated, and continually reconfigured through contact and exchange, while questioning ideas of authenticity. Hoggar’s movement from Ghana to the United States has further informed his engagement with cultural hybridity and the shifting conditions of identity.His practice approaches materials and bodies as terrains where histories, cultural associations, and meanings intersect, overlap, and transform. His ideas are informed by postcolonial theory, particularly its attention to the formation of identity, cultural hybridity, and the ongoing effects of colonial histories on cultural representation. Hoggar has exhibited internationally in Paris, London, New York, Accra, and Amherst. He is a recipient of the Kuenyehia Prize for Contemporary Art.

item.title: Putin Ofori Bempong
item.description: I am a Ghanaian contemporary artist based in Accra. My practice explores memory, Akan folklore, the environment, and African futures through painting and mixed media. I draw from stories of Ananse to explore intelligence, survival, change, and the ways knowledge is passed from one generation to another. I work with acrylic and industrial paints, resin, found materials, organic matter, photographs, and materials connected to mining and place. I see these materials as carriers of memory, allowing me to connect personal, cultural, and environmental histories with contemporary life.I hold a Bachelor of Fine Art in Painting and Sculpture from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Kumasi. My work has been exhibited at Gallery 1957, Nubuke Foundation, KNUST Museum, blaxTARLINES Project Space, TAIR Gallery, Origin Gallery, and Accra Art District. In 2026, I participated in the OUT Residency in Lagos, Nigeria, where I developed new research around memory, architecture, materiality, folklore, and African futures.

item.title: Paulcy Odama
item.description: Odama Paulcy (1994, Cross River, Nigeria) is a self-taught artist from Abuja, whose creative journey has been as diverse as her life experiences. She trained as a Medical Doctor, with a degree from the Zaporozhye State Medical University, Ukraine, and after five years of practice, she eventually found her way back to her true passion “Art”. Her transformation from a doctor to an artist reflects the power of self-discovery and the healing potential of creative expression.For the past four years, Odama has been fervently honing her skills in painting, developing a unique artistic voice that is both introspective and thought-provoking. Working from her home studio, she began her journey in 2020 with poster colour watercolor, gradually moving into oil and acrylic. Today, her practice has expanded into mixed media, where she explores earth pigment, charcoal, thread, wool, semiprecious stones, and acrylic paint. She often uses earth pigment to reflect impermanence, while her decision to paint the human aura rather than skin speaks to her deeper interest in the unseen dimensions of existence.Her art invites viewers to engage with her inner world, to contemplate the complexities of being, and to find meaning in the intricate dance of choices and fate. She has participated in several group exhibitions, including Masquerades (Cavic Hub, 2023), Echoes (Society of Nigerian Artists, Orisun Gallery, 2023), For Her Eyes Only (Leora Consult, 2024), Life and Times (Orisun Gallery, 2024), NBA Anniversary Exhibition (Windsor Gallery, 2024), Survive and Thrive (Windsor Gallery, 2024), Art and Tech Festival (Cavic Hub, 2024), Mindscape (Vom Network, 2024), Urban Kraft (2024), Subtly Stentorian (Nomadic Gallery, 2024), and UN Artvocacy (Windsor Gallery, 2024), Remember when (Nomadic Gallery 2025), Vantage point “2025” Astraeacurate, Groundwork (Nomadic gallery) 2026, Weight of traces (Soto Gallery, 2026).

item.title: Tochukwu Orazulike
item.description: Born in Aba, Abia State, Nigeria, in 1996, Tochukwu Orazulike is an artist originally from Anambra State and currently based in Lagos. His practice moves between mixed-media painting and experimental forms made from repurposed materials. He explores the relationship between humans and their surroundings, particularly how we interact with the world around us and how the affect us in return. Working with acrylic, spray paint, and oil on fabric, he allows material processes and unpredictable forms to play an active role in shaping his work.A graduate of the Institute of Management and Technology (IMT), Enugu, Orazulike has exhibited both locally and internationally. Recent highlights include his debut solo exhibition, The Order of Decay at Alliance Française de Lagos (2024), participation in the 1952 Africa Art Residency (2023), and selection as a finalist at the Absa L'Atelier Art & Lifestyle Fair, Johannesburg (2025). He currently lives and works in Lagos, Nigeria.

item.title: Wisdom Uche
item.description: Wisdom Uche (born 1993) is a Nigerian painter known for his Neo-Expressionist Figurative paintings. His work is psychologically playful, characterized by bold vibrant colours, stylized faces, and expressive lines that communicate emotion and explore the complexities of the human experience. He studied at the School of Art, Yaba College of Technology, Lagos State.Wisdom Uche contrasts notions of family with the encroaching reality of solitude that symptomises our contemporaneity. Combining figurative style with neoexpressionism, and featuring the postured body with a palette of whimsical emoticons for a face, the works leave us to contemplate and infer the implied dispositions and relationships of the portrayed figures.

item.title: Snelihle A. Maphumulo
item.description: Snelihle Maphumulo was born and raised in Durban, South Africa. She works with found material, particularly sheep hide. Her works explore the fruitful tensions of Zulu tradition and Christian faith. Through an intuitive engagement with material and form, Maphumulo draws on both personal and collective memory, allowing her work to unfold as a layered dialogue between tradition, belief and belonging. Maphumulo was awarded the Sasol New Signatures prize in both 2024 and 2025, recognizing her as one of South Africa’s most promising emerging artists. In 2024, she completed her Honours in Fine Art at Rhodes University, further developing her practice in sculpture, installation, and material exploration.Maphumulo’s practice explores the space where Christian faith and Zulu tradition meet; in harmony, tension, and sometimes within the uncertainty of being in-between. She works with materials that carry symbolic, cultural and tactile meaning, including cow hide, sheep hide and found objects. Rather than treating these materials as passive surfaces, she allows them to participate in the making. Their textures and histories guide her gestures, making touch a quiet form of testimony

item.title: Martine Margoles
item.description: Martine Margoles graduated from Michaelis (UCT) in 1986. After two solo exhibitions at Goodman Gallery, she moved to New York for seven years, where she manufactured and sold her Amos & Sophie T-shirts, worked as a fashion designer and made dresses for Patricia Field. On returning to Johannesburg, she established a commercial metalworking studio, working with steel on a large scale. In 2004, she won a tender to make gates for the judge’s chamber at Constitution Hill, where she also held a solo sculpture exhibition. Margoles has exhibited in South Africa and internationally, including at Goodman Gallery, Alliance Française, Constitution Hill, Lizamore Gallery and Glen Carlou Gallery. Her work has also been presented at Investec Cape Town Art Fair, with the Heidi Erdmann Gallery. Martine Margoles’ creative process began long before digital technology. As a young artist, she spent hours in libraries photocopying images from books, cutting them apart and collaging them together until they resembled the pictures that already existed in her imagination. As technology evolved, so did her process. Library books became a camera, then Google, Pinterest and today, ChatGPT.

item.title: Eunice Pais
item.description: Eunice Pais is a Portuguese interdisciplinary artist whose practice spans photography, and video installations. Her work explores visibility and invisibility, memory, ecology, identity and colonial histories, examining the relationship between bodies, landscapes and human–nature connections. Working across documentary and speculative forms, Pais draws on the intertwined histories of Portugal to investigate belonging, oral tradition, resistance and ecological care.In 2026, she presented her first institutional solo exhibition, Pele do Mar, at Galeria Municipal do Porto, Portugal. Her work has been presented internationally, including at Framer Framed (Amsterdam), Open Eye Gallery (Liverpool) and State of Fashion Biennale (Arnhem). She is part of the FUTURES Photography platform.

item.title: Amina Yehia
item.description: Born in Cairo, Egypt, Amina Yahia’s work examines systems of control within contemporary Egyptian society, tracing how they shape human interaction, belief, behavior, and dream. She’s particularly attentive to class structures and their subtle yet pervasive influence on the ways individuals internalize hierarchy. Merging folkloric residues with systemic and sociopolitical frameworks, Yahia explores socially conditioned behavior and the ritualistic–almost spiritual–dimension that emerges through repetition. Much of her practice is rooted in post- and neocolonial Egypt, where power structures continue to inform both collective consciousness and intimate self-perception.The female identity remains central to her work. She often positions my figures vis-à-vis mechanisms of control and surveillance, staging them within psychological and societal frameworks. Many of these figures–frequently life-sized–carry an undercurrent of satire, subtly destabilizing the very systems they inhabit. Her narratives persistently seek to dissect the uncanny, banal, intimate, violent, and sensual of the body. Through this inquiry, she traces the lingering imprints of cultural embeddedness as they manifest in gesture, movement, and bodily function, revealing the body as both site of inscription and potential resistance.Amina Yahia is currently pursuing her MFA in Art and Media at New York University. She held her first solo exhibition last November at Hunna Art Gallery in Kuwait, and has shown her work with Hunna Art at 1-54 Marrakech, 2025; Hayaty Diaries, London, 2025; Tahrir Cultural Center AUC, Cairo, 2023; New York University Abu Dhabi, Abu Dhabi, 2022; Firetti Contemporary, Alserkal Avenue, Dubai, 2022; 421, Abu Dhabi, 2021; Maisan15, Dubai, 2021, among others.

item.title: Ala Alhourani
item.description: Dr Ala Rabiba Alhourani is a Palestinian visual artist, filmmaker, and painter based in Cape Town. He held a solo exhibition, For Some but not for Others, in 2024 at Breakroom in Cape Town. In 2025 and 2026, he participated in the group exhibition Mis Fit in Cape Town and his work was included in the AVA members' group exhibition in 2026. He is an anthropologist and a senior lecturer in the Department for the Study of Religions at the University of Cape Town. His research focuses on the anthropology of religion, foregrounding aesthetic experiences of religion as embodied ethics, knowledge, power, and traditions.

item.title: Hayfa Elgwaiz
item.description: Hayfa Algwaiz (b. 1991) is a painter and architect based in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Her work has been presented internationally, including a group exhibition at Ithra Museum (Dhahran, KSA); Taymour Grahne Projects (Dubai, UAE); Art Basel Paris 2025 with Athr Gallery; Dot Ateliers (Accra, Ghana); Hatch Gallery (Paris, FR); Thaer Select (Paris, Abu Dhabi, and Dubai); N.E.S.T Art Space (AlUla, KSA); Bait Shouaib (Jeddah, KSA); Al Riwaq Art Space (Manama, Bahrain); and Misk Art Institute (Riyadh, KSA), as well as exhibitions supported by the Saudi Ministry of Culture. She also participated in the Saudi Pavilion at Expo 2025 in Osaka, Japan.Algwaiz has been selected for artist residencies at POUSH (Paris, FR), Bait Shouaib with Athr Foundation (Jeddah, KSA), Dot Ateliers (Accra, Ghana), Fikar Institute (Failaka Island, Kuwait), and Armature (Cambridge, UK). Her work has been supported through awards and programs including the Misk Art Grant (2023) and the 8th edition of Young Saudi Artists (Athr Foundation).In 2025, she published an essay titled "Arriving at a Place You Never Left" in Connections as Method: Relational Pedagogies and Participatory Spatial Practice, the second official catalogue of the National Pavilion of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia at the Venice Biennale Architettura, published by Kaph.

item.title: Chiedu Okonta
item.description: Chiedu Okonta (b.1979) is a Nigerian-British artist based in London. As an award-winning artist and the recipient of the prestigious Sir Frank Bowling Scholarship for MA Painting at the Royal College of Art, his artistic journey integrates both self-taught foundations and the depth of formal education.Okonta views his work as part of a contemporary school of thought focused on archiving, reporting, agitating, and questioning through deliberate objective positioning. His creations reflect a counter-hegemonic worldview, inviting diverse audiences to reflect on their place within the tapestry of humanity’s shared experience.Chiedu was born into a traditional middle-class Nigerian family and initially trained as a civil engineer, earning his MSc from the University of East London. Today, he channels technical prowess into a deeply empathetic artistic practice, exploring the dynamics of community, resilience, and the exploitation of natural resources, particularly in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria, which he hails from.The semiotic lexicon of his works binds together timelines that form a backdrop against which Okonta’s creations resonate with urgency, mirroring a collective longing for equity. They evoke hauntological themes - echoes of the lingering presence of future expectations.Having exhibited internationally and been featured in both domestic and international magazines, he is aware of the fleeting nature of contemporary attention and incorporates this awareness into his work, which resists a linear understanding of time. His works are designed to captivate viewers and encourage prolonged contemplation.

item.title: Mona Taha
item.description: Mona Taha's practice moves fluidly between drawing and painting, and across different media such as charcoal, ink, gouache, watercolor, and collage, among others. Her work is both figurative and atmospheric, balancing a distinctive sensuality with a raw, unguarded honesty.Process and material are central to her work. She often works intuitively, letting fluid mediums spread, stain, and settle unpredictably while building compositions through layering, interruption, and response. Collage, often composed of offcuts and remnants from earlier works, plays a central role in her recent practice. It introduces fragments that simultaneously conceal and disclose, suggesting incompletion and rupture as generative forces.Rooted in autobiography, her work explores identity, femininity, self-discovery, and transformation. For Taha, making art is a therapeutic process, allowing space for reflection, confrontation, and growth.While earlier works often centered on portraiture and the body as sites of inquiry, her recent paintings expand this exploration outward. Figures appear embedded within their environments, dissolving into and emerging from landscapes that act not as backdrop but as presence and structure.Taha's work continues to evolve as an intimate yet expansive exploration of selfhood. It opens toward broader ideas of connection, resilience, and renewal. Through this, she encourages deeper self-awareness and a reclamation of identity, especially for women navigating the tension between societal expectations and inner truth.She has shown her work in Surfaces (Afriart Gallery, 2019), Where the Wild Things are (Afriart Gallery, 2022), Echo (Jenkins Johnson Projects NYC, 2022), Shapes of Water (Afriart Gallery, 2023), and Eastern Voices: Contemporary Art from East Africa (Addis Fine Art, London, 2023). Besides, she has participated in Art Basel Miami Beach, Liste Art Fair Basel, Art Paris, 1-54 Contemporary African Art Fair New York and London, Art X Lagos, Abu Dhabi Art, and FNB Joburg.

item.title: Mahir Siraj
item.description: Mahir Siraj (born in 1992) is an Eritrean-born emerging artist based in Toronto. With a foundation in self-taught painting, Mahir has a BFA in Drawing and Painting from OCAD University. Mahir draws visual and historical references from his exposure to living in countries such as Ethiopia, Eritrea, Sudan (as a refugee), and Canada. With an emphasis on painting, his artistic practice utilizes a visual play of symbols and metaphors to explore the intricate connections between memory and the construction of meaning. Mahir is currently based in Toronto, Canada, where he continues to create breathtaking surrealist pieces that speak to his ancestry and the human condition.

item.title: Inioluwa Aboluwarin
item.description: Ini Oluwa (b. 1994, Ile-Ife, Nigeria) is a self-taught Nigerian visual artist based between Ile-Ife and Lagos. His practice examines solitude, intimacy, individuality, and the human condition through expressive portraiture rooted in Yoruba cultural and philosophical traditions. Working primarily in ink, acrylic, and charcoal on paper and canvas, his work explores the formative experiences that shape individual lives, revealing the profound significance of seemingly ordinary moments.His practice draws inspiration from the classical artistic tradition, the philosophy of Ayn Rand, and the intellectual traditions of Yoruba Ìṣẹ̀ṣe. A full-time artist since 2016, Ini Oluwa has exhibited internationally, including at Augusta Savage Gallery in the United States in 2020 and with Eno Gallery in London in 2022. His debut solo exhibition, Fountainhead, was presented in Lagos in 2023. His works are held in private collections across more than 20 countries. In 2026, he initiated The Atlas Project, an ongoing collaborative portraiture and storytelling project celebrating human resilience through portraits and personal accounts of adversity, perseverance, and transformation.

item.title: Luncedo Phillip
item.description: Luncedo Phillip is a multidisciplinary artist born and raised in South Africa, Gqeberha in the Eastern Cape, whose creative practice spans Visual Art, Music and Performance. Phillip has recently completed a BA Visual Art Degree at the University of Johannesburg where he majored in Painting. During the course of his third year Phillip has obtained distinctions in History of Art, Drawing and Studio Practice showing continuous dedication, curiosity and eagerness to learn in his growing artistic journey. The artist's work is a testament of ongoing healing and serves as a method of self discovery, learning and unlearning about some of the historical complications that still linger within us today, in order to find his position not only in the arts but across all boarders and the world at

item.title: Nomvuyo Maseko
item.description: Nomvuyo Maseko (b. 2001) is a visual artist based in Johannesburg. Raised between Vryheid and Ulundi, her practice examines early adulthood through the psychological and social condition of early exceptionalism, with a particular interest in Black giftedness. Working primarily in oil paint and ceramics, she creates figurative works that consider what happens when identities formed around exceptional ability, potential, and expectation encounter the uncertainties of adulthood.Her work explores the negotiation between who one was expected to become and who one is becoming, alongside the pressures, contradictions, and vulnerabilities that accompany exceptionalism. Light and the sun recur throughout her work as metaphors for giftedness, visibility, and the persistent demand to remain luminous, while also questioning what it means to exist beyond the conditions that made one exceptional.

item.title: Olebogeng Esemang
item.description: Olebogeng Esemang (b. 2001) is a Soweto-born multidisciplinary artist who has completed their Bachelor of Fine Arts from the University of the Witwatersrand. Their practice is an outpouring of self; honest, intuitive, and grounded in lived experience. Working experimentally across painting, sculpture, and installation, Esemang’s work draws deeply from personal and familial histories, engaging memory not as something fixed, but as something fluid, constantly moving, shifting, and living. Through their explorations of form and texture, they seek to give memory shape and presence, building a living archive that holds what has been as well as what continues to unfold.They often approach their practice as a process of excavation, layering materials and symbols to reveal fragments of past and present. Within this interplay, their work becomes a site where personal and collective memory converge, inviting viewers to engage with their own emotional landscapes and histories. Rather than providing fixed answers, their work remains open-ended of a quiet invitation toward reflection, reinterpretation, and encounter. Their ongoing dialogue with interiority, nostalgia, and subconscious narratives manifests as visual explorations of selfhood through poetic meditations on belonging, time, and transformation.

item.title: Kristina Nichol
item.description: Kristina Nichol (b. in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe 1997, and mostly growing up in Pretoria, South Africa) is a multidisciplinary textile artist. Focusing on ideas that surround identity and what ‘home’ really means is a reoccurrence in their work. Her childhood was mostly spent being alone.Experiencing depression, anxiety and mania further created a disconnect from self and others. She often would spend time with her grandmother and mother. With her fondest memories being in the garden with her grandmother and watching her mom paint and sew. The true artist’s and creators in her eyes and world.Pursuing her desires to create again in her late 20’s felt like a return ‘home’ in many ways for Kristina. Her art practice serves as a love letter and a form of remembering and connection to her late mother, who passed away when Kristina was 21. She also continues to pursue a BA in Creative Writing through UNISA. Finding ways to connect the threads of the stories she wishes to tell and explore.

item.title: Sagwadi Mohlabi
item.description: Sagwadi Mohlabi (b. 2002) is a Limpopo born South African self-taught fibre artist working through punch needling, tufting, and fibre-based photography construction, drawing on the woven Xitsonga traditions of the women who raised her in Limpopo. Her practice moves between the choreographies of everyday life : labour, self-presentation , gathering and the private language of cloth passed down through her grandmother's woven skirts, treating material as a carrier of movement, memory, and self-identity.Her work sits at the intersection of desire and acquisition within black womanhood, returning continously to her maternal archive. In 2025, she undertook an international residency with Rele Gallery in Lagos, Nigeria, was named a 2026 finalist for the Blessing Ngobeni Art Prize award and presented her first showing at RMB Latitudes Art Fair 2026.

item.title: Lesego Forbes
item.description: Lesego Forbes (b. 2005) is a South African artist living and working in Johannesburg. Working with charcoal as his main medium, he explores moments of negotiation and tension through the body and its engagement with material. His practice is concerned with paying careful attention to the ways in which material demands of the body through processes of drawing, writing and assemblage. His conceptual installational tableaux work grapples with practical ideas of building, the processes concerned with manually making something. By engaging with the objects and understanding how they behave naturally and how he can manipulate them, Forbes constructs moments he calls pockets of feeling where the material of the objects carries out an emotion, reaching outside of itself. His materials span across a range of material such as; concrete, cling wrap, gypsum board, fiberglass, newsprint, wood, etc. Forbes’ instances are rooted in the seen and the sensed, concerned with possessing the audience in a moment of questioning, presenting them into a sort of limbo. He understands surfaces and found materials as bodily gestures; as permeable, as hard or soft, as flexible, as sensitive, as skin. He utilises his writing in his practice as a way of thinking through the work as well as a tool for conceptualising. Forbes has participated in a few group shows in Johannesburg over the years, namely; to, fail to (2026), shifting figures (2025) as part of an initiative by the GALA Queer Archive. He is currently completing his undergraduate studies at the University of the Witwatersrand, acquiring a Bachelor of Arts in Fine Arts.

item.title: Cathy Xiao
item.description: Cathy Xiao is a Johannesburg-based photographer working across landscape and urban documentary photography. Her practice is grounded in spatial observation and informed by a background in science, shaping a meticulous and restrained approach to image-making. Working without intervention, she allows images to emerge through time and proximity rather than direction or staging. She holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Astronomy and Astrophysics as well as a Bachelor of Science Honours in Physics from the University of the Witwatersrand. Her work has been exhibited locally and internationally, and featured in both South African and international publications, alongside independent print projects.

item.title: Kirsty Tinkler
item.description: Kirsty Tinkler (b. 1971, Australia) holds a BA in Sculpture from the National Art School (1995–1999) and an MA in Sculpture from the Royal College of Art (2007–2009). After relocating to Cape Town in 2024, she completed the Sessions Studio Programme led by Dominique Edwards in 2025. Tinkler’s practice spans wall-based reliefs, objects, and large-scale, site-responsive installations presented internationally. Her work negotiates the line between formal material, visceral inquiry and contextual research. Engaging with historicism and speculative thought, she interrogates Western classical traditions, questioning linear narratives and fixed interpretations. Her first solo exhibition, Hoist, was presented at the University of Suffolk Waterfront Gallery (2011). Subsequent solo projects have included collaborations with London’s Vitrine Gallery, WW Gallery (Patio Projects), Quare Offsite Projects, and Shift Gallery. In 2024, she presented Vessel, her most ambitious solo exhibition to date, supported by Dalston Pier, London. Her most recent solo exhibition, Scared Debris, taking place at AVA Gallery in 2026, marks her first in South Africa.

item.title: Damon Botha & Lesego Forbes (collaborative)
item.description: Damon Botha (b. 2003) is a painter who thinks alongside the makeshift structures of his life in Krugersdorp and the processes of building that his late father used to shape the world around him. Lesego Forbes (b. 2005) is a South African artist living and working in Johannesburg. Working with charcoal as his main medium, he explores moments of negotiation and tension through the body and its engagement with material. His practice is concerned with paying careful attention to the ways in which material demands of the body through processes of drawing, writing and assemblage. His conceptual installational tableaux work grapples with practical ideas of building, the processes concerned with manually making something. By engaging with the objects and understanding how they behave naturally and how he can manipulate them, Forbes constructs moments he calls pockets of feeling where the material of the objects carries out an emotion, reaching outside of itself.

item.title: Brigitta Stone-Johnson
item.description: Dr Brigitta Stone-Johnson (Brigs) is an artist, architect, and researcher who lives in Johannesburg, South Africa. She has lectured at the Wits School of Architecture (SoAP) since 2016. Her work considers the post-mining city as a material ecology through its material markers: earth, air, water, and geology. She creates art and writes about a living material that represents a more-than-human world and bridges humans to the deep past and the deep future. She is concerned with the impacts of climate change on cities as living, more-than-human ecosystems. Alongside the human-geological relationships that take place in cities at all scales. My work is grounded in artistic and design practices as tools for counter-narrating extraction, colonialism, and the impacts of the Anthropocene.

item.title: Andrew Murray
item.description: Andrew Murray is a South African artist based in Johannesburg. Trained at the Johannesburg Art Foundation under Sophia Ainsley and at the Lorenzo de’ Medici School of Art in Florence, he has sustained a parallel artistic practice across four decades whilst creating a major South African construction company. His work has moved through classical figuration, portraiture and still life, into mixed-media works on paper, found-object sculpture and stop-motion animation, and most recently, large-format abstract painting in acrylic. His paintings are held in private collections in South Africa and internationally, and he has exhibited at the Everard Read Gallery (Johannesburg) on multiple occasions, as well as in Florence, Barcelona and Buenos Aires. Now retired from construction, he is returning to an active studio practice.

item.title: Reshma Chhiba
item.description: Reshma Chhiba (b. 1983, Springs, South Africa) is a visual artist and dancer based in Johannesburg, South Africa. Her multidisciplinary practice explores the intersection of contemporary visual art and classical Indian dance, drawing on feminist strategies, Hindu mythology and folk tales to challenge patriarchal expectations and interrogate race, gender, ethnicity and sexuality in post- apartheid South Africa. Working across analogue photography, soft sculpture, painting and performance, storytelling remains central to her practice. Chhiba holds a BAFA (2005) and MAFA (2013) from the University of the Witwatersrand, and a diploma in Bharatanatyam (2002) from the Institute of Indian Art and Culture. She is a lecturer in Fine Arts and a PhD candidate in African Literature at Wits University. She co-founded Sarvavidya Natyaalaya (2010), a Johannesburg-based Bharatanatyam collective, and co-edited The Yoni Book (2019) with Nontobeko Ntombela. Her co-created dance production Bhumi | Earth (2023) received the 2024 HSS Award for Best Public Performance.

item.title: Chidirim Nwaubani
item.description: Chidirim Nwaubani is the founder of LOOTY, a radical artivist collective that uses innovative art and technology to reclaim stolen artworks, revive cultural heritage and transform narratives about cultural ownership. In 2023, LOOTY orchestrated the world’s first digital heist, using LiDAR technology to 3D scan the Rosetta Stone at the British Museum and repatriate it to Egypt. LOOTY’s installations are not mere exhibits; they are portals where visitors become co-creators, confronting the stories behind looted treasures and restoring the creative spirit at their core. Nwaubani was the Tomorrows/Today Prize Winner at the Cape Town Art Fair 2026 and has previously exhibited at the Venice Biennale and London Design Biennale.

item.title: Delali Cofie
item.description: Delali Cofie is a Ghanaian-Nigerian photographer and visual artist currently living in Toronto, Canada. Through storytelling, he engages in multiple genres of photography such as fine art, documentary, and fashion. His personal work presents subtle beauty whilst exploring themes of self-formation and the process of becoming. Frequently creating work between his native city Accra and current city Toronto, his work tells a tale of two cities, linked by a diasporic thread. Recently, his practice has expanded to explore materiality,focusing on how materials carry histories and narratives that can be reimaginedin physical form. Using textiles and other forms, he engages with theirconnection to the body and identity to create layered works that reflectgrowth, selfhood, and the passage of time. Recent exhibitions include …The Candle Whispered Them Here,C2 Art Program, CIBC Square (2025), The Great Unseen, McMaster Museum of Art,Hamilton (2025), Tree of Life, PhotoVogue Festival, Italy (2025) and REVIVE,DesignTO Festival, Toronto (2025), where he was the recipient of the emergingartist/designer award; It comes to me in waves, Patel Brown Gallery (2024). In 2022 his work was featured in legendary Ghanaian photographer James Barnor’s exhibition catalogue at the Arles Photography Festival. He is a 2024 graduate of OCAD University, where he was the recipient of multiple program awards and the OCAD U Medal for Photography.

item.title: Chimmuanya Onuzulike
item.description: Chimmuanya Onuzulike (b. 2008) is an emerging Nigerian artist from Achi, Enugu State, and the second son of Professor Ozioma Onuzulike, a distinguished Nigerian ceramic artist and Professor of Ceramic Art. He recently completed his secondary school education. Raised in an active ceramics studio, Chimmuanya encountered clay and ceramic production processes from an early age, developing a practical understanding of materials and techniques that continues to inform his artistic practice.In 2026, his painting won a prize in the National Gallery of Art (NGA), Enugu, Children’s Day Art Competition. He presented his first solo exhibition, Becoming, 2015–2026, in 2026, marking a significant milestone in his artistic development. His works have also featured in exhibitions in Nsukka and Lagos. They are represented in public and private collections, including those of the National Gallery of Art, Enugu, and the Institute of African Studies Museum, University of Nigeria, Nsukka.Through his evolving practice, Chimmuanya continues to explore the expressive and conceptual possibilities of ceramics, alongside drawing and painting, as he develops his distinctive artistic voice.

item.title: Ikechukwu Nduka
item.description: Ikechukwu Nduka (b. 1997) is a Nigerian visual artist whose practice draws from Igbo heritage and cultural traditions. He received a Bachelor’s degree in Fine and Applied Arts from the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, where he is currently pursuing an MFA. Working primarily with net and striped belts, Nduka explores the alternative functions and possibilities of everyday materials to create vibrant sculptural forms.His practice engages themes of Igbo culture, communication, memory, apprenticeship, and traditional titles as markers of social progress and achievement. Recent presentations include the Biennale Internationale de Sculpture in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso (2025), and a residency at Guest Artists Space (G.A.S.), Lagos (2026). He has presented a solo exhibition in Lagos with Wunika Mukan Gallery and participated in group exhibitions with galleries and art platforms in Nigeria, the United States, and France, as well as art fairs in Portugal, Algeria, and the United States.Nduka’s works are held in institutional and private collections in Nigeria and internationally. He was a recipient of the Art Report Africa and DicaArts Prize (2025). He lives and works in Nsukka, Nigeria.

item.title: Louis Ifeanyi Igwegbe
item.description: Louis Ifeanyi Igwegbe (b. 1998, Umulewe, Imo State, Nigeria) is an emerging contemporary artist whose practice spans wood carving and painting. He was introduced to art at an early age through his father, an artist, and began creating biblical murals for local Catholic parishes as a teenager. Igwegbe studied Fine and Applied Arts at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, graduating with second class upper division as Best Graduating Student and Best Sculptor in 2022, alongside receiving several academic awards.Working primarily through carving and painting, Igwegbe explores the unconscious mind. His experimental “paintaglio” process combines painting with wood carving and burning, transforming surfaces into emotional topographies.Igwegbe has participated in group exhibitions including Ntachl Obi, Institute of African Studies Museum, University of Nigeria, Nsukka (2024); Art is Everywhere, Bona Art Gallery, Enugu (2024); LIMCAF, Enugu (2024, 2025, 2026); and Ihe Ncheta, Dominican University, Illinois, Chicago, USA (2025). He completed industrial training in wood carving at Tuff Studio, Enugu (2020), interned at the El Anatsui Studio, Nsukka (2025), where he gained experience in both small- and large-scale production and professional studio practice. In 2026, He lives and works in Nsukka, Nigeria.

item.title: Faustina Abah
item.description: Faustina Abah (b. 2001, Nsukka, Nigeria) is a contemporary artist whose practice transforms discarded jute bags gathered from local markets into sculptural forms. Drawing from her early observations of her mother and other traders using, repairing, and reusing jute bags, Abah approaches jute as a material that carries histories of labour, memory, and lived experience.Through stitching, layering, binding, and embroidery techniques she developed while studying Fashion at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, Abah repairs and transforms the material while preserving traces of its previous use. Her forms emerge from her subconscious and from the possibilities suggested by the material itself, allowing the history embedded within each jute bag to inform its transformation into new forms.Faustina has participated in exhibitions such as Uzo Ije (2023) and +234 Artfair (2026) and is a past resident artsit of Ulo Nka Artspace.

item.title: Sunday Ernest Nnamal
item.description: Sunday Ernest (b. 1977, Nsukka, Nigeria) is a sculptor and sculpture technician in the Department of Fine and Applied Arts at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka. His practice engages with the lingering effects of post colonial African challenges and consumerism while maintaining a firm footprint on environmental sustainability. Working extensively with discarded materials, particularly waste nylon wrappers, Ernest ties, binds, and reconfigures them into vibrant relief sculptural forms.Through his transformation of everyday waste, Ernest reflects on the superficial solutions often applied to deep-rooted environmental and social problems while exploring the possibilities of discarded materials as objects of aesthetics.Ernest was awarded the Best in Sculpture Prize at the Life in My City Art Festival (LIMCAF) in 2012. In 2019, he participated in the Flag Art Exhibition, which opened the Cheongju Craft Biennale in South Korea. His recent exhibitions include his debut solo exhibition, Folding and Tying Narrative, Institute of African Studies, University of Nigeria, Nsukka (2024); +234 Art Fair, Lagos (2025, 2026); and Beautiful Game, Mitochondria Gallery, Houston, Texas (2026). He lives and works in Nsukka, Nigeria.

item.title: Emmanuel Chinenye Ifoegbuike
item.description: Emmanuel Chinenye Ifoegbuike is a Nigerian visual artist, art writer, and poet. He holds a Bachelor of Arts (BA) and a Master of Fine Arts (MFA) from the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, where he is currently pursuing a PhD in Art History.Ifoegbuike’s practice explores the relationship between circles and cycles as recurring visual elements and metaphors through which he reflects on social, political, cultural, and economic realities. Working primarily with fabric, thread, and flexible wire, he constructs circular and spiral forms that are bound into relief sculptural compositions.Ifoegbuike has participated in exhibitions in Nigeria and has undertaken a residency at Soto Gallery, Ikoyi, Lagos (2023). Recent exhibitions include +234 Art Fair, Lagos (2026); New Directions, Kó Art Space, Lagos (2024); Uplifting Spirit, Soto Gallery, Lagos (2024); Introspection, Soto Gallery, Ikoyi, Lagos (2023); and Songs for the Weaver Bird, a group exhibition held in honour of Christopher Okigbo, Lagos (2022). Earlier, he participated in Anya Fulu Ugo, a group exhibition honouring Obiora Udechukwu and El Anatsui at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (2015).He lives and works in Nsukka, Nigeria.

item.title: Igbobinna Eze
item.description: Igbobinna Eze (b. 2000, Nsukka, Nigeria) is a Nigerian contemporary artist and graduate of Fine and Applied Arts from the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, where he majored in Painting. His practice draws from childhood experiences of local culture, religion, spirituality, and tradition, with particular reference to Igbo visual traditions.Influenced by Uli, Nsibidi, and the legacy of the Nsukka Art School, Eze develops vibrant compositions that explore spirituality, cultural memory, and the divine nature of the feminine.Eze has participated in group exhibitions including Dreams Alive (2019), LIMCAF (2019), Shadows of Solitude (2021), Uzo-Ije (2023), Nwa Ala (2023), Vessels (2024), Things Fall Apart Festival (2025), and Connecting Africa and Japan through Art (2025). He was awarded the Gerald Chukwuma Prize for a Burgeoning Creative Painter in 2023. He lives and works in Nigeria.

item.title: August Tondo
item.description: August Tondo (b. 1994) is a Nigerian sculptor and multidisciplinary artist from Benue State, Nigeria. He holds an NCE in Fine and Applied Arts and a Bachelor’s degree in Fine and Applied Arts from the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, where he graduated in 2023. His practice encompasses sculpture, painting, drawing, wood carving, and monumental works, with a particular interest in woven sculpture using raffia and sweet palm.Recent group exhibitions include LIMCAF 2025, Enugu (2025), where he presented Uncovering and My Cave, A Gift; and +234 Art Fair (2025), presented by Soto Gallery in partnership with Ecobank and AFC, where his sculpture Leaking Treasure (2024) was exhibited. Earlier exhibitions include Nwa Ala at the Obiora Udechukwu Gallery, University of Nigeria, Nsukka (2023), subsequently presented at De La Roke Arts Gallery (2023); Uzo-Ije at the Centre for Memories, Enugu (2023); and Nwa Ala at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (2023). His earlier exhibition history includes Shadows of Solitude at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (2020) and The Mirror, his final-year exhibition at the College of Education, Katsina-Ala.Tondo lives and works in Benue State, Nigeria.

item.title: Oluchi Anaghoba
item.description: Oluchi Anaghoba (b. 2001, Nigeria) is a Nigerian visual artist whose painting and mixed media practice explores memory, survival, landscape and community. Her work looks closely at the people, histories and environments that shape our sense of identity and belonging. Through layering, photographic collage and screenprinting, she draws from personal memories, archival materials and lived environments to examine how the past continues to shape the way we see and experience the present.Since earning her Bachelor’s degree in Fine and Applied Arts from Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka, in 2021, she has participated in several group exhibitions, including The Weight of Traces (2026, Soto Gallery, Lagos), Digital Canvas (2025–2026, Arkhive by Creath, Lagos), Design Week Lagos (2025, Nahous Lagos), Identity in Reflection (2025, Creath Lab, Lagos), Undiscovered 2.0 (2024, Thought Pyramid Art Centre, Abuja), and The Heartscape Exhibition (2024, Yenwa Gallery, Lagos). She is a fellow of the Imọra Art Intensive at G.A.S. Foundation (2025) and an alumna of the Nchedo Artist Residency (2026).With a growing interest in incorporating wood into her practice, she participated in the Roots and Resilience Sustainable Carpentry Workshop and Residency (2025) in Lagos. She was also part of the African Female Artist Mentorship Program (AFAMP) Residency (2024) in Lagos. Anaghoba currently lives and works in Lagos.

item.title: Warren Maroon
item.description: Warren Maroon (b. 1985) is a Cape Town-based sculptor whose work is deeply rooted in his personal history. Growing up in Mitchell’s Plain on the Cape Flats, an area associated with significant social challenges, Maroon turned to art as a means of escape and a tool for expression. He graduated from Ruth Prowse with a Diploma in Fine Art in 2011, finding his distinct voice as a sculptor in 2018.Inspired by an Arte Povera aesthetic, Maroon works primarily with found objects, rearranging their context to tell powerful stories. His practice serves as a poignant commentary on his lived experience—a culmination of events he has faced as a person of colour in Cape Town. Through his sculptural artworks, Maroon interrogates the unequal disposition so many experience as ‘normal life’, offering a narrative that is both deeply personal and widely resonant.
